topics.name: Triaging and passing on fuzzed issues
topics.summary:
- 讨论认为应区分通过 fuzzing/自动化扫描发现的问题与在真实生态代码中遇到的问题，因为许多 fuzzed issues 未经过 triage；这类问题仍可能存在 soundness 或其他严重影响，但大量普通 ICE 或理论性问题不值得逐一投入同等时间。
- 已新增并建议使用 `S-found-by-fuzzing`，以及用于标记已在生态代码中得到验证的 `S-found-in-wild`；后者通常叠加在前者之上。`needs-triage` 可继续作为通用默认标签，不必为 fuzzed issues 更名或改变现有查询；也有人提出过 `fuzzed-untriaged`、`S-artificial-code` 等替代方案，但未形成结论。
- 关于 LLM：多数意见认为不能简单把 LLM 辅助编写 fuzzer、自动扫描发现的问题，与单纯由 LLM 生成的错误或幻觉式 issue 混为一谈；若需要标记“由 LLM 发现”，应使用独立标签。当前共识倾向于 `S-found-by-fuzzing` 是否涉及 LLM 并不重要，关键是问题是否来自寻找 bug 的自动化测试过程。
- 对 LLVM miscompile 的处理建议是：Rust 侧只保留那些可能需要 backport、涉及 opsem、safe code unsoundness 或严重 Rust UX 影响的问题；若只是普通且不值得 backport 的 LLVM bug，尤其已经有明确 LLVM 修复路径的 fuzzed issue，应尽快关闭 Rust 侧 issue。若问题来自真实代码，则通常更可能需要跟踪和 backport；不过仍应允许提交者无法或不愿创建 LLVM issue 时在 Rust 侧报告。
- 仍需依靠人工判断具体优先级，不能机械关闭所有 fuzzed issues；LLVM miscompile 的 backport 政策和流程（LLVM 修复是否 backport、Rust LLVM submodule 更新及其 backport）也未完全明确。相关 fuzzing 指南、issue template 及 `S-found-by-fuzzing` 的说明正在考虑或提议更新。

messages.en:
:vi_fon: my attempt at a first pass for this: added `S-found-by-fuzzing` and `S-found-in-wild` labels can be used to tag whether something has been found via LLMs/fuzzing (and hence, it's unclear whether it is shown in practice) and whether something *has* been demonstrated in ecosystem code. the latter is mostly something to add to existing `S-found-by-fuzzing` issues and not needed in general

these seem compatible with the existing `S-has-mvce` and `E-needs-mcve` labels with the exception that we don't want to add an `E-please-go-on-a-wild-goose-chase-to-find-code-that-demonstrates-this-fuzzed-bug` label, and so both are just `S-` labels
messages.zh:
: vi_fon:我对此的首次尝试: added`S-found-by-fuzzing`和`S-found-in-wild`标签可用于标记是否已通过LLM/fuzzing找到某些内容（因此，尚不清楚它是否在实践中显示） ，以及是否在生态系统代码中*已*演示了某些内容。后者主要是添加到现有`S-found-by-fuzzing`问题，一般不需要

这些似乎与现有的`S-has-mvce`和`E-needs-mcve`标签，但例外是我们不想添加`E-please-go-on-a-wild-goose-chase-to-find-code-that-demonstrates-this-fuzzed-bug`标签，所以两者都只是`S-`标签

messages.en: perhaps we can even add an explicit issue template for issues found via fuzzing, not that people would explicitly use those
messages.zh: 也许我们甚至可以为通过模糊处理发现的问题添加一个明确的问题模板，而不是人们会明确使用这些模板

and I think I have sinned against this by having a label that was for a single target but I just expected there to be another such issue/PR in the next 10 years or however long we're on GitHub/the target is supported.

which is why the only time I raised my voice about this was like "...okay but it's a minor libs thing it is probably just going to live only long enough until we submit a stab report and have no particular issues while it's unstable because those are 90% bikeshedding".

messages.en:
so it did but I had an Opinion
which is that fuzzing, according to our guide, is any method of
> For the purposes of this guide, *fuzzing* is any testing methodology that involves compiling a wide variety of programs in an attempt to uncover bugs in rustc. F
messages.zh:
所以确实如此，但我有一个意见
也就是说，根据我们的指南，模糊处理是任何
>在本指南中， * fuzzing *是指涉及编译各种程序以试图发现rustc中的错误的任何测试方法。F

messages.en: And also that we have had the problem of "dual-use" labels before.
messages.zh: 而且我们以前也遇到过“两用”标签的问题。

messages.en:
Which is why C-gub exists.
Because passively-aggressively labeling the many issues that boil down to "rustc miscompiles my code" "...but your code is UB?" "...oh. erm. well. it shouldn't miscompile my code!" ":woman_facepalming:" with `C-discussion` makes it hard to find the **actual discussions**.
messages.zh:
这就是C-gub存在的原因。
因为被动地-积极地标记归结为“rustc错误编译我的代码”的许多问题...但是你的代码是UB ？ ““ “哦，嗯。好吧。它不应该错误编译我的代码！” “： woman_facepalming ：”`C-discussion`很难找到* *实际讨论* *。

messages.en: So if we need a special label for "found using an LLM", I think it should be a separate one.
messages.zh: 因此，如果我们需要“使用LLM找到”的特殊标签，我认为它应该是一个单独的标签。

messages.en: Do LLMs "compile a wide variety of programs" to find bugs? I suspect that some LLM workflows involve mostly reading the compiler source code instead.
messages.zh: LLM是否“编译了各种各样的程序”来查找错误？我怀疑一些LLM工作流程主要涉及阅读编译器源代码。

messages.en: ...well obviously this person is compiling a wide variety of programs or they wouldn't have found 20 issues.
messages.zh: ...很明显，这个人正在编写各种各样的程序，否则他们不会发现20个问题。

messages.en: I'm not sure there's a meaningful difference between "traditional" fuzzers and LLM based fuzzing, except that the *users* of traditional fuzzers often know how to format the information in a more useful way, due to the barrier to entry.
messages.zh: 我不确定“传统”模糊和基于LLM的模糊之间是否有有意义的区别，除了传统模糊的*用户*通常知道如何以更有用的方式格式化信息，由于进入障碍。

messages.en: I guess we have a different idea of what counts as "wide" lol
messages.zh: 我想我们对什么是“宽”有不同的看法lol

messages.en: "wide" is vague on purpose, yes.
messages.zh: “宽”是有意模糊的，是的。

messages.en: Our issue labels have to communicate their intent with their name or a *very* short description (if anyone ever reads it)
messages.zh: 我们的问题标签必须用他们的名字或*非常*简短的描述（如果有人读过）传达他们的意图

messages.en: I do not want this label applied to a random bullshit LLM-vomit issue that we check for repro and then throw back as nonsense.
messages.zh: 我不希望将此标签应用于随机废话LLM呕吐问题，我们检查REP ，然后将其视为无稽之谈。

messages.en: Fair enough.
messages.zh: 就是 如此 。

messages.en: If we need a separate "it came from an LLM" label for whatever reason I strongly feel it should just be a different label, because we should have the courage to say `this-issue-is-ass` when that is what we are trying to say.
messages.zh: 如果我们出于任何原因需要一个单独的“它来自法学硕士”标签，我强烈认为它应该是一个不同的标签，因为我们应该有勇气说`this-issue-is-ass`而这正是我们要说的。

messages.en: And if everyone else sincerely believes "no, this is different, we won't apply this label to random issues which are terrible token vomit just for being terrible token vomit without even thinking about whether or not they were indeed sourced by any kind of automated testing regime", then feel free to add "and LLMs" back to the label description and apply it as you deem appropriate.
messages.zh: 如果其他人真诚地认为“不，这是不同的，我们不会将此标签应用于随机问题，这些问题仅仅是因为是可怕的代币呕吐，甚至没有考虑它们是否确实来自任何类型的自动化测试制度” ，然后随时在标签描述中添加“和LLM” ，并在您认为合适的情况下应用它。

messages.en: and I will be fine with this until the day I find that a nontrivial % of these issues, despite the label being applied to hundreds of issues, are just getting the label because they are bad bugs from a hallucination by often individual users and no automated testing regime was even implied.
messages.zh: 直到有一天，我发现这些问题中有很大一部分（尽管标签适用于数百个问题）只是得到了标签，因为它们通常是个人用户幻觉中的坏错误，甚至没有暗示自动化测试制度。

messages.en: and then I will say "I told you so" and wrack my brain for an equally silly name.
messages.zh: 然后我会说“我告诉过你” ，然后绞尽脑汁想一个同样愚蠢的名字。

messages.en: ( the whimsy is terribly important, you see. )
messages.zh: （奇思妙想非常重要，你看。）

messages.en:
@_**theemathas|739695** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Triaging.20and.20passing.20on.20fuzzed.20issues/near/637082271):
```quote
Do LLMs "compile a wide variety of programs" to find bugs? I suspect that some LLM workflows involve mostly reading the compiler source code instead.
```

Yes they compile a lot of programs. LLMs have a lot of bad ideas, the trick is that they are enormously better at guessing an exciting input than chance, and you can eliminate the cruft mechanically.
messages.zh:
@_* * theemathas | 739695 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Triaging.20and.20passing.20on.20fuzzed.20issues/near/637082271):
```quote
Do LLMs "compile a wide variety of programs" to find bugs? I suspect that some LLM workflows involve mostly reading the compiler source code instead.
```是的，他们编译了很多程序。 LLM有很多糟糕的想法，诀窍在于他们在猜测令人兴奋的输入方面比偶然性要好得多，你可以机械地消除困难。

messages.en: Perhaps the core idea here is bugs that are found by looking for them, and are not known to be impacting normal usage. Maybe that devalues human efforts at looking for bugs :shrug:
messages.zh: 也许这里的核心思想是通过寻找它们发现的错误，并且不知道这些错误会影响正常使用。也许这会贬低人类寻找虫子的努力：耸耸肩：

messages.en: my understanding is every "agentic" harness is or at least was prone to neurotically verifying everything.
messages.zh: 我的理解是，每个“特工”线束都倾向于或至少倾向于神经性地验证一切。

messages.en: but I fear getting too deep into that particular direction, whereas what I would describe as "core" to "fuzzing" is the automated testing regime which has selected, essentially, some... horizon?... of possible programs and is scanning along that.
messages.zh: 但我担心过于深入那个特定的方向，而我所描述的“核心”到“模糊”是自动化测试制度，它基本上已经选择了一些可能的程序，并且正在沿着这个方向扫描。

messages.en: and I would be averse to conflating an issue found by such *scans* with intentional programming efforts that are LLM-assisted or involve driving an LLM but are trying to *actually do something*, even if what LLM-based tools do "by default" resembles certain kinds of algorithmic searches.
messages.zh: 我反对将此类*扫描*发现的问题与LLM辅助或涉及驾驶LLM但试图*实际做某事*的有意编程工作混为一谈，即使基于LLM的工具“默认”类似于某些类型的算法搜索。

messages.en: one, at the very least, started life as a query for "find me a problem" and the other started as a query for "find me a solution".

and I would be averse to conflating an issue found by such *scans* with intentional programming efforts that are LLM-assisted or involve driving an LLM but are trying to *actually do something*, even if what LLM-based tools do "by default" resembles certain kinds of algorithmic searches.
```

( also to be clear I think it's fine if people think *both* of these cases are lower-priority, I just want to like... clearly tier "this issue is real and we can repro it" above "this issue is itself a confabulation". )

messages.en: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/165439 is a potential example of a wasteful fuzzer issue, the kind we should really need preparing for.
messages.zh: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/165439是一个潜在的浪费引信问题的例子，这是我们真正需要准备的。

messages.en: Expect fuzzing of LLVM to get more effective at finding bugs, and then people to use LLMs to craft Rust reproducers for all LLVM miscompiles as they are reported
messages.zh: 希望模糊LLVM能够更有效地发现错误，然后人们使用LLM为所有LLVM错误编译创建Rust复制器

messages.en: :river_fon: so to be clear, is this the kind of issue we should close as not useful or just be annoyed about
messages.zh: : river_fon:所以要明确的是，这是我们应该关闭的那种无用的问题，还是只是对

messages.en: Can we add that to documentation about how to fuzz? Namely if you're tempted to write something like "The LLVM IR rustc emits is correct" Then it's not a bug in our code, reported upstream, and don't report it to us.
messages.zh: 我们可以将其添加到有关如何模糊处理的文档中吗？也就是说，如果你想写一些类似“LLVM IR rustc发出的是正确的”这样的东西，那么它不是我们代码中的错误，而是上游报告，不要向我们报告。

messages.en: tbh keeping track of upstream bugs is sometimes useful but here, yes, not in this way
messages.zh: tbh跟踪上游bug有时是有用的，但在这里，是的，不是这样

messages.en: I was particularly annoyed by an issue recently that boiled down to "this was already fixed in LLVM and just needs to get in LLVM releases and then rust will pick it up" and it didn't even seem like anything critical
messages.zh: 我对最近的一个问题感到特别恼火，这个问题可以归结为“这已经在LLVM中修复了，只需要进入LLVM版本，然后生锈就会捡起来” ，它甚至看起来并不像任何关键的

messages.en: if it's not making safe code unsound, or something that seriously harms UX in Rust... like the many cases that are just an optimization issue... and it has already gotten to LLVM then just close the issue on our side.
messages.zh: 如果它没有使安全代码变得不健全，或者严重损害Rust中的用户体验......就像许多只是优化问题的案例......并且它已经到达LLVM ，那么只需在我们这边关闭问题即可。

messages.en: in saying this I am partially echoing @**Nikita Popov** whomst already voiced a comment that these are probably not useful (though did not say specifically to close them) #**t-compiler/llvm>Notifications about LLVM issues@636969366**
messages.zh: 在说这句话时，我部分回应了@ * * Nikita Popov * * ，他已经发表评论说这些可能没有用（尽管没有具体说明关闭它们） # * * t-compiler/llvm >关于LLVM问题的通知@ 636969366 * *

messages.en:
> Expect fuzzing of LLVM to get more effective at finding bugs, and then people to use LLMs to craft Rust reproducers for all LLVM miscompiles as they are reported

I think it’s important to call out that this appears *not* to have been the case here.
messages.zh:
>期望模糊LLVM能够更有效地发现错误，然后人们使用LLM为所有LLVM错误编译创建Rust复制器

我认为重要的是要指出，这里的情况似乎并非如此。

messages.en: I think @**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** did not necessarily mean to imply a causal link between these events, @**Frank Steffahn**.
messages.zh: 我认为@ * * Ben Kimock （ Saethlin ） * *并不一定意味着这些事件之间存在因果关系， @ * * Frank Steffahn * *。

messages.en:
> this appears *not* to have been the case here

I.e. “Found by an LLM-built differential fuzzer (`-O0` vs `-O1+` vs Miri); I reproduced it on the versions above.” (in the description of #165439) sounds to me like an LLM helped with building a fuzzer *on rust code* (but the fuzzing itself was not involving an LLM porting any known LLVM issue over to Rust, or anything like that).
messages.zh:
>这似乎*不是*这里的情况

即“由LLM制造的差分引信（`-O0`对比`-O1+`vs Miri ） ；我在上面的版本中复制了它。”（在# 165439的描述中）在我看来，这听起来像是LLM帮助*在Rust代码上*构建引信（但模糊本身并不涉及LLM将任何已知的LLVM问题移植到Rust或类似的东西）。

messages.en: right.
messages.zh: 是

messages.en: These are not made more-useful by being independent events.
messages.zh: 这些活动并不会因独立活动而变得更有用。

messages.en:
@_**workingjubilee|281757** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Triaging.20and.20passing.20on.20fuzzed.20issues/near/637365636):
```quote
I think @**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** did not necessarily mean to imply a causal link between these events, @**Frank Steffahn**.

sure may be the case, but regardless it took me a while to figure out that this appears not to have been the case here, so I thought it’s important to mention for this discussion :innocent:
messages.zh:
@_* * workingjubilee | 281757 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Triaging.20and.20passing.20on.20fuzzed.20issues/near/637365636):
```quote
I think @**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** did not necessarily mean to imply a causal link between these events, @**Frank Steffahn**.
```当然可能是这样，但无论如何，我花了一段时间才发现这里的情况似乎并非如此，所以我认为在这次讨论中提及这一点很重要：无辜：

messages.en: A Rust reproducer *was* crafted for an LLVM miscompile.
messages.zh: Rust复制器*是为LLVM错误编译而制作的*。

messages.en: It was not *deliberately* crafted *based on* an LLVM miscompile.
messages.zh: 它不是基于* LLVM错误编译的*故意*精心制作的*。

messages.en: But it is still a Rust reproducer of an LLVM miscompilation.
messages.zh: 但它仍然是LLVM错误编译的Rust复制器。

messages.en: I swear I am not just trying to be dense.
messages.zh: 我发誓我不只是想变得稠密。

messages.en:
I suppose the Rust issue becomes relatively useless as soon as it’s sufficiently evident that any fix of the LLVM issue will definitely fix the Rust reproducer.

Otherwise, it’s still *somewhat* useful to be tracking the issue on our side, isn’t it? As in: someone can re-run the rust-reproducer *as a sanity check* before saying “yes the LLVM fix that’s now part of rustc does indeed fix this miscompile” and closing it on our side.
messages.zh:
我认为，只要足够明显的是LLVM问题的任何修复肯定会修复Rust复制程序， Rust问题就会变得相对无用。

否则，在我们这边跟踪问题仍然*有些*有用，不是吗？ 如：有人可以重新运行rust-reproducer *作为健全性检查* ，然后说“是的，现在是rustc的一部分的LLVM修复确实修复了此错误编译” ，并在我们这边关闭它。

messages.en: Well, in the past it was quite clear that if someone hits a Rust miscompile in the wild and it's root-caused to an LLVM miscompile we should at least backport the LLVM fix to beta, and having an issue on our side was possibly useful for tracking that progress. Increasingly, that logic just does not apply.
messages.zh: 嗯，在过去，很明显，如果有人在野外点击了Rust错误编译，并且它是由LLVM错误编译引起的，我们至少应该将LLVM修复程序反向移植到测试版，并且我们方面的问题可能对跟踪该进度很有用。这种逻辑越来越不适用。

messages.en: :river_fon: correct me if I'm wrong, but the current process seems to be to always backport minor LLVM version bumps and then wait until new releases for major bumps?
messages.zh: : river_fon:如果我错了，请纠正我，但当前的过程似乎总是回移次要LLVM版本颠簸，然后等到新版本出现重大颠簸？

messages.en:
* get the LLVM fix backported on the LLVM side
* wait for our LLVM people to update the LLVM submodule
* wait for our LLVM people to backport the LLVM submodule update

I think?
messages.zh:
*将LLVM修复程序反向移植到LLVM端
*等待我们的LLVM人员更新LLVM子模块
*等待我们的LLVM人员回移LLVM子模块更新

我想是吧？

messages.en: so, loosely what I said but potentially with more active effort to ensure the fix does get into a minor LLVM version we can backport?
messages.zh: 所以，我所说的很松散，但可能会更积极地努力确保修复进入我们可以反向移植的次要LLVM版本？

messages.en: Yes. LLVM does not have a policy of backporting miscompile fixes.
messages.zh: 是。LLVM没有反向移植错误编译修复的策略。

messages.en: do they otherwise not do minor versions unless people are explicitly interested in backporting fixes?
messages.zh: 除非人们明确表示对反向移植修复感兴趣，否则他们不会做次要版本吗？

messages.en: basically I'm wondering if the policy is *always* to backport minor version bumps or just if we specifically have something we want in them, and it's within the release branch window
messages.zh: 基本上，我想知道策略是*始终*回移次要版本凹凸，还是仅仅是我们特别想要的东西，并且它位于发布分支窗口中

messages.en: That's not a question I can answer. I just know that most of the time when I root-cause a miscompile to LLVM there is already an LLVM issue for it that's been closed and the fix not backported.
messages.zh: 这不是我能回答的问题。我只知道，大多数时候，当我从根本上导致错误编译到LLVM时，已经存在LLVM问题，该问题已被关闭，并且修复未向后移植。

messages.en: fair enough. I guess most people just care about this on clang which is implicitly always going to contain the correct fixes in whatever the next version is
messages.zh: 公平。我猜大多数人只是关心clang上的这个，无论下一个版本是什么，它总是隐含地包含正确的修复

messages.en:
I also just want to emphasize how many miscompile issues are filed against LLVM: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Amiscompilation

LLVM has about half as many miscompile issues per week as we have issues total. That's why I'm bringing up this entire possibility.
messages.zh: 我还想强调一下有多少错误编译问题是针对LLVM提出的：https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AmiscompilationLLVM每周的错误编译问题大约是问题总数的一半。 这就是我提出这种可能性的原因。

@_**workingjubilee|281757** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Triaging.20and.20passing.20on.20fuzzed.20issues/near/637360403):
```quote
if it's not making safe code unsound, or something that seriously harms UX in Rust... like the many cases that are just an optimization issue... and it has already gotten to LLVM then just close the issue on our side.
```

If they all got LLVM reports that would be nice. But we have some LLVM bugs in our issue tracker that don't even have an LLVM report...
messages.zh:
@_* * workingjubilee | 281757 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Triaging.20and.20passing.20on.20fuzzed.20issues/near/637360403):
```quote
if it's not making safe code unsound, or something that seriously harms UX in Rust... like the many cases that are just an optimization issue... and it has already gotten to LLVM then just close the issue on our side.
```如果他们都有LLVM报告，那就太好了。 但我们的问题跟踪器中有一些LLVM错误，甚至没有LLVM报告...

messages.en: And I think people fuzzing and then expecting us to do the work of reducing and bisecting the compiler output to make it presentable for LLVM is *far* more unreasonable.
messages.zh: 我认为人们模糊不清，然后期望我们做减少和二分编译器输出的工作，使其可供LLVM使用，这*远*更不合理。

messages.en: My general thinking is that we should only track basic LLVM bugs on the Rust side if we believe that we may want to backport them. For https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/165439 this should lead to a clear decision (utterly uninteresting and irrelevant miscompile, certainly no need to backport). Other cases may be less clear though. If a backport doesn't seem justified, we should just close the Rust side issue right away.
messages.zh: 我的总体想法是，如果我们认为我们可能想要回移它们，我们应该只在Rust端跟踪基本的LLVM bug。https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/165439这应该会导致一个明确的决定（完全无趣和不相关的错误编译，当然不需要回溯）。但其他情况可能不太清楚。如果后端似乎不合理，我们应该立即关闭Rust端问题。

messages.en: I think the opsem-relevant issues should also stay open
messages.zh: 我认为与opsem相关的问题也应该保持开放

messages.en: That's why "basic LLVM bugs". Those that don't have anything interesting going on.
messages.zh: 这就是“基本LLVM错误”的原因。那些没有任何有趣的事情发生的人。

messages.en: Ah, I see. Do we tell the people doing fuzzing to reduce the issue and file an LLVM report, or what do you propose?
messages.zh: 啊，我明白了。我们是否告诉做模糊处理的人来减少问题并提交LLVM报告，或者你有什么建议？

messages.en: Also would you apply this to basic LLVM bugs in general, or only fuzzed ones?
messages.zh: 您是将其应用于一般的基本LLVM漏洞，还是仅适用于模糊漏洞？

messages.en: If by "not fuzzed" we mean "someone encountered it in a real-world codebase" (as opposed to "not fuzzed" in the sense of "people used their own brain as a fuzzer") that's a strong indication that the fix should be backported, so we should track the issue.
messages.zh: 如果“不模糊”是指“有人在真实世界的代码库中遇到它” （而不是“人们将自己的大脑用作引信”意义上的“不模糊” ） ，这强烈表明修复程序应该反向移植，因此我们应该跟踪问题。

messages.en: thanks, that's a useful "ballpark measurement" for us when triaging and prioritizing :)
messages.zh: 谢谢，这对我们进行分类和优先排序时来说是一个有用的“球场测量”:)

messages.en: I would consider "not fuzzed" to mean "found for a purpose other than finding bugs", but I guess it makes no difference, since at that point there is also at least *something* interesting (to rustc) about the bug
messages.zh: 我认为“不模糊”的意思是“发现bug以外的目的” ，但我想这没什么区别，因为在那一点上，这个bug至少还有*一些*有趣的东西* （对rustc来说）

messages.en: Does it make sense to rename the label to `S-artificial-code` or something?
messages.zh: 将标签重命名为`S-artificial-code`或者其他的东西”

messages.en: eh, i think the label is fine
messages.zh: 嗯，我认为这个标签很好

topics.name: Arbitrary int sizes
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：提议支持 `2..=128` 位的任意整数类型（包括 `i24`、`u18` 等非 2 的幂），在内存中扩展到下一个 2 的幂；内部可用 `u23` 表示大小，以匹配 LLVM 对整数位宽的限制。动机包括支持 eZ80 等奇特目标、嵌入式开发和模拟器。
- **方案与实现方向**：讨论中指出该提案与已有的 RFC 3686 基本相关；目前更倾向先做一个增量式 proof of concept：先让 `u<N>`/`i<N>` 对现有标准整数类型起别名，初步对非标准 `N` 报错，之后支持 `N <= 128`，最终再考虑更大的范围。编译器需要处理 `N` 的推导、MIR lowering，以及 LLVM 后端所需的位宽扩展。
- **trait 与文档设计存在分歧**：有人建议增加 `Int`/`Uint` trait 及关联常量（如 `SIZE`/`BITS`），通过统一 trait impl 减少整数方法和文档重复；但反对意见认为这可能改变 inherent method 与 trait method 的名称解析行为，造成 breaking change，也不一定减少代码。如何生成和展示这些整数类型的 rustdoc 仍是主要难题。
- **ABI、对齐和布局尚未解决**：不同位宽整数的 alignment 是否随 `N` 单调增加、`u24` 是否至少按 2 字节对齐，以及 `N > 128` 应采用何种 ABI，都没有结论。x86 的 `_BitInt`/128 位整数 ABI 与其他目标不一致，可能需要 `c_bitint` ABI wrapper；相关 ABI 问题被认为是推进该功能的重要阻碍。
- **性能与后端实现问题**：在小型目标上，LLVM 和 compiler-rt 当前对 bitint libcalls 的支持不足，可能导致大整数运算生成严重膨胀的指令序列；有人提出使用类似 `awint` 的统一泛化实现来减少重复特化。总体上，参与者支持继续推进，并已提出项目目标，但尚未形成最终 RFC 或实现方案。

- Feature Name: `arbitrary_ints`
- Start Date: 2026-10-31
- RFC PR: [rust-lang/rfcs#0000](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/0000)
- Rust Issue: [rust-lang/rust#0000](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/0000)

## Summary
[summary]: #summary

Add support for arbitrarily-sized integers that aren't powers of two, in the range `2..=128`. These would be extended to the next power of two, as LLVM targets are allowed to require a power of two. The size would be stored in a `u23` and support internally the range `1..=(1<<23)` for [parity with LLVM](https://llvm.org/doxygen/classllvm_1_1IntegerType.html#details:~:text=enum,23%29%20%7D).

## Motivation
[motivation]: #motivation

Rust has rapidly become an embedded language and a language used for esoteric targets. Many of these, such as the eZ80 (24-bit pointers, also used in the TI-84+CE graphing calculator, which has an extensive community surrounding it and the community-driven C toolchain), and very old computers such as the UNIVAC-418 (with 18-bit pointers) have oddly sized words. Even outside of actually running Rust on them, emulating them is useful for preservation purposes, and being able to have a integer sized appropriately for their pointers instead of having to fake it with a too-large one, or in the future use pattern types to represent them, would be very useful.

## Guide-level explanation
[guide-level-explanation]: #guide-level-explanation

You can use any size integer between 2 and 128 bits. The use of a `u1`/`i1` is not allowed, as a one-bit integer is pretty much pointless and can be replaced with using a `bool`. This includes sizes that are not powers of two, such as `i24` or `u18`. Each of these has the associated methods and constants of the standard power of two types, such as `::MAX`, `::MIN`, as well as stuff like `.clamp` and more niche methods like `.strict_add_signed`. Each of these is expanded in memory into the next power of two, but in all other respects can and should be treated as though it is actually the size it is listed as.

## Reference-level explanation
[reference-level-explanation]: #reference-level-explanation

The `UintTy` and `IntTy` enums will be replaced with a newtype wrapper around a new `IntSize` type that will initially store a `u32` representing the number of bits, and after the change is merged, then a `u23` (and with the value of 1 being disallowed) as we do need a `u8388608`/`i8388608` for LLVM parity. As a final step of MIR lowering before being passed to backends, all integer types with a size that is not a power of two will be sign-extended to the next power of two.

From the perspective of the standard library, two new traits (and associated lang items) will be added (with `#[rustc_deny_explicit_impl]`), `Int` and `Uint`. These traits will only include one item that has to be provided with impls within them, `BITS`, which will be automatically implemented by the compiler for all integer types used in the crate being built and its dependencies. Notably, the impl will be synthesized at compile time when it is actually needed from the integer type being used. This will then be used with the general impls replacing the macros currently used to generate all the methods and other associated items, and those items will instead be associated with the traits, which will be included in the prelude. Use of these traits directly would also allow library authors to let users decide on the size of integers used in certain scenarios, and so might be split off into a separate feature.

Errors for different unsupported sizes would have different messages. For `u0`/`i0`, the message would recommend use of `()`. For `u1/i1`, the message would recommend `bool`. For `uX`/`iX` where X is over 128, then the message would mention that `u128`/`i128` is the largest supported size.

## Drawbacks
[drawbacks]: #drawbacks

This would add more complexity to lowering and the language overall, but having the additional flexibility of arbitrarily sized integers is worth the additional complexity.

## Rationale and alternatives
[rationale-and-alternatives]: #rationale-and-alternatives

Alternatives include some existing libraries which have wrappers around the existing types. We could also include something similar in the standard library itself. This is not the best option, as then that means you can't use the literal syntax and have to construct all of them with a `::new` static method, or at the very least wrap them with a newtype constructor. This also means that on stable they may have fewer optimizations compared to built-in types, as pattern types are not stabilized yet.

## Prior art
[prior-art]: #prior-art

Zig has arbitrary integer integer, sized up to `65535`. Some other languages have features similar to pattern types, allowing mimicing this feature (most notably, Ada). In Rust specifically, [there](https://lib.rs/crates/ux) [are](https://lib.rs/crates/unin) [many](https://crates.io/crates/twelve_bit) [different](https://lib.rs/crates/u7) crates mimicking this feature, many of which (but not all) are for only specific sizes.

## Unresolved questions
[unresolved-questions]: #unresolved-questions

- How do we deal with documentation?
- What methods/constants do we add to integer types? One that comes to mind is associating the type that it is extended to with the types.
- Do we have the compiler synthesize all of the integer types when compiling the standard library, or do we have it synthesize them when they are used?

## Future possibilities
[future-possibilities]: #future-possibilities

- Allowing `repr(packed)` structs to pack integers into just a few bytes (i.e. packing two `u4`s into a single byte), or adding a new kind of type for these kind of bitfields

-功能名称：`arbitrary_ints`-开始日期： 2026-10-31
- RFC PR ： [rust-lang/rfcs # 0000] （https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/0000)-生锈问题： [rust-lang/rust # 0000] （https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/0000)# #摘要
[summary] ： # summary

在范围内添加对非2的幂的任意大小整数的支持`2..=128`。这些将扩展到下一个2的幂，因为LLVM目标允许需要2的幂。尺寸将存储在`u23`并在内部支持该系列`1..=(1<<23)`[与LLVM同等] （https://llvm.org/doxygen/classllvm_1_1IntegerType.html#details:~:text=enum,23%29%20%7D).# #激励
[motivation]: # motivation

Rust已迅速成为一种嵌入式语言和用于深奥目标的语言。 其中许多，例如eZ80 （ 24位指针，也用于TI-84 + CE图形计算器，该计算器周围有广泛的社区和社区驱动的C工具链） ，以及非常古老的计算机，例如UNIVAC-418 （带有18位指针） ，都有奇怪大小的单词。即使在它们上实际运行Rust之外，模拟它们对于保存目的也很有用，并且能够为它们的指针指定适当大小的整数，而不必用太大的整数伪造它，或者在将来使用模式类型来表示它们，将是非常有用的。

# #指南级解释
[guide-level-explanation] ： # guide-level-explanation

您可以使用2到128位之间的任何大小的整数。 使用`u1`/`i1`不允许使用，因为一个位整数几乎毫无意义，可以用`bool`。这包括不是2的幂的大小，例如`i24` 或 `u18`。它们中的每一个都有两种类型的标准幂的相关方法和常数，例如`::MAX`, `::MIN`，以及诸如`.clamp`以及更多利基方法，例如`.strict_add_signed`。它们中的每一个都在内存中扩展为下一个2的幂，但在所有其他方面，可以而且应该被视为实际上是它被列为的大小。

# #参考级解释
[reference-level-explanation] ： # reference-level-explanation

这`UintTy`和`IntTy`枚举将被替换为围绕新类型的包装`IntSize`类型，最初将存储`u32`表示位数，变更合并后，`u23`（并且不允许使用1的值） ，因为我们确实需要`u8388608`/`i8388608`对于LLVM奇偶校验。作为传递到后端之前降低MIR的最后一步，大小不为2的整数类型将被符号扩展到下一个2的幂。

从标准库的角度来看，将添加两个新的特征（和相关的语言项目） （`#[rustc_deny_explicit_impl]`),`Int`和`Uint`。这些特征将只包括一个必须在其中提供含义的项目，`BITS`，它将由编译器为正在构建的crate及其依赖项中使用的所有整数类型自动实现。值得注意的是， impl将在编译时从正在使用的整数类型实际需要时合成。然后，这将与通用暗示一起使用，替换当前用于生成所有方法和其他相关项目的宏，这些项目将与特征相关联，这些特征将包含在前奏中。 直接使用这些特征也将允许库作者让用户决定在某些场景中使用的整数的大小，因此可能会被分割成一个单独的功能。不同不支持的大小的错误会有不同的消息。对于`u0`/`i0`，消息将建议使用`()`对于`u1/i1`，消息将推荐`bool`对于`uX`/`iX`其中X超过128 ，则消息会提到`u128`/`i128`是最大支持的大小。

# #缺点
[缺点] ： #缺点

这将增加降低和整体语言的复杂性，但具有任意大小整数的额外灵活性值得额外的复杂性。

# #理由和替代方案
[理由和替代方案] ： #理由和替代方案

替代方案包括一些现有的库，这些库在现有类型周围具有包装。我们也可以在标准库本身中包含类似的内容。这不是最好的选择，因为这意味着您不能使用文字语法，必须使用`::new`静态方法，或者至少用newtype构造函数包装它们。 这也意味着，与内置类型相比，在稳定模式下，它们的优化可能更少，因为模式类型尚未稳定。

# #现有技术
[prior-art]: # prior-art

Zig具有任意整数，大小为`65535`。其他一些语言具有类似于模式类型的功能，允许模仿此功能（最着名的是Ada ）。特别是在Rust中， [那里] （https://lib.rs/crates/ux)是https://lib.rs/crates/unin)许多https://crates.io/crates/twelve_bit)不同https://lib.rs/crates/u7)模仿此功能的板条箱，其中许多（但不是全部）仅适用于特定尺寸。

# #未解决的问题
[unresolved-questions]: #个未解决的问题

-我们如何处理文件？
-我们为整数类型添加哪些方法/常量？ 我想到的一个是将其扩展到的类型与类型相关联。-我们是让编译器在编译标准库时合成所有整数类型，还是让编译器在使用它们时合成它们？

# #未来的可能性
[未来的可能性] ： #未来的可能性

-允许`repr(packed)`将整数打包成几个字节的结构（即打包两个`u4`为单个字节） ，或为这些类型的位字段添加一种新类型

messages.en:
A few years ago I was interacting with the way 128-bit operations would compile down on extremely small targets. They way it is currently set up with compiler-builtins shims and LLVM, it ends up inlining all the shift operations and many things. This is fine for first one or maybe two integer sizes above the register size, but really likes to explode beyond that (e.x. on current nightly AVR 128 bit division takes 3395 lines of assembly, ~10 kb of instructions). It could be changed to use a single generic function that doesn't call recursively to smaller functions, but even then there is a ridiculous amount of duplication if there are a lot of different integer sizes being specialized for.
One of the original reasons I made my `awint` crate back in the day, was that I was going to propose incorporating `awint` to do all operations for  integers more than twice the target register size. `awint` is unusual for a bigint library in that it separates the reference type from the storage type. It can support arbitrary fixed-width stack types as well as dynamically allocated ones, and they all can have a unified `Bits` reference made to them, that does all the work for any size of integer with a single set of functions. So the only specialization involves setting up a pointer and a constant size before calling the generic `Bits` functions. Would we need something like it for this proposal?
messages.zh:
几年前，我正在与128位操作在非常小的目标上编译的方式进行交互。它们目前使用编译器内置的垫片和LLVM进行设置，最终内联了所有的移位操作和许多东西。这对于寄存器大小以上的前一个或两个整数大小来说是可以的，但真的很喜欢超出这个范围（例如在当前的夜间AVR 128位划分中，需要3395行装配，约10 kb的指令）。 可以将其更改为使用单个泛型函数，该函数不会递归调用较小的函数，但即使这样，如果有很多不同的整数大小专门用于此，也会有大量的重复。
我最初的原因之一是`awint`当时的板条箱是，我提议将`awint`对超过目标寄存器大小两倍的整数执行所有操作。`awint`对于bigint库来说是不寻常的，因为它将引用类型与存储类型分开。它可以支持任意固定宽度的堆栈类型以及动态分配的堆栈类型，并且它们都可以具有统一的`Bits`对它们的引用，这为具有单个函数集的任何大小的整数完成了所有工作。因此，唯一的专业化涉及在调用泛型之前设置指针和恒定大小`Bits`函数。对于此提案，我们是否需要类似的东西？

topics.name: Issue with Rust-analyzer, LLVM codebase and VS Code
topics.summary:
- 核心问题是 Rust 代码在 LLVM passes 中发生错误编译（对应 Issue #164667）。讨论者观察到 LLVM IR 中原本只有一次 load，但经过 x86 instruction selection 后，从同一 stack location 生成了两次 load；禁用 Stack Coloring 和 DAGCombiner 后输出恢复正常，因此怀疑问题与 SelectionDAG 有关，并在 Stack Coloring 阶段暴露。
- 该问题涉及 MIR 优化和 LLVM 的 soundness，社区认为对新贡献者而言较难入手；建议优先从 diagnostics 或 internal compiler errors（ICEs）等更容易通过搜索错误字符串展开调查的问题开始。
- 关于 LLM，提问者主要用 ChatGPT 分析 intermediate representations 和生成的 assembly，以定位出错的 pass 或阶段。社区提醒 LLM 可能掩盖症状，使 ICE 根因追踪更困难，并建议参考 Rust 项目的 LLM 使用规范及 `#llm-reviews` 频道。
- VS Code 加载 Rust 仓库、LLVM submodule、rust-analyzer 及相关扩展时会占用大量 CPU 和内存，甚至导致设备崩溃；有人反馈 8GB 和 16GB 设备都可能无法承受。可行的临时办法是增加 RAM 或禁用 rust-analyzer/相关扩展，提问者已通过禁用扩展缓解。
- 目前尚未确认 LLVM 侧是否已有对应 issue，也未形成明确修复方案；话题的解决状态还曾被标记为 resolved 后又标记为 unresolved。

topics.name: PSA: GitHub Copilot data training will be enabled
topics.summary:
- **核心问题：** GitHub 宣布自 4 月 24 日起，Copilot Free、Pro 和 Pro+ 用户的交互数据（包括输入、输出、代码片段及相关上下文）默认用于训练和改进 AI 模型，用户需要主动选择退出。讨论者担忧这是默认开启、缺乏明确同意，并可能涉及代码隐私、许可证和用户授权问题。

- **重要观点与建议：** 可在 `GitHub Settings → Copilot → Privacy` 中关闭“允许 GitHub 使用数据训练 AI 模型”；同时检查 `Settings → Applications → Authorized GitHub Apps`，关注 `Copilot Pull Request Reviewer` 和 `Copilot SWE Agent` 等授权。有人建议直接关闭 Copilot Free，或联系 GitHub Support 请求完全停用 Copilot。

- **授权行为引发争议：** 多名用户发现相关 GitHub Apps 在未明确同意的情况下被授权，撤销后还会反复出现，且不同用户的情况不一致。GitHub Support 说明，打开 Pull Request 页面可能触发 `Copilot SWE Agent` 的后台活动并刷新授权；后续又承认即使关闭 Copilot，授权仍可能通过独立请求重新添加，已升级给工程团队调查。

- **数据训练范围存在疑问：** 讨论认为关闭隐私设置据 GitHub 说法主要适用于用户使用 Copilot 产生的交互数据；公开仓库代码是否会被用于训练、他人使用 Copilot 访问个人代码时如何处理，缺乏明确说明。GitHub FAQ 表示，不会训练付费组织仓库的内容，但用户对其承诺和执行仍缺乏信任。

- **已知结论与未解决问题：** GitHub Support 表示目前可通过关闭 Copilot Free 和撤销授权来减少相关功能，但无法保证 `Copilot SWE Agent` 不再出现，也无法为账户提供更彻底的停用方式；授权反复出现、后台活动的具体权限与影响，以及数据是否实际用于 AI 训练，仍未得到明确解决。

`````

I couldn't say for certain without seeing their internals. If we take GitHub at their word, my understanding is that disabling this setting only really applies to code related to your use of Copilot. As per the FAQ:

```quote

**What data are you collecting?**
* When an individual user has this setting enabled, the interaction data we may collect includes:
  * Outputs accepted or modified by the user
  * Inputs sent to GitHub Copilot, including code snippets shown to the model
  * Code context surrounding the user’s cursor position
  * Comment and documentation that the user wrote
  * File names, repository structure, and navigation patterns
  * Interactions with Copilot features including Chat and inline suggestions
```


I'm not aware of any way to opt-out for public repositories and I would suspect that public repositories are thought of as "fair game", especially if permissively licensed (but I am not aware of official statements on such either way).

In theory, if you have this setting disabled and don't use Copilot, nothing has changed. Other than new authorizations potentially being added to your account. Which... do something, apparently, even if you don't use Copilot? Perhaps also if someone else with access to your code has the setting enabled. That might be a concern; if they use Copilot, GitHub only seems to try to protect the code if it is from an enterprise repository. As per the FAQ:

```quote

**What safeguards are in place to prevent enterprise code being used for model training due to an individual using a personal Copilot license while working in their employer’s codebase?**
* We do not train on the contents from any paid organization’s repos, regardless of whether a user is working in that repo with a Copilot Free, Pro, or Pro+ subscription. If a user’s GitHub account is a member of or outside collaborator with a paid organization, we exclude their interaction data from model training.

```

I would not personally trust any company to not train on every bit of data they can get their hands on. Especially when said company uses [dark patterns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_pattern) and engages in generally anti-user behavior. But I encourage people to make their own informed opinions.

messages.en:
Since I'm waiting on some workflows right now... here's where I am on my adventure with GitHub support, if anyone was curious:

- Oct 19, 2026, 9:14 AM GMT, ticket closed because... they took too long to get to it and assumed it was "fixed"? I mean, see below:

```spoiler GitHub Support Ticket Closed

Hi Sam,

We're writing to follow up on this ticket, and first to apologize. You reached out to GitHub Support and we did not get back to you in a reasonable amount of time. That's not the experience we want any customer to have, and we're sorry for the delay and for any frustration or disruption it caused you.

For transparency: over the past several weeks we've been working through an unusually high ticket volume alongside a series of platform incidents that affected many customers. Our engineering teams have since resolved those incidents and shipped a number of fixes. To be clear that this is context, not an excuse - regardless of what was happening behind the scenes, we should have replied to you sooner, and we didn't.

Because so much has changed since you first wrote in, there's a good chance the issue you reported has already been addressed. Rather than leave this ticket sitting open any longer, we're going to close it out.

If you're still seeing the problem - or anything related - please reply to this email or open a new ticket here: https://support.github.com/

A new ticket will reach the team faster and let us start fresh with the current state of your environment. If it helps, you're welcome to reference this ticket number in the new request and we'll pick up the history from there.

Thanks,
Ivy

```

- Oct 19, 2026, 10:50 PM GMT, I respond "My issue has not been resolved.", ticket is reopened
- Oct 20, 2026, 5:45 AM GMT, I get this response:

```spoiler GitHub Support Response

Hello Sam Kellam,
 
Thanks for writing in to GitHub Support and apologies for the substantial delay in getting back to you.
 
Opening a pull-request page can trigger background activity through the Copilot SWE Agent app to load Copilot code-review information for that page. We found this in the events you reported and noted it runs when viewing [this pull request](https://github.com/github/site-policy/pull/582), as an example.
 
These background requests use app access associated with your account and can create or refresh that access. The activity we checked does not show you deliberately starting a coding-agent task or requesting a new AI review. The app listing and these events are not, by themselves, evidence that your data was used for AI training.
 
To disable Copilot Free on GitHub.com and remove the current app authorisations, please follow these steps in order:
 

1. Open **Copilot settings**, then under **Visibility**, set **Show Copilot** to **Disabled**. See [Disabling GitHub Copilot Free](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/manage-your-account/disable-copilot-free).
2. Open **Settings > Applications > Authorized GitHub Apps** and select **Revoke all**, rather than revoking the Copilot apps individually. This removes all GitHub App authorisations, not just Copilot, so other apps you use may need to be authorised again. See [Reviewing and revoking authorization of GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/using-github-apps/reviewing-and-revoking-authorization-of-github-apps).

In our test, Copilot SWE Agent did not reappear when we reopened the example pull request after completing this sequence.
 
If you have more questions, please let us know.
 
Warmest regards,
GitHub Support

```

- Oct 20, 2026, 11:39 PM GMT, I get another response:

```spoiler GitHub Support Followup Response

Hello Sam Kellam,
 
Thanks for your patience. I'm writing to correct some of what we told you earlier.
 
We suggested disabling Copilot Free and using **Revoke all**, and said Copilot SWE Agent didn't reappear in our test. Since then, our further testing has shown that Copilot SWE Agent can be authorised again through a separate request, even with Copilot disabled. So those steps may not stop the authorisation from coming back, and we shouldn't have presented them as a fix.
 
We've escalated this to our engineering team to confirm what's expected, how to prevent it, and what access is involved. You can still revoke the authorisation if you want it removed in the meantime, but it may reappear.
 
We'll update you as soon as we have more information.
 
Warmest regards,
GitHub Support

```

- Oct 21, 2026, 1:21 AM GMT, I did revoke the authorizations. (not sure if before or after my response)
- Oct 21, 2026, 1:21 AM GMT, I respond: "Thanks for the updates. Would you be able to disable copilot entirely for my account? I've heard https://github.com/jieyouxu was able to have this done."
- Oct 21, 2026, 3:52 AM GMT, they respond:

```spoiler GitHub Support Response Three

Hello Sam Kellam,
 
Thank you for getting back to us.
 
The **Show Copilot** setting under **Visibility** in your [Copilot settings](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/manage-your-account/disable-copilot-free) disables Copilot Free, which turns off all features of Copilot on GitHub. Beyond this setting, Support doesn't have a way to disable Copilot further for an account.
 
As we mentioned, it may not stop the authorisation from being added again. Some GitHub-owned apps are [privileged apps](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/using-github-apps/privileged-github-apps) that GitHub needs for parts of the platform to work, so they can't always be switched off from your settings. We haven't confirmed whether that applies to the Copilot SWE Agent authorisation, and our engineering team is looking into it.
 
We hope this helps to clarify.
 
Warmest regards,
GitHub Support

```

topics.name: Result without value
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论是否应提供一种“无返回值”的 `Result<E>`，等价于 `Result<(), E>`，以避免显式写 `()` 和 `Ok(())`，并让类型更自描述。典型场景包括 `write!` 以及其他只需表示成功或失败的函数。
- **主要观点**：
  - Rust 中通常使用类型别名，例如 `type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, crate::Error>`；也可以定义 `type Result<E> = std::result::Result<(), E>`，但这种用法较少见，且可能与常见的 `std::io::Result`、`std::fmt::Result` 风格混淆。
  - Rust 一般不为已有类型组合额外引入新类型；`Result<(), E>` 已能表达该语义。通过 `use Result::Ok` / `use Result::Err`、带默认泛型参数的类型别名，或定义常量 `OK`，可以减少部分书写负担。
  - `Ok(())` 虽然略显笨拙，但 `Result<T, E>` 中 `Ok` 携带的值不能默认被视为“不重要”；新增单参数 `Result` 还会与已有的单参数别名产生显著混淆。
- **补充澄清**：`write!` 实际调用目标对象的 `write_fmt`；对 `String` 等对象，其结果是 `Result<(), std::fmt::Error>`，而不一定是 `std::io::Error`。
- **结论**：讨论中没有形成引入新 `Result<E>` 类型或为 `Ok()` 增加特殊语言行为的支持；更倾向于继续使用 `Result<(), E>`、类型别名及现有导入方式。
- **仍未解决的问题**：如何在不引入类型混淆或特殊语言规则的前提下，进一步简化无返回值 `Result` 的 `Ok(())` 写法。

messages.en:
Hi all, apologies if this has been discussed before.

The current convention for a value-less Result is to use a unit as in `Result<(), Error>`.

To me, this feels explicit, which is nice, but also like a bit of a missed opportunity.

What are feelings on a `Result<E>`type that behaves identically to the existing result type but is self documenting in its lack of a value?

https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=c5326c3d26aaff53618afd72de78f581

This is inspired by a C# result type I use, where `Result<T>` handles results with a value and a non-generic `Result ` handles results without a value. In this case, error types are anything that implements `IResultError`. On the Rust side, the closest equivalent would be like if the error type was defined on the variant and constrained by the `std::error::Error`trait and `Err()` accepted `dyn Error`

什么是感受`Result<E>`类型，其行为与现有结果类型相同，但由于缺少值而自我文档化？https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=c5326c3d26aaff53618afd72de78f581这是受我使用的C #结果类型的启发，其中`Result<T>`处理具有值和非泛型`Result `处理没有值的结果。在这种情况下，错误类型是任何实现`IResultError`。在Rust方面，最接近的等价物将是如果错误类型在变体上定义并受`std::error::Error`特质和`Err()`正取`dyn Error`

So if it's on something like a `String`, it returns `std::fmt::Result<()> = Result<(), std::fmt::Error>`

messages.en:
You can also do `type Result<T = (), E = MyError> = std::result::Result<T, E>;` which lets you use either plain `Result`, or `Result<SomeOkTy>`, or `Result<SomeOkTy, SomeErrTy>. I've occasionally done this for validators that just check things, and it's always nice not to need to re-quantify `std::result::Result` in the case that you need to specify parameters.

Doesn't save you from writing the extra `()` in `Ok(())` but I think that's something you'll quickly get used to. Can always `const OK: Result = Ok(())` if you really care

这并不能让您免于写下额外费用`()` 在 `Ok(())`但我认为这是你很快就会习惯的。总是可以`const OK: Result = Ok(())`如果你真的在乎

messages.en:
@**Saoirse** We only allow this equivalence:
```rust
fn do_something_explicit() -> () { }
fn do_something_implicit() { }
```
because the absence of a meaningful value of a return can be implied by the absence period. In this case you have a `Result::Ok`. What is the `Ok` wrapping?  Nothing important? That's fine, but that isn't implied, because `Result<T, E>` means *there can be anything there*. You entered a context, in the constructor of `Result`, where "what is it wrapping?" needed an answer. By adding a different `Result` with only one type parameter, we introduce a potential for significant confusion, especially when we have already made a single-parameter `Result`... with an already-specified `Err` variant.

Notably, you want us to allow these to be equal:
```rust
Enum::Variant(())
Enum::Variant()
```
Often, we like it when there is some symmetry between the constructors of enum variants and the constructors of structs, but this change could not be compatible with special-casing `Struct()` vs. `Struct(())` in an important way: if you do not have access to the private fields of `Struct`, and its single field is private, then you cannot construct `Struct(())` even if it is indeed always a unit constructor.
messages.zh:
@ * * Saoirse * *我们只允许以下等价物：```rust
fn do_something_explicit() -> () { }
fn do_something_implicit() { }
```因为缺席期间可以暗示缺少有意义的回报值。 在这种情况下，您有一个`Result::Ok`请告知`Ok`包装？没什么重要的？没关系，但这不是暗示的，因为`Result<T, E>`意味着*那里可以有任何东西*。您在的构造函数中输入了一个上下文`Result`，其中“包装什么？”需要一个答案。通过添加其他`Result`只有一个类型参数，我们会引入重大混淆的可能性，特别是当我们已经制定了单个参数时`Result`...具有已指定的`Err`变量。

值得注意的是，您希望我们允许这些条件相等：```rust
Enum::Variant(())
Enum::Variant()
```通常，我们喜欢枚举变体的构造函数和结构体的构造函数之间存在一些对称性，但这种更改不能与特殊情况兼容`Struct()`对比`Struct(())`以一种重要的方式：如果您无权访问的私有字段`Struct`，且其单个字段为私有字段，则无法构造`Struct(())`即使它确实始终是单元构造函数。

topics.name: opt-level 1
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论 `opt-level=1` 是否适合 CPU-heavy、浮点数或 SIMD 代码的开发场景。有人认为它常以约 30% 的编译时间换来测试负载显著提速，值得使用；也有人强调 `dev` 的首要目标应是尽可能快地构建，并保留最大调试能力。
- **关于优化级别**：多数参与者认为 `opt-level=1` 通常比 `opt-level=3` 编译快，且运行性能明显更好；但有人希望存在介于 `0` 和 `1` 之间、只启用最快且收益最高优化的级别。也有人提出类似 GCC/Clang `-Og` 的“优化调试”选项，但其具体语义尚未确定。
- **`opt-level=0` 的取舍**：讨论了将“最快编译”和“最佳调试能力”从 `opt-level=0` 中分离的可能性，例如区分 `0` 与某种 `debug` 配置；不过有人反对进一步削弱 `opt-level=0` 的运行性能，担心迫使更多项目改用编译更慢的 `opt-level=1`。`#[inline(always)]` 在 `opt-level=0` 是否应被忽略也存在分歧：忽略它可能改善编译速度和增量编译，但可能影响部分依赖内联的代码生成场景。
- **实现细节与限制**：`opt-level=1` 不运行 MIR inliner，这是通过特殊配置逻辑实现的；该做法是目前唯一显著区分 `-Copt-level=1` 与 `-Copt-level=2` 的 MIR 优化行为，并正在阻碍 `#[optimize]` 属性的清理式整合。另有人提出需要确认 `opt-level=1` 是否启用 thin local LTO。
- **后续方向**：Cargo 正在考虑将“快速迭代”和“调试”拆分为不同 profile，初步区分点计划是 `debug`；Cargo issue #17681 将收集确定 `dev` 的 `opt-level` 时所需的评估标准，包括应更重视编译时间，还是编译时间与执行时间的总和。 ચર્ચ论中尚未形成新的 `opt-level` 或 `-Og` 方案的最终结论。

messages.en:
So, it certainly sounds like opt-level=1 is doing its job, of being an optimization level that makes things noticeably faster without taking as much time as opt-level 2 or 3 to compile.

But that doesn't make it a good default for `dev`. `dev` should build as fast as possible. It should do any optimizations that *make the code faster to compile*, but it already does; opt-level 0 includes some MIR optimizations that are faster than not doing them, because they result in doing less work in compilation.
messages.zh:
因此，听起来 opt-level=1 确实正在发挥作用，作为一个优化级别，它可以使事情明显更快，而无需花费像 opt-level 2 或 3 那么多的时间来编译。

但这并不能使它成为一个很好的默认值`dev`。`dev`应该尽快构建。它应该做任何优化来*使代码编译速度更快*，但它已经这样做了； opt-level 0 包含一些比不执行更快的 MIR 优化，因为它们会减少编译工作。

messages.en: If people *want* to turn on optimizations on `dev`, they can. But our defaults should aim for fast builds.
messages.zh: 如果人们“想要”开启优化`dev`，他们可以。但我们的默认设置应该以快速构建为目标。

messages.en: opt-level=0 has a dual purpose of compiling as fast as possible and giving maximum debugging fidelity. When these are in conflict you have to pick one or the other. We may have some MIR passes right now that vary behavior based on debug info level but at least in LLVM it's explicit policy to not do that. Between that and "opt level < 0" looking silly, I think it's better to call the "compile as fast as possible at expense of debuggability" optimization level something different than "0" (assuming this level can realistically exist at all).
messages.zh: opt-level=0 有双重目的：尽可能快地编译并提供最大的调试保真度。当这些发生冲突时，你必须选择其中之一。我们现在可能有一些 MIR 通道，它们会根据调试信息级别改变行为，但至少在 LLVM 中，明确的策略是不这样做。在这和看起来很愚蠢的“opt level < 0”之间，我认为最好将“以牺牲可调试性为代价尽可能快地编译”优化级别称为与“0”不同的东西（假设这个级别实际上可以存在）。

messages.en: yeah, if build time were the only metric for `dev`, we would turn off debuginfo entirely
messages.zh: 是的，如果构建时间是唯一的衡量标准`dev`，我们将完全关闭 debuginfo

messages.en: The `dev` profile is caught between too many conflicting preferences, same with `release` because it enables *some* optimizations but we still have guidance all over the internet about "oh, do you really want good code? Apply these options instead of using the defaults"

@_**Josh Triplett|239881** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/opt-level.201/near/620377919):
```quote
So, it certainly sounds like opt-level=1 is doing its job, of being an optimization level that makes things noticeably faster without taking as much time as opt-level 2 or 3 to compile.

But that doesn't make it a good default for `dev`. `dev` should build as fast as possible. It should do any optimizations that *make the code faster to compile*, but it already does; opt-level 0 includes some MIR optimizations that are faster than not doing them, because they result in doing less work in compilation.
```

To be clear, I was not suggesting that we do anything to opt-level=0.

messages.en:
@_**Hanna Kruppe|124289** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/opt-level.201/near/620379492):
```quote
opt-level=0 has a dual purpose of compiling as fast as possible and giving maximum debugging fidelity. When these are in conflict you have to pick one or the other. We may have some MIR passes right now that vary behavior based on debug info level but at least in LLVM it's explicit policy to not do that. Between that and "opt level < 0" looking silly, I think it's better to call the "compile as fast as possible at expense of debuggability" optimization level something different than "0" (assuming this level can realistically exist at all).
```

I personally think that we should separate those two, yes. But one interesting question is whether we call them "0" and "fast" or "0" and "debug". I would personally favor the latter, and making 0 the fastest possible.

messages.en: It can make sense to inline a cold path if it’s sufficiently small and gives more information to the optimizer. That’s why we have `hint::cold_path()`, and an inlinable `#[cold]` call is basically the equivalent of that when it’s needed in multiple places and you don’t want to repeat the actual logic or the `hint::cold_path()` in each of those places.
messages.zh: 如果冷路径足够小，并且为优化器提供了更多信息，则内联冷路径是有意义的。这就是为什么我们有`hint::cold_path()`和一个内联的`#[cold]`调用基本上等同于在多个地方需要它，并且您不想重复实际的逻辑或`hint::cold_path()`在这些地方的每一个地方。

messages.en: so to be clear, I think that in most cases the chance to inline cold paths is fine, especially since it's unlikely to happen across crate boundaries, and if the main issue is code size with `panic!` calls, maybe we should have a separate way of tagging those than just always having `#[cold]#[inline(never)]`

topics.name: moving out of a pattern matching a dereferenced boxed slice
topics.name_zh: 移出与取消引用的盒装切片匹配的图案
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：对 `Box<[NonCopy]>` 解引用后使用切片模式匹配时，无法将非 `Copy` 元素移出，例如 `match *s { [v] => Some(v), _ => None }` 会触发 `E0508`；而类似操作对 boxed array 可以工作。
- **主要观点**：有人认为该能力符合直觉且没有明显的安全问题，但可能需要 RFC 和 lang 团队批准。讨论中还希望未来能支持直接对 `Vec` 进行类似匹配，不过这被认为是另一个更复杂的问题。
- **可能方案**：`&own` / owning references 以及模式中的 `ref own` 被认为可以解决从 owned place 获取子对象所有权的问题；也有人主张即使不依赖 owning references，直接匹配 owned `[T]` 也应支持该行为。
- **实现难点与限制**：固定长度的完整切片匹配相对直接；带 `..` 的 variadic slice patterns 可能需要在模式中处理 drop，或引入新的 drop tracking，使 drop flags 依赖切片长度，因此可以暂时禁止这类模式。
- **已有相关能力与结论**：其他 unsized 类型中，若字段本身是 sized，已经可以从 boxed 值中通过模式匹配移出该字段；总体上讨论者认为该功能值得实现，借用检查方面似乎不难，主要复杂点在 drop elaboration，但目前没有形成正式 RFC 或确定实现。

topics.name: compiler struggles with coinductive trait implementations
topics.name_zh: 编译器在coadductive trait实现方面苦苦挣扎
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`T2` 为 `B<T>` 提供实现，但其约束又要求 `T: T1<B<T>>`；而 `T1<I> for A` 需要 `I: T2`，形成 `B<A>: T2 → A: T1<B<A>> → B<A>: T2` 的循环。当前编译器报错：`overflow evaluating the requirement B<A>: T2`，即使启用 `next-solver=globally` 也无法通过。
- **重要观点**：从 coinduction 的角度看，这种循环理论上应可成立；但 Rust 中普通 trait 默认并不允许按 coinductive 方式处理。
- **现有方案**：在 nightly 上使用 rustc 内部属性，将这两个 trait 标记为 coinductive，可以成功编译；该方案依赖内部属性，不是稳定 Rust 的常规用法。
- **稳定 Rust 的限制**：目前稳定版允许声明为 coinductive 的 trait 主要是 auto trait；`TransmuteFrom` 也属于类似 auto trait 的特殊情况，其实现会针对类型对动态生成。
- **未解决问题**：聊天中没有给出稳定版或 `unsafe` 的替代方案，也没有明确说明 `next-solver` 未来是否会支持解决这类循环。

messages.en: If you mark the two traits as coinductive (requires a nightly and a rustc internal attribute) then it compiles https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=nightly&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=ed61dcc26db95a494b2958a2098ce3d5

topics.name: RFC for the (weak) linkage feature
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论为 Rust 增加更直接对应平台/LLVM 的 weak linkage 支持，尤其区分 ELF 中的 weak definition（弱定义/导出）与 `extern_weak` 对应的 weak import/reference（弱导入/引用）。现有实现主要面向内部用途，缺少清晰的规范，用户认为其行为不够明确、可靠。
- **RFC 方向与方案**：倾向将 weak linkage 与 `extern_weak` 拆成两个 RFC；weak linkage 作为面向 FFI/ABI 对齐的底层构件，按目标文件中的符号属性进行定义（例如 ELF 的 `STB_WEAK`），而更用户友好、跨平台的可选实现应由 EII（externally implementable items）承担。讨论还提出 weak import 可用隐式 `Option`、`WeakImport<T>` 或仅允许原始指针访问等方式改善现有 API。
- **安全性与约束**：多位参与者认为 `#[unsafe(weak)]` 应是 unsafe attribute，因为它可能改变最终链接到的函数或静态项；EII 与 `#[unsafe(weak)]` 同时用于一个 item 应报错。较强的建议是要求 weak item 使用显式 link name（`#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` 或 `#[unsafe(export_name = ...)]`），但是否允许 mangled 名称仍可作为稳定化阶段的未决问题。
- **链接与代码生成语义**：静态库中对象文件是否被拉入、链接顺序以及 CGU 划分，都可能导致强定义未覆盖弱定义；这主要由 linker 决定，且不同平台和 linker 的行为并不一致。weak item 还应阻止内联（LLVM 已对部分 linkage 类型如此处理，MIR inliner 是否需要额外保证仍需注意）；是否对同时使用 `#[inline]` 发出警告留作未决问题。
- **仍未解决的问题**：ELF、Mach-O、COFF/MinGW、WASM 等平台的等价语义和 linker 差异尚需明确，Apple 的 weak 支持本身也存在不确定性；需要规定同名 weak import 与 strong export 等属性冲突时的优先级，以及静态/动态链接中符号缺失时的行为。RFC 草案仍在完善，weak aliases 被认为应作为未来可能性，而不应纳入当前 weak linkage RFC。

In [this comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/29603#issuecomment-1067621147), a caveat is mentioned to how weak linkage works:
> If there's a strong definition it wins (except sometimes it doesn't because static library semantics are weird)

It'd probably be worthwhile to figure out these semantics, whether they need to be emulated, and then document them accordingly in the RFC.
If anyone knows the details about those semantics, please let me know :purple_heart:
```

An object file inside an archive file is only included in the link if there is a missing symbol with that name earlier in the linkage order (the order of the list of libraries on the command line).

That means a weak definition can win if, for example:
- the strong definition is *early* on the command line, *inside an archive*, and in an object file *without* any symbols that are required by an earlier linked object file (so it *doesn't* get linked)
- the weak definition is *later* on the command line, and *is linked*, either because it is:
  - *inside an archive*, in an object file *with* one or more symbols that are required by an earlier linked object file
  - in an object file (with no archive), so the object file is guaranteed to be linked

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51656838/attribute-weak-and-static-libraries/51970423#51970423

```只有当链接顺序（命令行上库列表的顺序）中缺少具有该名称的符号时，存档文件中的对象文件才会包含在链接中。

这意味着弱定义可以获胜，例如：-强定义是*早期*在命令行上， *在存档中* ，并且在对象文件中*没有*任何早期链接的对象文件所需的符号（因此它*不会*链接）

  - *在存档中* ，在对象文件中*具有*早期链接的对象文件所需的一个或多个符号-在对象文件中（没有存档） ，因此对象文件保证链接https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51656838/attribute-weak-and-static-libraries/51970423#51970423

messages.en: This might seem like weird semantics, but it allows linkers to do a single ordered linking pass, skip object files in libraries which aren't needed (or entire libraries that aren't needed), and avoids any kind of topological dependency sorting. (Which was important when memory and CPU was scarce.)
messages.zh: 这可能看起来很奇怪，但它允许链接器执行单个有序链接传递，跳过不需要的库中的对象文件（或不需要的整个库） ，并避免任何类型的拓扑依赖排序。（当内存和CPU稀缺时，这一点很重要。）

> If you wish to override the standard library malloc family of functions and have automatic initialization/finalization of process and threads, define __ENABLE_OVERRIDE__ to non-zero (default is 1) which will include the `malloc.c` file in compilation of __rpmalloc.c__, and then rebuild the library or your project where you added the rpmalloc source. If you compile rpmalloc as a separate static library and use only the overridden libc entry points (you call plain `malloc`/`free` but never any `rp*` function directly), the linker may not pull the rpmalloc object out of the archive, and the overrides will silently not take effect. To force its inclusion you must reference at least one symbol from the library: the easiest way is to include `rpmalloc.h` in at least one source file and call `rpmalloc_linker_reference` somewhere - it's a dummy empty function provided for exactly this purpose. This is not needed if you call `rpmalloc`/`rpfree` (or any other `rp*` function) directly, link the dynamic library, or use `LD_PRELOAD`/`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`. For C++ operator overrides the behaviour is platform specific. On Windows you must `#include <rpnew.h>` in exactly one source file (it defines the `new`/`delete` operators with external linkage and has no include guard, so including it in more than one translation unit causes duplicate symbol errors). On other platforms the `new`/`delete` operators are overridden automatically by the library - do not include `rpnew.h` there, as it will conflict with the operators already provided. The list of libc entry points replaced may not be complete, use libc/stdc++ replacement only as a convenience for testing the library on an existing code base, not a final solution.

messages.en:
# Semantics when symbol doesn't exist

On platforms that support it, an external symbol of type T and the name of the static item is created. If the symbol isn't present at link time or run time, no error is generated. If the program has loaded a dynamic library that defines the symbol, as_ref returns a reference to the symbol, otherwise it returns None. If the platform doesn't support this, a compile-time error is generated.

I think this is the behavior that people actually want, and is supported on Linux, OSX, and Windows. Getting it to work this way requires providing some flags to the linker (`-U foo` on OSX and [`/ALTERNATENAME:foo=null_foo`](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20200731-00/?p=104024) on Windows), and it would be much easier and less error-prone for the compiler to do this than the programmer.

## PE / COFF (Windows)

Windows [doesn't support weakly linked symbols at load-time](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20160317-00/?p=93173), the recommended alternative is to use [runtime dynamic linking](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dlls/run-time-dynamic-linking). So we'd direct users to [the `libloading` crate](https://docs.rs/libloading/latest/libloading/) or similar instead.

## Mach-O (macOS/iOS/tvOS/watchOS/visionOS)

`dyld`.

We _could_ get around this by passing `-U my_symbol` to the linker, but that's bad for performance, and especially startup time.

If the user wants to use `#[weak]` with arbitary symbols on macOS, they either need to:
1. Tell `rustc` to pass `-U` as a linker flag (if you don't know where the symbol will come from).
    - Using a build script:
        ```rust
        // build.rs
        if std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_VENDOR").unwrap() == "apple" {
            print!("cargo::rustc-link-arg=-Wl,-U,my_symbol");
        }
        ```
    - After https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/99427, doing it inline:
        ```rust
        #[cfg_attr(
            target_vendor = "apple",
            link(kind = "link-arg", name = "-U"),
            link(kind = "link-arg", name = "my_symbol"),
        )]
        unsafe extern "C" {
            // ...
        }
        ```
2. Create a `.tdb` file, and link against that (if you know where the symbol will come from, but just don't have that library available).

In any case, we should provide clear guidance for this in the docs.

Docs:
- https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPFrameworks/Concepts/WeakLinking.html
- https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/DeveloperTools/Conceptual/DynamicLibraries/100-Articles/DynamicLibraryUsageGuidelines.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40001928-SW20
messages.zh:
#符号不存在时的语义

在支持它的平台上，将创建类型为T的外部符号和静态项的名称。 如果符号在链接时或运行时不存在，则不会生成错误。 如果程序加载了定义符号的动态库， as_ref返回对符号的引用，否则返回None。 如果平台不支持此操作，则会生成编译时错误。我认为这是人们真正想要的行为，并且在Linux、OSX和Windows上受到支持。要使其以这种方式工作，需要向链接器提供一些标记（`-U foo`在OSX和[`/ALTERNATENAME:foo=null_foo`](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20200731-00/?p=104024)） ，编译器比程序员更容易、更不容易出错。

# #精灵

?

# # PE/COFF （ Windows ）

Windows [加载时不支持弱链接符号] （https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20160317-00/?p=93173),推荐的替代方案是使用[运行时动态链接] （https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dlls/run-time-dynamic-linking).因此，我们将用户引导到[`libloading`制作https://docs.rs/libloading/latest/libloading/)或类似的东西。

某种程度上？https://maskray.me/blog/2021-04-25-weak-symbol
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/debug/pe-format#auxiliary-format-3-weak-externalsWasmhttps://github.com/WebAssembly/tool-conventions/blob/main/DynamicLinking.md# # Mach-O （ macOS/iOS/tvOS/watchOS/visionOS ）`dyld`.

我们_可以_通过传递来解决这个问题`-U my_symbol`链接器，但这不利于性能，尤其是启动时间。

如果用户想使用`#[weak]`在macOS上使用任意符号，他们需要：
1.告诉`rustc`及格线`-U`作为链接器标志（如果您不知道符号将来自何处）。
    -使用构建脚本：```rust
        // build.rs
        if std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_VENDOR").unwrap() == "apple" {
            print!("cargo::rustc-link-arg=-Wl,-U,my_symbol");
        }
        ```突破后属性https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/99427,内联执行此操作：```rust
        #[cfg_attr(
            target_vendor = "apple",
            link(kind = "link-arg", name = "-U"),
            link(kind = "link-arg", name = "my_symbol"),
        )]
        unsafe extern "C" {
            // ...
        }
        ```2.创建`.tdb`文件，并针对此链接（如果您知道符号将来自何处，但没有该库可用）。

无论如何，我们都应在文件中提供明确的指导。

messages.en:
Another piece of motivation is "Higher performance than `dlsym`".

I also think it's useful to mention use-cases explicitly in the RFC, exactly because the term "weak linkage" is ill defined. A few that I've collected:
- Importing symbols added in newer versions of a library/OS (such as currently done by `std`).
- Allowing the user to optionally provide a symbol elsewhere (EII).
- Allowing multiple definitions of a symbol.
messages.zh:
另一个动机是“更高的性能比`dlsym`".

我还认为在RFC中明确提及用例是有用的，因为术语“弱链接”的定义不正确。 我收集了一些：
-导入库/操作系统较新版本中添加的符号（例如当前由`std`).
-允许用户选择性地在其他地方提供符号（ EII ）。
-允许对符号进行多个定义。

topics.name: I snuck into the Rust Foundation's secret meeting
topics.name_zh: 我溜进了Rust基金会的秘密会议
topics.summary:
- **会议背景与核心认识**：所谓“秘密会议”实际是 Rust Foundation 在罗马举行的为期 5 天的全体员工线下聚会，目的是让远程团队在没有外部活动压力的情况下集中交流。参会者仅 13 人，且不少人同时承担 Foundation 员工与 Rust Project 成员等多重角色。
- **Foundation 与 Rust Project 的关系**：虽然 Foundation 是承担法律、资金、基础设施和雇佣责任的独立实体，但其员工与 Project 成员联系紧密，实际工作中与 Project 的其他团队有相似之处。Foundation 的工作既包括支撑 Project 的“外部支柱”，也有部分工作逐渐被纳入 Project 内部。
- **重要观点与案例**：Rust 社区应继续设法将 Foundation 支持的工作纳入 Project；无法纳入时，也应让相关人员感到被 Project 接纳，并方便 Project 成员与其协作。Jess 最近推动的 **t-security** 工作被视为将 Foundation 外部工作带入 Project 内部的例子。
- **讨论重点与未解决问题**：会议大量讨论了 Foundation 过去的工作方式，哪些经验应保留、哪些应改变，以及不同团队之间能否借鉴彼此的成功或失败。由于各团队面临的问题、历史和约束不同，具体哪些做法最适合 Foundation 仍需继续判断，记录中未给出明确的统一方案。

messages.en:
OK, the title is clickbait. The meeting in question was the week (5 day) long staff in person get together and off site in Rome. Like many remote teams the foundation staff mostly see each other in small groups when they happened to be at (or running) high pressure public events. This trip is the exception, when everyone tries to get together without the pressure of external involvement.

Sneaking in is also an exaggeration. I was invited, if at the last minute. The meeting is intended for "staff". Given that I'm working as a contractor for the foundation, but full time, but on a temporary grant, that we're trying to renew. A truly Talmudic Tractate could be written about whether I qualify as "staff". It seems like the deciding factor was that they wanted to hear from my unique perspective. Or, at least, I hope they wanted to hear my opinion because while I have the right to remain silent I do not have the ability.

I am in no way an unbiased observer of this meeting. For the past handful of months I work full time for the Foundation. If the grants come through I hope this work will continue. Which is a real bias, but pales in comparison to my relationship with the project. I have been using Rust and following its development since 2015. I have officially been in the project since 2018. This project and community is a big part of my identity. I plan to still stay involved with the project whenever my time at the foundation ends. By the sheer stubbornness of staying involved I have somehow managed to become one of the "old timers". So I went into this meeting "wearing multiple hats", which was a big part of why I was invited.

The Foundation looms large in the formal structures of how this "Rust" works. All the donations, both in kind and financial, are technically made to the Foundation. This zulip, the CI that runs our tests, the servers that host our releases In docs.rs and [crates.io](http://crates.io/) and so much more. So the first surprise of this meeting was **how small a group we were**. There were 13 of us. That is it. It is a small crue.

The next surprise was that most of us wore multiple hats. For example, half of us where already Project Members. (Several more were on track to be added soon.) Several had more and more complicated hats to juggle. Going into this meeting, there were several people where intellectually I knew they work on Team X and for the Foundation, but deep down inside I had compartmentalize that slack and that zulip/github identities as separate entities. No, just a person sitting across the room from me. All of us had a deep well of past experiences and contacts that we pulled from to provide interesting perspectives on the problems we were discussing. The Foundation may feel "Other" from the project, but in practice every Foundation employee is 2 (at most 3) degrees of separation from any Project member. In that respect they're not so different from any other team in the project.

Some of us in the meetings this week are pillars of the project, critical to holding the project up from the inside. The others are flying buttresses, just as critical to holding up the project but doing so from the outside. (Playing with Churchill's famous Metaphor.) You may not know the work each of these people put in to keep Rust a going concern -- before this week I certainly didn't -- but we are all reliant on this work getting done. Sometimes the load on the building shifts In such a way That the support is no longer critical and by moving load to other parts of the structure the support can be removed without damage. (My civil engineering degree is showing and how much I'm torturing this metaphor.) The stress and deformation caused by recent removals were clear overtones to many of the conversations this week. Other times, when you look at an old building, and there were many in Rome, the way spaces get used changes overtime. A fence makes an outside space into a courtyard. A roof makes a courtyard into a room. And before you know it an outside support is now inside. Jess' recent efforts on t-security is a great example of taking work that the Foundation (Walter and I) was doing outside the Project and bring it inside. The Rust community should continue to find ways to enclose the work done by these flying buttresses. And where that's not possible, the Rust community should find other ways to make them feel welcomed by and available to the project members.

Every team in the project has ways that it works that are slightly different from how everyone else works. These differences are brought on by idiosyncrasies of the existentially important problems that team is in charge of fixing. Mixed with path dependant history of how they've done things in the past. Lots are legacies of good decisions made in the past, some are legacies of bad decisions that were made, more are from decisions that were the best decision that could be made at the time but no longer serving its purpose. The interconnectedness of the the Teams that make up the Project give us opportunities to learn from others mistakes. Both of the form "Team Y tryed X, and it went so badly that we should not try X" and "I know we  tried X and it did not work, but Team Y has made it work so maybe we should try it again". (Yes, categorically those are opposite recommendations. Even with all the data it is hard to know what is best to do.) A lot of the Foundation's meetings this week were dedicated to figuring out what lessons to learn. Which of the ways the Foundation did things in the past worked and which ones we should try changing. A history of mistakes, A unique set of pressures and responsibilities, A constant drive to figure out how to do better, in these aspects they are like every other Team in the Project.

I went into this week well aware of the important ways The Foundation must be different from The Project. The Foundation is a legal entity with the privileges and responsibilities to come with that. It's staff are paid and therefore can be fired. It's responsible to the Board of Directors and The Project Directors. (It uses slack :-P) Ect. I came out of the week much more aware of the ways it's just like any other part of the Project.
messages.zh:
好的，标题是点击诱饵。 这次会议是为期一周（ 5天）的工作人员在罗马亲自聚会并离开现场。 与许多远程团队一样，当基金会工作人员碰巧参加（或举办）高压公共活动时，他们大多会以小组的形式见面。 这次旅行是个例外，每个人都试图在没有外部参与的压力下聚在一起。

偷偷溜进来也是一种夸张。我被邀请了，如果是在最后一刻。会议面向“员工”。鉴于我是基金会的承包商，但全职，但临时补助金，我们正在尝试续签。一个真正的《塔木德学报》可以写出我是否有资格成为“员工”。看来，决定性因素是他们想从我独特的角度听到。或者，至少我希望他们想听听我的意见，因为虽然我有权保持沉默，但我没有能力。

我绝不是本次会议的公正观察者。 在过去的几个月里，我全职为基金会工作。 如果补助金通过，我希望这项工作能够继续下去。 这是一种真正的偏见，但与我与项目的关系相比却相形见绌。自2015年以来，我一直在使用Rust并关注其开发。我自2018年以来一直正式参与该项目。这个项目和社区是我身份的重要组成部分。每当我在基金会的时间结束时，我都计划继续参与该项目。由于我顽固地参与其中，我以某种方式成为了“老计时器”之一。所以我“戴着多顶帽子”参加了这个会议，这也是我被邀请的重要原因。

基金会在“Rust”工作方式的正式结构中占有重要地位。 所有捐赠，无论是实物还是资金，在技术上都是向基金会提供的。 这个zulip ，运行我们测试的CI ，在docs.rs和[cates.io]中托管我们版本的服务器（http://crates.io/)还有更多。 因此，这次会议的第一个惊喜是* *我们的团队规模有多小* *。 我们有13个人。 就是这样，这是一个小小的残酷。

接下来的惊喜是，我们大多数人都戴着多顶帽子。 例如，我们一半的人已经是项目成员。 （还有几个正在按计划进行，很快就会添加。） 有几个人戴着越来越复杂的帽子。参加这次会议时，有几个人在理智上我知道他们在X团队和基金会工作，但在内心深处，我将这种松弛和zulip/github身份划分为独立的实体。不，只有一个人坐在我对面。我们所有人都有深厚的过去经历和接触，我们从中汲取经验，为我们讨论的问题提供有趣的视角。基金会可能会从项目中感受到“其他” ，但在实践中，每个基金会员工与任何项目成员都有2个（最多3个）分离度。 在这方面，他们与项目中的任何其他团队没有太大不同。

参加本周会议的一些人是项目的支柱，对从内部支撑项目至关重要。其他人正在飞翔的支柱，这对阻碍项目同样重要，但却是从外部进行的。（玩弄丘吉尔著名的比喻。）您可能不知道这些人为保持Rust的持续经营而投入的工作-在本周之前，我当然不知道-但我们都依赖于这项工作的完成。有时，建筑物上的载荷会以支撑不再是关键的方式移动，并且通过将载荷移动到结构的其他部分，可以在不受损的情况下移除支撑。（我的土木工程学位正在显示，我在多大程度上折磨着这个比喻。）最近的移除造成的应力和变形是本周许多对话的明显暗示。其他时候，当你看到一座古老的建筑时，罗马有很多，空间的使用方式会随着时间的推移而改变。围栏将室外空间变成了庭院。屋顶使庭院变成了一个房间。在你知道之前，现在有一个外部支持在里面。Jess最近在t-security方面的努力就是一个很好的例子，它将基金会（ Walter和我）在项目之外所做的工作带到了项目内部。Rust社区应该继续寻找方法来封闭这些飞行支柱所做的工作。 如果无法做到这一点， Rust社区应寻找其他方式，让他们感到受到项目成员的欢迎，并可供项目成员使用。

项目中的每个团队的工作方式都与其他人的工作方式略有不同。这些差异是由团队负责解决的存在性重要问题的特质引起的。与他们过去如何做事的路径相关历史记录混杂在一起。许多是过去做出的良好决策的遗产，有些是做出的错误决策的遗产，更多是来自当时可能做出的最佳决策，但不再符合其目的的决策。组成项目的团队之间的相互联系使我们有机会从他人的错误中吸取教训。“Y团队尝试了X ，结果非常糟糕，我们不应该尝试X”和“我知道我们尝试了X ，但它不起作用，但Y团队已经成功了，所以也许我们应该再试一次”。（是的，这些绝对是相反的建议。即使有了所有的数据，也很难知道什么是最好的。）本周基金会的很多会议都致力于找出可以吸取的教训。 基金会过去的工作方式有哪些，我们应该尝试改变哪些。 错误的历史，一组独特的压力和责任，不断努力找出如何在这些方面做得更好，他们与项目中的其他团队一样。本周，我充分意识到基金会必须与项目不同的重要方式。基金会是一个法律实体，拥有相应的特权和责任。它的员工是有报酬的，因此可以被解雇。它对董事会和项目总监负责。（它使用slack: -P ）等。一周后，我对项目的其他部分有了更多的了解。

topics.name: `crabi` generics
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论如何让 `crabi` 支持泛型且避免单态化（monomorphization）。提议在调用约定中为每个类型参数传递一个 type object，其中保存 trait bounds 各方法（包括静态方法和非静态方法）的函数指针；但这可能要求编译器修改许多默认依赖单态化的部分。
- **重要观点**：Fon 指出，这种方案严格来说更接近多态（polymorphism），而不是传统意义上的泛型；使用多态替代单态化的讨论已经持续了一段时间，Swift 似乎已经实现了类似机制。Hanna Kruppe 分享了 Swift ABI 相关资料。
- **相关工作**：Noah Lev 表示，其正在进行的 polymorphization 项目与该思路基本相符。目前主要目标是优化编译时间和二进制大小，也考虑将其用于提供稳定 ABI 或实现“重新链接而无需重新构建”（relink-don’t-rebuild）。
- **当前进展与未解决问题**：Noah Lev 的项目仍处于设计和初始 proof of concept 阶段；如何在 `crabi` 中具体实现非单态化泛型、需要对编译器进行哪些调整，以及该方案的完整可行性，讨论中尚未解决。

messages.en: I'm curious how much this has been thought about, but I have an idea for supporting generics with `crabi` without monomorphizing (at least, it would in theory work, though likely a lot of stuff in the compiler would have to be changed to not assume monomorphiziation). The idea is pretty much just a sort of type-object be passed for each type parameter as part of the call convention. Then the type-object would store function pointers for each of the methods of the trait bounds (static or not). I'm probably missing something, but I'm curious what that is. I also have a feeling that `crabi` hasn't been very actively discussed based on, well, the lack of activity in the github issue as well as not a ton of discussion on zulip.

topics.name: ✔ Understanding stacked borrow-based deallocation MIRI re...
topics.name_zh: ✔ 了解基于堆叠借款的解除分配MIRI re...
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：Miri 在 `dealloc(backing_ptr, layout)` 处报告“deallocating while item … is strongly protected”。原因是 `CoverageMap` 中保存了指向该分配的 `&mut [u8]`（甚至是 `&'static mut [u8]`）；即使显式 `drop` 该引用，引用本身的生命周期和保护仍覆盖整个函数调用，因此不能在函数内释放其底层内存。
- **重要观点**：函数参数中的引用必须在整个函数体期间保持有效，这与 LLVM 对引用的 `dereferenceable` 等语义保证有关；该限制不仅适用于 `&mut`，不可变引用也会阻止底层分配被释放。引用字段在传递结构体时会被 retag，Miri 默认执行字段 retagging。
- **解决方案**：不要在 `CoverageMap` 中保存 `&mut [u8]`，而是保存原始指针，仅在实际需要访问时临时创建引用，并使用原始指针进行释放。讨论中还提醒不要假设 `Deref::deref` 每次都返回同一个引用。
- **已达成结论**：将 `CoverageMap` 改为使用原始指针后问题已解决，话题由提问者标记为 resolved。提问者也表示需要进一步学习 Rust 内存模型；讨论推荐了 Stacked Borrows、Tree Borrows 相关资料。
- **仍未解决的问题**：Miri 的该诊断在 Stacked Borrows 下没有指出 protector 的创建位置；该信息在访问诊断中存在，但在释放诊断中缺失，已有人提出 `miri#5411` 以改进这一点。

messages.en:
I use miri to check some of my code when doing particularly unsafe things. MIRI currently complains about a [pointer deallocation](https://codeberg.org/addisoncrump/libfuzzer-ng/src/branch/main/benchmarks/src/coverage_map.rs#L96) with the following message:
```
test coverage_map::test::test_benchmarks ... error: Undefined Behavior: deallocating while item [Unique for <138816>] is strongly protected
  --> benchmarks/src/coverage_map.rs:96:14
   |
96 |     unsafe { dealloc(backing_ptr, layout) };
   |              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Undefined Behavior occurred here
   |
   = help: this indicates a potential bug in the program: it performed an invalid operation, but the Stacked Borrows rules it violated are still experimental
```

However, I'm quite certain there are no longer any remaining references to this value. I [create a slice from this pointer earlier](https://codeberg.org/addisoncrump/libfuzzer-ng/src/branch/main/benchmarks/src/coverage_map.rs#L74-L76) and make sure to [drop any references to it before deallocating](https://codeberg.org/addisoncrump/libfuzzer-ng/src/branch/main/benchmarks/src/coverage_map.rs#L95). Am I missing something, or is this output a false positive?

topics.name: ✔ Deferred statements
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论是否应在 Rust 中加入类似 Go 或 Zig 的 `defer` 语句，使传入的值被保存，并在当前作用域结束时执行；提议者认为现有通过带析构函数的类型实现的方式不够直观。
- **重要观点**：Ben Kimock 认为该功能目前可以通过库实现，因此不一定需要语言层面的特性；他还认为提议的行为与闭包捕获没有明显区别。
- **现有方案**：Jules Bertholet 提到即将稳定的 `std::mem::DropGuard`，可用于实现类似的作用域结束清理逻辑。
- **结论**：提议者得知 `DropGuard` 即将稳定后表示感谢，并将话题标记为已解决。

messages.en:
Has there been any past discussion about adding `defer`red statements, like what Go or Zig have? The syntax might look similar to:
```
defer do_something();
```
(ignore this specific syntax, bikeshedding can happen at a different time)
Then what it would actually mean is that the values passed would be saved and the statement would evaluate at the end of the current scope. Probably lifetime-wise, the values passed have to live for the entire scope, and an assignment or similar would be disallowed.

I can't immediately find an open or closed RFC about this, so I'm curious. Also, I am aware this restriction can technically be worked around by creating a new type with a destructor and assigning it to a variable, but that isn't very clear and is an annoying workaround.
messages.zh:
过去是否曾讨论过添加`defer`红色语句，比如Go或Zig有什么？ 语法可能类似于：```
defer do_something();
```（忽略此特定语法，自行车挂牌可能会在不同时间发生）
那么它实际上意味着传递的值将被保存，并且语句将在当前作用域结束时进行评估。 可能从整个生命周期来看，传递的值必须适用于整个范围，并且不允许分配或类似的值。

我无法立即找到打开或关闭的RFC ，因此我很好奇。此外，我知道这个限制在技术上可以通过使用析构函数创建一个新类型并将其分配给变量来解决，但这不是很清楚，而且是一个恼人的解决方法。

topics.name: Random question: is there any plan on introducing restrict
topics.name_zh: 随机问题：是否有任何引入限制的计划
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：Rust 目前似乎没有引入类似 C `restrict` 的机制，用于对 raw pointers 表达 no-aliasing 保证；提问者希望在不能使用 references（例如指针可能未对齐）时，仍能把“不重叠”信息传递给 optimizer。

- **现有方案与讨论**：
  - 可以通过 `&mut`、nightly 的 `unsafe<'a> &'a Foo`，或封装并隐藏 reference 的 `NoAliasConstPtr<T>` 等方式，获得接近 `restrict` 的效果，但 references 还带有生命周期、validity、reborrowing 等额外要求。
  - 有人提到 Clang 的 `__builtin_assume_separate_storage`，但它保证的是指针属于完全分离的 allocation，强于一般的 non-overlapping；也有人建议用 intrinsic 表达较弱的约束，不过具体语义仍需明确。
  - 在 Tree Borrows（TB）模型下，现有 `&mut` 方案可以接近 `restrict`，但仍可能比 C `restrict` 更强；例如函数体内释放 restrict pointer，或返回经过 `&mut` 派生的指针，都可能产生额外限制。

- **重要分歧**：讨论者认为“这些 raw pointers 不 alias”容易描述，但要将其形式化为与 Rust aliasing model、provenance 和 optimizer 一致且可用的语义很困难。约束必须明确作用范围、指针有效期、原始指针何时可再次使用等，否则可能导致过强、过弱或难以实现的规则。

- **具体用例**：提问者提出 in-place buffer transformation：函数在调用期间利用 no-alias 保证优化，并返回输入指针；C `restrict` 允许调用结束后通过原始指针和返回指针交替访问，而若 Rust 通过 `&mut` 派生返回指针，Tree Borrows 可能留下 lingering restrictions。保留并返回原始指针可以绕开这一问题，但这说明 call-scoped noalias 可能有价值。

- **结论与未解决问题**：聊天中没有形成引入 `restrict`、新 pointer type 或 intrinsic 的计划或共识。是否确实存在 `&mut` 无法覆盖且需要更灵活 no-alias 机制的实际场景，以及如何定义 sound、可优化、不会过度限制用户的语义，仍未解决。

```
````

FWIW, neither of those seem practical to me at first glance. The first seems to have complicated exceptions that LLVM can’t understand (“valid for reads” is a Rust-type concept, so you have to understand Rust validity to know what those ranges are) so LLVM wouldn’t be able to do anything with it. The second is under-specified but probably too strong because it talks about the indeterminate future and that kind of thing tends to leak into the past (via desirable optimizations) and outside the code region you want to make statements about (because there’s no clear end point). Generally you have to more carefully express such things as “create new pointers with restricted provenance for some time, and either invalidate them when the original pointers are used again, or prevent use of the original pointers until some obvious end marker” and at that point you’re back in the deepest parts of the aliasing model mines (as well as probably needing expensive dominance checks in alias analysis).

indeed, that is one such case. The other is when you return the restrict pointer from the function: since it is a reference, it "leaves behind" lingering restrictions
