Would an in place buffer transformation that returns its input pointer be a concrete example of this?

With restrict, the function could optimize under the aliasing guarantee during the call, but afterwards the caller could freely alternate accesses through the original pointer and the returned pointer.

If the returned pointer were derived from an &mut used inside the function, writing through the original pointer could invalidate it under Tree Borrows, right?

topics.name: Documentation on Features
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：目前 crate feature 无法直接附加文档；docs.rs 的 features 页面也不会显示 crate-level 文档中的相关说明。讨论者还希望按 feature 列出所有被 `#[cfg]` 条件编译的 items。
- **方案与语法**：RFC 3485 提议在 `Cargo.toml` 的 `[features]` 中为 feature 添加元数据，例如 `x = { enables = [...], doc = "..." }`，或使用 `[features.x]`；其中 `x = ["reqwest"]` 可作为简写。该方案比通过注释扩展 TOML 更明确、更具未来兼容性。
- **TOML 兼容性争议**：有人提议利用注释保存 feature 文档，但反对者指出 TOML 注释不具语义含义，通用 TOML 解析器通常会丢弃注释；这样会形成需要 Cargo 特殊逻辑处理的 TOML 方言。
- **已达成的进展**：feature 文档方案已有 RFC 3485 和 Cargo tracking issue（#17445），并且已经在 Cargo 侧实现，当前作为 nightly feature 提供。
- **展示位置计划**：计划由 `rustdoc` 自身渲染 feature 文档，可能提供专门的 feature 页面；在此之前，docs.rs 可能作为中间方案扩展现有 features 页面。已有 Rust PR 尝试实现相关功能，但 UI 部分是否完成尚不确定。
- **仍未解决的问题**：Cargo 如何将 feature 文档信息提供给 `rustdoc`、最终 UI 具体呈现方式，以及是否、如何在 features 页面展示每个 feature 对应的 `#[cfg]` items，仍未完全确定。

messages.en: My understanding is that there is no way to add documentation to a crate feature.  Of course you can put it in the crate-level documentation, and many crates do, but if you are looking at the actual features page on docs.rs, this documentation won't be there.  I think it would improve the user experience of looking at features if the feature documentation could actually be associated with the features themselves, rather than just floating in the crate documentarjon.  This would also simplify and incentivise documenting crate features.
messages.zh: 我的理解是，无法将文档添加到Crate功能中。当然，您可以将其放在crate-level文档中，许多crate都可以，但如果您正在查看docs.rs上的实际功能页面，则不会有此文档。我认为，如果功能文档实际上可以与功能本身相关联，而不仅仅是漂浮在crate documentarjon中，这将改善查看功能的用户体验。这也将简化和激励记录板条箱功能。

messages.en: The toml spec says that comments don't have Semantic meaning. If we pick that kind of API would mean that parsing cargo.toml with a generic toml parser would no longer be able to find all of the important information.
messages.zh: Toml规范表示注释没有语义含义。如果我们选择这种API ，将意味着使用通用toml解析器解析cargo.toml将不再能够找到所有重要信息。

messages.zh: 但同样，这意味着我们的`toml`成为一种定制的rust-toml方言，通常与兼容的toml解析器不兼容。

messages.en: Yes, cargo can definitely be augmented to read toml+comments. After several years work, our current TOML crate preserves comments, so we have the ability to parse them. But making our language a superset of TOML means that someone who wants to parse it in Python can't use a normal TOML lib to get all the information, but needs one with special logic to read our format. All choices have consequences. This is one of the consequences of that API.
messages.zh: 是的，货物绝对可以增加阅读toml +注释。经过几年的工作，我们目前的TOML Crate保留了评论，因此我们能够解析它们。但是，使我们的语言成为TOML的超集意味着想要在Python中解析它的人无法使用普通的TOML库来获取所有信息，而是需要一个具有特殊逻辑的TOML库来读取我们的格式。所有的选择都会产生后果。这是该API的后果之一。

topics.name: Help needed to fix ancient async lowering soundness issue
topics.name_zh: 需要帮助来解决古代异步降低声音的问题
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：Issue #63818 是一个长期存在的 async/await lowering soundness 问题。虽然已通过实现 `UnsafePinned`（#125735）取得进展，但 coroutine lowering 仍未使用它；现有草案 PR #139896 长期无人维护，后续认为该任务已开放给其他人接手。
- **分析与实现方向**：BN 认为不需要 #139896 中新增的分析 pass，已有的 `MaybeBorrowedLocals` 足以识别跨 suspension point 存活的借用及 self-referential locals。#152946 被视为较新的实现方向，BN 一度计划继续推进，之后 Zoxc 表示可以接手。
- **主要性能与递归限制担忧**：将字段包装为 `UnsafePinned<MaybeUninit<T>>` 会增加类型嵌套层数，可能加剧 #152942 的性能问题并触发 `recursion_limit`。讨论过让特定包装层不计入递归限制，或引入类似 `SelfReferentialCoroutineField` 的专用 core 类型；也有人建议暂时观察实际问题，RalfJ 倾向于后者延后处理。近期 async 嵌套有所减少，可能释放部分预算。
- **`UnsafePinned` 与 coroutine 语义**：RalfJ 解释 `UnsafePinned` 类似针对 `&mut` 的 `UnsafeCell`，用于允许可安全表达的 aliased mutable references；pinning 是 library-level 机制，而 `UnsafePinned` 是 language-level 支持。Zoxc 提议使用单独的部分唯一类型，但 RalfJ 指出 LLVM 的 `noalias` 不能表达“部分”范围，且该类型的安全用途并不明确。
- **当前进展与未解决问题**：RalfJ 后续提出让整个 coroutine 直接表现为 `UnsafePinned + UnsafeCell`，作为较简单的起点，并创建了不完整的 PR #165300；仍需让 trait system 正确处理 coroutine 不实现 `Freeze` 和 `UnsafePinned`，并确认所有 `UnsafeCell` 特殊处理（如 variance、invariance）都覆盖到。讨论还涉及 Miri、LLVM 优化精度以及错误信息影响，但尚未形成完整解决方案。

messages.en: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/63818 is a soundness issue that has been open for many years, but recently we started making progress towards solving it by implementing `UnsafePinned` (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/125735). However, what's still missing is actually adjusting the async/await lowering to use `UnsafePinned`. Do we have anyone left who actually understands that lowering and would they be willing to try and finally fix this old problem? :)
messages.zh: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/63818是一个多年来一直存在的健全问题，但最近我们开始通过实施`UnsafePinned` (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/125735).但是，仍然缺少的是实际上调整异步/等待降级以使用`UnsafePinned`.我们还有人真正理解降价吗？他们是否愿意尝试并最终解决这个旧问题？:)

messages.en:
@_**Zoxc|116466** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Help.20needed.20to.20fix.20ancient.20async.20lowering.20soundness.20issue/near/593783914):
```quote
So #152946 is the latest PR here? #139896 seems to add an analysis pass #152946 doesn't have.
```

It's been some time since I looked at https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/139896 in detail, but the analysis in that PR doesn't seem to be necessary (it also seemed flawed as they [ran a pass](https://github.com/Sky9x/rust/blob/3e1cce772d118dbb22f2e32bf97445fce1d1fb74/compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine.rs#L749) for each saved local). The existing `MaybeBorrowedLocals` analysis should already give us this information. It tracks all borrows that are alive across yield points, and we store the locals that need to be kept alive due to outstanding borrows + the borrows themselves. So any borrow that is kept alive across a suspension point is self-referential.
messages.zh:
@_* * Zoxc | 116466 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Help.20needed.20to.20fix.20ancient.20async.20lowering.20soundness.20issue/near/593783914):
```quote
So #152946 is the latest PR here? #139896 seems to add an analysis pass #152946 doesn't have.
```我已经有一段时间没看了https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/139896细节，但公关方面的分析似乎没有必要（这似乎也有缺陷，因为他们[跑了一通] （https://github.com/Sky9x/rust/blob/3e1cce772d118dbb22f2e32bf97445fce1d1fb74/compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine.rs#L749)对于每个保存的本地）。现有的`MaybeBorrowedLocals`分析应该已经为我们提供了这些信息。它跟踪所有在收益率点存活的借款，我们存储由于未偿还借款+借款本身而需要存活的当地人。因此，任何在悬挂点上保持活跃的借款都是自我引用的。

messages.en: Yeah I think `MaybeBorrowedLocals` would suffice (assuming it hasn't changed since I added it) though not optimal.
messages.zh: 好的，我认为`MaybeBorrowedLocals`就足够了（假设自从我添加它以来它没有改变） ，尽管不是最优的。

messages.en: my main concern is https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/152942
messages.zh: 我主要关心的是https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/152942

messages.en: when we added `MaybeDangling` to `ManuallyDrop`, that increased the nesting of types in `MaybeUninit` by 1, causing trouble for deeply nested async coroutines because each such layer counts for the recursion limit
messages.zh: 当我们添加`MaybeDangling` 到 `ManuallyDrop`，这增加了类型的嵌套`MaybeUninit`通过1 ，给深度嵌套的异步协程带来麻烦，因为每个这样的层都计算递归限制

messages.en: making it `UnsafePinned<MaybeUninit<T>>` will add two more layers
messages.zh: 让它成为现实`UnsafePinned<MaybeUninit<T>>`将再添加两层

messages.en:
I can think of two solutions
- find a way to have these layers not count for the recursion limit since we know these types are not by themselves recursive (@**oli** is that a terrible idea or remotely plausible?)
- add a new libcore type `SelfReferentialCoroutineField` and ensure that it has all the effects of UnsafePinned, UnsafeCell, MaybeUninit, etc (by setting the [flags](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_middle/ty/struct.AdtFlags.html) and ensuring everything in the compiler checks the flags, not the lang items)
messages.zh:
我能想到两个解决方案
-找到一种方法，使这些层不计入递归限制，因为我们知道这些类型本身不是递归的（ @ * * oli * *这是一个糟糕的想法还是远程合理的？ ）
-添加新的libcore类型`SelfReferentialCoroutineField`并确保它具有UnsafePinned、UnsafeCell、MaybeUninit等所有效果（通过设置[标志] （https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_middle/ty/struct.AdtFlags.html)并确保编译器中的所有内容都检查标志，而不是语言项目）

messages.zh: 是的，我知道，但我认为这是一个结构不同的原因。但我可能错过了一些东西。

messages.en: I'm not sure if `recursion_limit` is worth working around. It leaks implementation details of libraries and internal details of the compiler. We don't handle it correctly for incremental / parallel compilation. Maybe having a cargo feature to bump it for upstream dependencies would help?
messages.zh: 我不敢肯定`recursion_limit`是值得努力解决的。它泄露了库的实现细节和编译器的内部细节。对于增量/并行编译，我们没有正确处理它。也许有一个cargo功能可以将其用于上游依赖项会有所帮助？

messages.en: We could also have cargo bump it for upstream dependencies by default as they will likely compile without any issues. That would leave a bit of a buffer for changes.
messages.zh: 默认情况下，我们也可以让上游依赖项的cargo bump它，因为它们可能会在没有任何问题的情况下编译。这将为更改留下一些缓冲区。

messages.en: no having 5 nested layers of types could also make a perf difference
messages.zh: 没有5个嵌套层的类型也可能产生性能差异

messages.en: Getting rid of the internal layers of `UnsafePinned` and `MaybeUninit` could also help performance wise? Then you'd be down to 2. I assume `UnsafePinned` is generally useful so it wouldn't serve as `SelfReferentialCoroutineField`. I haven't read up on it.
messages.zh: 摆脱内部层`UnsafePinned`和`MaybeUninit`也可以帮助明智地实现绩效？那你就只剩下2个了。我想`UnsafePinned`通常很有用，所以它不会用作`SelfReferentialCoroutineField`。我还没有读过这方面的内容。

messages.en: ``SelfReferentialCoroutineField<T>`` would be basically `UnsafePinned<MaybeUninit<T>>`
messages.zh: ``SelfReferentialCoroutineField<T>``基本上是`UnsafePinned<MaybeUninit<T>>`

messages.en: the idea is that ``UnsafePinned`` will also be stabilized for direct use by unsafe code
messages.zh: 我们的想法是，``UnsafePinned``也将稳定供不安全代码直接使用

messages.en: I did try to read up a bit on `UnsafePinned`. It introduces the concept of references to partially unique data. It also ties it into the concept of pinned data, but these concepts don't seem fundamentally linked? Wouldn't it allow having say a `PartiallyUnique<&mut T>` type?
messages.zh: 我确实试着阅读了一下`UnsafePinned`。它引入了对部分唯一数据的引用的概念。它也将其与固定数据的概念联系起来，但这些概念似乎并没有从根本上联系起来？难道不允许说`PartiallyUnique<&mut T>`类型

messages.en:
@_**Zoxc|116466** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Help.20needed.20to.20fix.20ancient.20async.20lowering.20soundness.20issue/near/594004926):
```quote
It introduces the concept of references to partially unique data.
```

yes, it's basically like `UnsafeCell` but for `&mut`.  (note that `&mut UnsafeCell<T>` still has the usual noalias requirements, `UnsafeCell` is only special for *shared* references.)

@_* * Zoxc | 116466 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Help.20needed.20to.20fix.20ancient.20async.20lowering.20soundness.20issue/near/594004926):
```quote
It introduces the concept of references to partially unique data.
```是的，基本上就像是`UnsafeCell`但是对—”`&mut`注意`&mut UnsafeCell<T>`仍然有通常的noalias要求，`UnsafeCell`仅适用于*共享*推荐语。）

messages.en:
@_**Zoxc|116466** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Help.20needed.20to.20fix.20ancient.20async.20lowering.20soundness.20issue/near/594004926):

@_* * Zoxc | 116466 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Help.20needed.20to.20fix.20ancient.20async.20lowering.20soundness.20issue/near/594004926):

messages.zh: 请注意，固定是一个库概念，而不是一个语言概念，所以这两个概念存在于不同的世界

messages.zh: 即使您使用`UnsafePinned`，退货不健全`&mut`引用这种类型，因为用户可以执行调用等操作`mem::swap`在他们身上

messages.en: It does seem rather strange to me. Maybe an non-generator example where you wouldn't just use `Pin<&T>` would help?
messages.zh: 这对我来说确实很奇怪。也许是一个非生成器示例，在这个示例中，你不会只使用`Pin<&T>`会有帮助吗？

messages.en: Another thing I'm unsure about is how the provenance passed in `Pin<&mut T>` to a coroutine would stay valid between `resume` calls? As it would be used for the self-references.
messages.zh: 另一件我不确定的事情是出处是如何传递的`Pin<&mut T>`协程将保持有效之间`resume`调用？因为它将用于自我引用。

messages.en:
@_**Zoxc|116466** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Help.20needed.20to.20fix.20ancient.20async.20lowering.20soundness.20issue/near/594018934):
```quote
Maybe an non-generator example where you wouldn't just use `Pin<&T>` would help?
```

do you have such an example?
the claim is that no such example exists, hence the name `UnsafePinned`. Pinning is the library-level mechanism that is required to be able to make sound use of the language-level concept of "aliased mutable references" that is allowed by this type.
messages.zh:
@_* * Zoxc | 116466 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Help.20needed.20to.20fix.20ancient.20async.20lowering.20soundness.20issue/near/594018934):

Maybe an non-generator example where you wouldn't just use `Pin<&T>` would help?
```你有这样的例子吗？
声称不存在这样的示例，因此名称`UnsafePinned`。固定是库级机制，需要能够合理使用此类型允许的“别名可变引用”的语言级概念。

messages.en: `noalias` affects every access done via that pointer. it has no range or size associated with it, the semantics are entirely based on how the pointer is used.
messages.zh: `noalias`影响通过该指针完成的每次访问。它没有与之关联的范围或大小，语义完全基于指针的使用方式。

messages.en:
so, "half `nooalias`" doesn't really make sense when talking about LLVM `noalias`. one could imagine other kinds of alias annotations where that might make sense, but that's not how LLVM works.

Stacked/Tree Borrows support pointers that are unique/read-only for some range but not for others. That's what we actually use for `UnsafeCell` and hopefully eventually will also use for `UnsafePinned`. But those pointers cannot be `noalias` so this information is lost when translating to LLVM IR.
messages.zh:
所以， ”一半`nooalias`“在谈论LLVM时真的没有意义`noalias`。人们可以想象其他类型的别名注释，这可能是有意义的，但这不是LLVM的工作方式。

Stacked/Tree Borrows支持某些区域唯一/只读的指针，但其他区域不支持。 这就是我们实际使用的`UnsafeCell`希望最终也能用于`UnsafePinned`。但这些指针不能`noalias`因此这些信息在转换为LLVM IR时会丢失。

topics.name: nounwind inference: `aarch64` instruction delta 20x `x86_64`
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：PR #165326 将 `nounwind` 推断从 declaration 级别改为 monomorphization 级别，使 `fn ABI` 的 `can_unwind = false`，从而生成普通 `call` 而非 `invoke`。整体中位数开销很小（aarch64 +0.06%、x86_64 +0.11%），但 `clap_derive` 等在 aarch64 上的指令数、`max-rss` 和 cycles 增幅远高于 x86_64，最高约有 20 倍差异。
- **重要分析**：该分析本身没有 target-specific 代码，无法直接解释差异。讨论认为可能涉及 codegen scheduling、函数成本估算变化导致的 codegen units 重新划分，以及不同平台 intrinsic 缺失时使用 fallback 实现。
- **目前较明确的原因**：`clap_derive` 的本地检查显示，MIR lowering 后模块反而缩小了 2.1%，减少 604 个 `invoke`；但经过 LLVM 优化后模块增大 8.3%，主要增长在 `syn` AST 的递归 drop glue 中（`Expr` 从 4093 行增至 6825 行）。这表明 `nounwind` 变化使 LLVM 进行了更多内联，原本保留为 `call` 的 body 被展开，从而产生额外工作。
- **仍未解决的问题**：初步怀疑 AArch64 与 x86_64 使用了不同的 cost model，使相同函数在 inlining threshold 两侧产生不同结果；不过讨论中确认 instruction selection 阶段的 cost model 差异很大，而 inlining cost model 是否如此仍不确定，尚未完全定位二十倍差异的具体根因。

messages.en:
Hi. I have a draft PR up that infers nounwind per monomorphization rather than per declaration ([rust-lang/rust#165326](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/165326)): a new query proves that the body codegen will emit for one instance cannot unwind, and the fn ABI then gets `can_unwind = false` so codegen emits a plain call instead of an invoke. The perf run puts the cost entirely in `opt/full`, which is what I expected, and the median across the 59 benchmarks that report both targets is +0.06% on aarch64 and +0.11% on x86_64. What I can't account for is the top end. `clap_derive-4.5.32` gains 9.45G instructions on aarch64 (+23.1%) but only 0.45G on x86_64 (+1.1%). `serde_derive` is 1.92G against 0.57G, `syn` 1.44G against 0.44G. The first two are proc-macro crates and syn is the parse library they both use. The same rows show `max-rss` +18.3% and cycles +21.6% on aarch64 against +0.1% and +0.2% on x86_64, so the aarch64 build really is doing more work, not just retiring more instructions. Meanwhile `cranelift-codegen`, `image`, `ripgrep` and `regex-automata` improve on both targets.

The analysis itself has no target-specific code in it. It looks at the unwind strategy, the ABI kind, a handful of lang items and whether a MIR body is available, so I'd expect roughly the same amount of work on either target, and a twentyfold difference in absolute instruction delta isn't something the analysis can explain.

I’d like to ask if anyone else has encountered a similar situation? What could be the cause of this?

分析本身没有目标特定的代码。 它着眼于放松策略、ABI类型、少数语言项目以及是否可以使用MIR主体，因此我预计在任何目标上的工作量大致相同，并且绝对指令增量的二十倍差异不是分析可以解释的。

topics.name: ✔ ./x test library/compiler-builtins doesn’t work
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`./x test library/compiler-builtins` 未按预期运行 `compiler-builtins` 的 unit/integration tests；通常只看到 `alloc` doctests，使用 `--test` 则没有测试执行。对 `thumbv7m-none-eabi`、`thumbv7em-none-eabi`、`thumbv8m.main-none-eabi` 等目标，测试本身可能无法运行，但至少应能编译检查。
- **原因判断**：`compiler-builtins` 是 workspace，且其 `Cargo.toml` 中设置了 `test = false`，因此 bootstrap 当前的通用 library 测试逻辑可能只处理了 doctests，或者根本没有为 `compiler-builtins` 实现专门的测试支持。相关代码位于 `src/bootstrap/src/core/build_steps/test.rs`。
- **现有方案**：在 `library/compiler-builtins` 子目录中运行 `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features` 可以正常工作，但只能覆盖一部分测试；直接通过 `x test` 时，即使构建成功，也可能出现 `target filter 'tests' specified, but no targets matched`，实际没有执行测试。
- **重要观点**：应同时参考 `compiler-builtins` 自身 CI 中的测试内容，而不能只依赖 `rust-lang/rust` 子树里的测试；有人建议为 `compiler-builtins` 增加单独的 bootstrap 测试逻辑。此前已有相关 PR（#142106），Trevor Gross 表示若继续推进会很有帮助。
- **进展与结论**：Jakub Beránek 表示会尝试接手，并提交了 PR #164162 进行修复/支持；该话题随后被标记为 resolved。
- **仍未明确的问题**：聊天记录没有说明 PR #164162 是否最终合并，也没有确认 `./x test library/compiler-builtins` 是否已经完整执行了所有应有测试。

topics.name: vibe check - removing Option from Terminator
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：提议将 `BasicBlockData::terminator` 从 `Option<Terminator>` 改为必有的 `Terminator`。目前绝大多数使用点都假定 terminator 存在，导致大量 `unwrap` 或隐式解包；不同代码路径对 `Option` 的处理也不一致，尤其是 MIR building、`SimplifyCfg` 和少数其他 pass。
- **主要方案与观点**：原型曾使用 `Goto BasicBlock::MAX` 作为临时哨兵值，但大家认为这会降低类型安全，最终不应依赖这种方案。讨论倾向于先用“明显错误”的临时值完成迁移，再逐步修复所有使用点；MIR building 中可以先收集语句、计算 terminator，再一次性创建 block，部分优化则可能使用 swap 避免临时哨兵。
- **对特殊占位 terminator 的讨论**：有人提出 `TerminatorKind::ICE`、`Error` 或类似 `TyKind::Error` 的变体，但反对意见认为许多代码只匹配具体 terminator variant，可能会静默忽略该值；支持者则认为可依靠 MIR validator 报 ICE，并在已有的 `bug!()` 分支中处理。当前更倾向于不需要这些方案。
- **已达成的共识**：多数参与者赞成移除 `Option`，认为这是可行且能改善现状的改动；建议分步提交，暂时保留 `terminator()` / `terminator_mut` 等 option-like 方法，并先尽量清理代码，再在后续 PR 中移除哨兵或其他临时机制。已有 PR #165517 和 #165502 作为初步步骤。
- **仍未解决的问题**：Drop tree building、优化过程及部分 MIR building 场景的 terminator 生命周期和临时状态仍较复杂；还需确定如何在不依赖 sentinel 的情况下重构这些位置，以及是否存在少数必须保留特殊占位值的场景。

messages.en:
I have a draft PR for changing `terminator` field in `BasicBlockData` from `Option<Terminator>` to `Terminator`. Does anybody see a reason not to do this? The Option always felt awkward to me, but I don't know if I'm alone feeling this. Some notes:

 - Almost every place that processes Terminator expects it to be there, so we have bunch of unwrapping (or hidden unwrapping) everywhere

 - through making the draft, I also found that handling it is not very consistent across the codebase
     - some passes match on it, even though they should probably unwrap for correctness reasons
     - Visitors match on it and they are used in both contexts (where unwraping is desirable and where it is not) 
     - field docs says you should be using `terminator()` or `terminator_mut`, but some places don't, sometimes probably just because the field is public, sometimes because they can't (they need partial borrow)

 - Currently the places that use the option are mainly MIR building, SimplifyCfg and some other passes (I believe just one or two, though).

The way I did it in the draft was just by using sentinel value in the `Terminator` itself (`Goto BasicBlock:MAX`), but I don't think that's a good approach, I'd rather restructure those few places that use the option to track this differently.

PR: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/165369
messages.zh:
我有一份公关草稿需要更改`terminator`字段在`BasicBlockData` 从 `Option<Terminator>` 到 `Terminator`。有人看到不这样做的理由吗？ 这个选择对我来说总是很尴尬，但我不知道是否只有我一个人有这种感觉。一些注意事项：

 -几乎每个处理Terminator的地方都希望它在那里，所以我们到处都有很多拆包（或隐藏拆包）

 -通过制作草稿，我还发现在整个代码库中处理它不是非常一致-一些通行证与之匹配，尽管出于正确的原因，它们可能应该展开
     -访客在上面匹配，并且在两种情况下都使用（需要展开包装和不需要展开包装） 
     - field docs说您应该使用`terminator()` 或 `terminator_mut`，但有些地方没有，有时可能只是因为该领域是公开的，有时是因为他们不能（他们需要部分借款）

 -目前使用此选项的房源主要是MIR大楼、SimplifyCfg和其他一些通行证（不过我相信只有一两个）。

我在草稿中这样做的方式只是通过使用哨兵值在`Terminator`要注意`Goto BasicBlock:MAX`） ，但我认为这不是一个好方法，我宁愿重组那些使用该选项以不同方式跟踪的地方。

公关：https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/165369

messages.en: Using a sentinel value instead of `Option` sounds like decreasing the type-safety of the API. In my mind, the primary reason we even have `Option` is to not have sentinel values. So the reason to not do this is that it's against like, the basic design of the language? I think the better question is why do you want to do this.
messages.zh: 使用Sentinel值而不是`Option`听起来像是降低了API的类型安全性。在我看来，我们甚至有主要的原因`Option`就是没有Sentinel值。所以不这样做的原因是它违背了语言的基本设计？我认为更好的问题是你为什么要这样做。

messages.en: Like I said, I don't want to use the sentinel value in the end, that's just how I prototyped it.
messages.zh: 就像我说的，我不想最终使用哨兵值，这就是我原型的方式。

messages.en: Ah! Then yes I would much prefer to have the Terminator be mandatory. I have always just assumed it's optional for the use of some part of the compiler I don't work on
messages.zh: 啊！那么是的，我更希望终结者是强制性的。我一直认为，对于编译器中我不使用的部分，这是可选的

messages.en: I feel like it'd be worth it even if a few select places had to use some ugly sentinel value for their needs, but that's debatable and certainly not preferable.
messages.zh: 我觉得这是值得的，即使一些精选的地方不得不使用一些丑陋的哨兵价值来满足他们的需求，但这是有争议的，当然也不可取。

There's two reasons I think it would be fine if it proved useful (instead of "where did that goto come from?!?"):
1. You'd get a descriptive error in the MIR validator that would produce an ICE, so it wouldn't be "silently ignored" if a pass ever leaves it there

topics.name: with_fn! adds baffling self-links to many Diag::* docs
topics.name_zh: with_fn!向许多Diag:: *文档添加了令人困惑的自我链接
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`rustc_errors::diagnostic::Diag` 的许多方法文档存在令人困惑的自链接。例如，`Diag::span_label()` 的文档链接会指向自身。
- **原因**：问题与 `with_fn!` 宏有关；该行为自其引入以来就存在。宏生成的方法文档沿用了旧版 `forward` 宏的链接处理方式。
- **历史背景**：旧版 `forward` 宏会在 `Diag`（当时为 `DiagnosticBuilder`）中生成转发方法，并链接到 `DiagInner`（当时为 `Diagnostic`）中的实际方法，因此链接目标是合理的。
- **变化来源**：后来相关方法被移动到现在的 `Diag` 中，但文档链接没有同步调整，导致链接最终指向同一个方法；这一问题当时没有被注意到。
- **未解决问题**：聊天记录中尚未提出或确认具体修复方案，也未说明是否会提交修复。

messages.en:
I was looking at the Diag docs as background for figuring out https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/100896 and I noticed that, for example, [Diag::span_label()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_errors/diagnostic/struct.Diag.html#method.span_label) docs link right back to that same function.

A quick peek at the source revealed the involvement of the [with_fn macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_errors/diagnostic/macro.with_fn.html), which has apparently been doing this since it was introduced in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/f6f87798439e2ce7861da761b444fe0978335ed9 ... oh.
messages.zh:
我把Diag文档看作是找出答案的背景https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/100896我注意到，例如， [Diag:: span_label ()] (https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_errors/diagnostic/struct.Diag.html#method.span_label)docs链接到同一个函数。

快速浏览来源揭示了[with_fn宏]的参与（https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_errors/diagnostic/macro.with_fn.html),这显然是自从它被引入以来一直在做的，https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/f6f87798439e2ce7861da761b444fe0978335ed9哦，

messages.en: Looks like this behavior was adapted from the old [forward macro](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/f6f87798439e2ce7861da761b444fe0978335ed9#diff-6c98b29d710fd5dbb3073d32b31b83021fdd67d5eb7713027c4b3b421423e623L188) in that commit, where it generated both methods to `Diag` (well, at the time it was `DiagnosticBuilder`) to forward to one method in `DiagInner` (then called `Diagnostic`), and the links went to *that* one. So then the commit in question moved those methods over to what we now call `Diag`and I guess nobody noticed at the time that those links ended up pointing to the very same method and that this is, in fact, disorienting.
messages.zh: 看起来这种行为是根据旧的[转发模板] （https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/f6f87798439e2ce7861da761b444fe0978335ed9#diff-6c98b29d710fd5dbb3073d32b31b83021fdd67d5eb7713027c4b3b421423e623L188)在该提交中，它生成了两个方法来`Diag`（嗯，当时`DiagnosticBuilder`)转发到一个方法中`DiagInner`（然后被称为`Diagnostic`） ，链接转到*那个*。因此，有问题的提交将这些方法移到了我们现在称之为`Diag`and I guess nobody noticed at the time that those links ended up pointing to the very same method and that this is, in fact, disorienting.

topics.name: glibc version support
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：Rust 的大多数 `linux-gnu` 目标目前将 glibc 2.17 作为最低版本；为在 `std` 中切换到 64 位 `time_t`，32 位目标可能需要 glibc 2.34。当前讨论仅涉及 32 位系统，64 位目标暂不受影响。
- **现状澄清**：`std` 使用的 `fstat64` 并不一定意味着需要 glibc 2.33，因为 glibc 2.17 中存在内联函数和 `libc_nonshared.a` shim；真正使用 time64 版本的 `__fstat64_time64` 才需要约 glibc 2.34。现有文档中的 2.17 基线被认为仍然有效。
- **主要观点**：有人建议按固定年限（如发布 10 年后）定期提高基线，但反对者认为没有实际需求就不应增加下游和维护者负担。RHEL 7 仍需支持 Firefox ESR 的 Rust 构建，RHEL 8 使用 glibc 2.28，因此过早提高所有目标会影响长期维护的发行版、嵌入式设备和旧工业系统。
- **倾向方案**：初步倾向于将除 `i686-unknown-linux-gnu` 外的 32 位目标（后来也倾向排除 `i586`）提高到 glibc 2.34，以支持 time64 并为 2038 年问题做准备；`i686` 可能等到 RHEL 8 延长支持结束、约 2029 年再迁移。该方案仍需目标维护者和发行版打包者确认。
- **仍未解决的问题**：部分目标（如 `armv4t`、`aarch64 ... ilp32`）缺乏主流发行版支持或无法使用 glibc 2.34，尚不清楚是否值得对其他目标单独提高基线；SLES、Debian 等发行版在旧 glibc 上提供新 Rust 工具链的兼容需求，以及长期运行的 32 位软件需求，也仍需进一步评估。

messages.en:
How do we determine what versions of glibc we should support?

Currently most of our linux-gnu targets list 2.17, which was released in 2012. I'm poking at swapping to 64-bit `time_t` in `std` but that would rocket our minimum to about 2.34, from 2021.
messages.zh:
我们如何确定应该支持哪些版本的glibc ？

目前，我们的大多数linux-gnu目标列表2.17于2012年发布。 我正在戳交换到64位`time_t` 在 `std`但从2021年起，我们的最低值将升至2.34左右。

messages.en: To be clear, any kind of bump only applies to 32-bit systems.
messages.zh: 需要明确的是，任何类型的凹凸仅适用于32位系统。

messages.en: Hm, interesting: we're actually using symbols from glibc 2.33 already, e.g. `fstat64`. So I guess the versions at https://doc.rust-lang.org/beta/rustc/platform-support.html are just incorrect?
messages.zh: 嗯，有趣的是：我们实际上已经使用了glibc 2.33中的符号，例如`fstat64`。所以我猜版本在https://doc.rust-lang.org/beta/rustc/platform-support.html只是不正确？

messages.en: @**Josh Stone (cuviper)** I believe you've been involved with this version support in the past
messages.zh: @ * * Josh Stone （ cuviper ） * *我相信您过去曾参与此版本的支持

messages.en: fstat64 exists in 2.17 as an inline function calling __fxstat64. I haven't checked how rust is hooking that up.
messages.zh: fstat64作为调用__ fxstat64的内联函数存在于2.17中。我还没有检查生锈是如何连接起来的。

messages.en: But I'm reasonably sure that our documented baseline is correct, given that we're building the x86 dist artifacts on CentOS 7 with that glibc version :)
messages.zh: 但我有理由相信我们记录的基线是正确的，因为我们正在CentOS 7上使用该glibc版本构建x86 dist工件:)

messages.en: If we wanted to raise the glibc requirement, I don't think we would be able to go higher than 2.28 (the version used by RHEL 8 derivatives).
messages.zh: 如果我们想提高glibc要求，我认为我们不能高于2.28 （ RHEL 8衍生品使用的版本）。

messages.en: FWIW, the last glibc version bump was driven by LLVM build requirements more than anything (see https://blog.rust-lang.org/2022/08/01/Increasing-glibc-kernel-requirements/).
messages.zh: FWIW ，最后一个glibc版本颠簸主要是由LLVM构建要求驱动的（请参阅https://blog.rust-lang.org/2022/08/01/Increasing-glibc-kernel-requirements/).

messages.en: It's using them directly via a binding https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/92b5b8c87c61b20adc9001b41baf587634a74734/library/std/src/sys/fs/unix.rs#L35-L37, which is in the 2.33 list https://github.com/sailfishos-mirror/glibc/blob/20313cef40912b1f52cc49f399db7ea618e37e3f/sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/i386/libc.abilist#L2470-L2480
messages.zh: 它通过绑定直接使用它们https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/92b5b8c87c61b20adc9001b41baf587634a74734/library/std/src/sys/fs/unix.rs#L35-L37,它在2.33列表中https://github.com/sailfishos-mirror/glibc/blob/20313cef40912b1f52cc49f399db7ea618e37e3f/sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/i386/libc.abilist#L2470-L2480

messages.en: That was a poorly explained example since it has three variants: the baseline `fstat`, the LFS64 version `fstat64` which came in 2.33 (at least according to that list), and the LFS+time64 version `__fstat64_time64` that came in 2.34. std currently uses the second, a change to time64 would mean using the third
messages.zh: 这是一个解释不清的例子，因为它有三个变体：基线`fstat`， LFS64版本`fstat64`它出现在2.33中（至少根据该列表） ，以及LFS + time64版本`__fstat64_time64`2.34。std当前使用第二个，对time64的更改意味着使用第三个

messages.en: How would people feel about bumping the official baseline to at least Debian 9 (glibc 2.24, kernel 4.9)?
messages.zh: 如果将官方基线至少提高到Debian 9 （ glibc 2.24 ，内核4.9 ） ，人们会有什么感受？

messages.en: Anything specific around that version?
messages.zh: 围绕该版本有什么具体内容吗？

messages.en:
Well, I think we should be bumping the requirement regularly. Setting an arbitrary baseline of 10 years after release seems like a reasonable rule of thumb. I doubt anyone would object to dropping support for Debian 8, for example, which was released back in 2015.

Once we establish that as a baseline, we can always consider raising it further if it makes sense.
messages.zh:
嗯，我认为我们应该定期提高要求。 将释放后的10年设定为任意基线似乎是一个合理的经验法则。 例如，我怀疑是否有人会反对放弃对Debian 8的支持， Debian 8早在2015年就发布了。

一旦我们确定这是一个基线，如果有意义的话，我们可以随时考虑进一步提高。

messages.en:
> I doubt anyone would object to dropping support for Debian 8, for example

Careful about that, you might want to look at some previous version bump discussions (I think it was in libc or some MSRV? not sure), this usually makes people with ancient, broken and crusty targets come out of the woodworks.
I recall some people saying they're building new rust executables and ship them to old industrial/appliance-like thingies to keep them working.
messages.zh:
>例如，我怀疑是否有人会反对放弃对Debian 8的支持

注意这一点，你可能想看看以前的一些版本碰撞讨论（我认为这是在libc或一些MSRV中-不确定） ，这通常会让有古老，破碎和硬壳目标的人从木制品中走出来。
我记得有些人说他们正在构建新的生锈可执行件，并将它们运送到旧的工业/电器之类的东西上，以保持它们正常工作。

messages.en: I am mildly opposed to just bumping if we have no reason to.  I'm reasonably confident there are people (if a relatively small population) still stuck on older versions for one reason or another and bumping just because doesn't seem useful enough to justify breaking them
messages.zh: 如果我们没有理由，我温和地反对只是碰撞。我有理由相信，由于某种原因，有些人（如果人口相对较少）仍然坚持使用旧版本，只是因为似乎没有足够的用处来证明打破它们是合理的

messages.en:
@**Fabio Valentini** what does Fedora have?

we bump glibcs so infrequently, and we change our use of APIs so slowly, it often only increases the version we *de facto* demand well after the *de jure* change lands. so I really wouldn't mind doing the formal bump to as-high-as-we-can-go for these targets. it will only affect new builds for 32-bit, non-x86 targets that often have a different glibc minimum than our x86 or x86-64 stuff anyways.
messages.zh:
@ * * Fabio Valentini * * Fedora有什么？

我们很少碰到glibcs ，我们改变API的使用非常缓慢，它通常只会在*法律上*改变土地后增加我们*事实上*需求的版本。所以我真的不介意为这些目标做正式的碰撞。它只会影响32位非x86目标的新构建，这些目标通常具有与我们的x86或x86-64不同的glibc最小值。

topics.name: Creating a codegen backend with fast compilation
topics.name_zh: 使用快速编译创建代码源后端
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论是否应尝试使用 LLM 创建面向开发构建的快速 codegen backend，或优先改进现有的 `rustc_codegen_cranelift`；关键挑战不仅是生成 x64 的 Hello World，而是支持完整 Rust、Tier 1 targets 及各种边界特性。
- **Cranelift 现状**：`rustc_codegen_cranelift` 的编译速度较好，但生成代码的运行时性能约为 LLVM `-O0` 的 2 倍以内；开启 Cranelift 优化后会更接近 LLVM。其采用外部 assembler 处理 inline asm，实际会额外启动 LLVM backend 编译 `global_asm!()`，fallback 机制仍较 hacky。
- **可能的架构方向**：有人认为“快速 backend + 运行时 JIT/optimizer”可能是 Rust debug builds 的理想方向，也可以考虑 interpreter；LLVM IR 配合 `lli` 或 LLVM JIT 是相关方案。另一个重要方向是让 LLVM backend 更容易作为 edge cases 的 fallback。
- **TPDE 进展与数据**：TPDE 可使用 LLVM 作为约 2% CGUs 的 fallback。一个基于 TPDE 和 custom IR 的 backend 在 Linux/x64 上测试，关闭 debuginfo 时平均编译时间比 LLVM 快约 2.6%–10.0%（单线程约 10.0%），启用 always-inline 后运行时平均比 LLVM 快约 7.9%，而 `rustc_cranelift` 慢约 18.7%。其当前仍不支持 inline assembly 和 debuginfo，另有少量 LLVM intrinsics 未支持。
- **仍未解决的问题**：快速 backend 对完整 Rust 特性、inline asm、debug-info 和 LLVM intrinsics 的覆盖，以及可靠、低成本的 LLVM fallback 方式仍需完善；此外，LLM 方案是否适合 Rust compiler project 尚无进一步结论，讨论中指出项目采用 LLM 会受到相关 policy 限制，而个人或 out-of-tree 实验不受此影响。

messages.en:
I'm wondering if it makes sense to experiment with using LLMs to create a fast codegen backend for development builds. That would noticeably overlap with `rustc_codegen_cranelift`. So I'm wondering a bit what the status of that is. I get the impression it hasn't seen a lot of adoption, so I'm wondering what the current pitfalls of it is? Is the output much slower than LLVM's -O0?
cc @**bjorn3**
messages.zh:
我想知道，尝试使用LLM为开发版本创建一个快速的codegen后端是否有意义。这将明显重叠于`rustc_codegen_cranelift`。所以我想知道它的状态是什么。 我得到的印象是它没有得到很多采用，所以我想知道它目前的陷阱是什么？ 输出是否比LLVM的-O0慢得多？
cc @ * * bjorn3 * *

messages.en: [here](https://perf.rust-lang.org/compare.html?start=65872f1ea564eab345f03ad14e54001032cffeb0&end=65872f1ea564eab345f03ad14e54001032cffeb0&stat=instructions%3Au&selfCompareParameter=backend&nonRelevant=true&opt=false) is a recent diff of Cranelift vs LLVM (though the debuginfo they generate is not completely the same, so it's not completely apples to apples)
messages.zh: 这里。https://perf.rust-lang.org/compare.html?start=65872f1ea564eab345f03ad14e54001032cffeb0&end=65872f1ea564eab345f03ad14e54001032cffeb0&stat=instructions%3Au&selfCompareParameter=backend&nonRelevant=true&opt=false)是Cranelift与LLVM的最新差异（尽管它们生成的debuginfo并不完全相同，因此它并不完全是apples to apples ）

messages.en: TPDE might also be interesting.
messages.zh: TPDE也可能很有趣。

messages.en: Creating a codegen backend that can compile hello world to x64 is probably not *that* difficult. Creating a backend that can compile all of Rust, across even just all Tier 1 targets, including all the bells and whistles, is something else (even if you don't take optimization into account).
messages.zh: 创建一个可以将hello world编译到x64的codegen后端可能并不*那么*困难。创建一个可以编译所有Rust的后端，甚至可以编译所有1级目标，包括所有铃铛和哨子，这是另一回事（即使您没有考虑优化）。

messages.en: Runtime performance of Cranelift output is within 2x of LLVM -O0.
messages.zh: Cranelift输出的运行时间性能是LLVM -O0的2倍以内。

messages.en: What does performance (compile time / runtime) look like with cranelift optimizations? -O0 can be quite slow for some use cases already.
messages.zh: Cranelift优化的性能（编译时/运行时）是什么样的？ -O0对于某些用例来说可能相当慢。

messages.en:
> experiment with using LLMs

For your own personal use/enjoyment? Sure. For adoption by the project? That would obviously violate the LLM policy.
messages.zh:
>尝试使用LLM

供您个人使用/享用？ 当然可以，供项目采用？ 这显然违反了法学硕士政策。

messages.en: I assume you mean adoption by the compiler team? Which would be unlikely anytime soon anyway. Has the project adopted a LLM policy?
messages.zh: 我猜你的意思是编译器团队采用？无论如何，这在短期内是不太可能的。该项目是否采用了法学硕士政策？

messages.en: You are asking in the T-compiler stream. This implies you want something tangled with the compiler. If not, you can also just generate it out of tree without anyone being affected or any policies applying
messages.zh: 您在T编译器流中询问。这意味着你想要一些与编译器纠缠在一起的东西。如果没有，您也可以从树中生成它，而不会影响任何人或应用任何政策

messages.en:
I'm mostly asking if it would make sense to focus on improving `rustc_codegen_cranelift` instead, as its compile times are quite good already, which suggests some other reason for less adoption.

I think it could make sense to experiment with Swift style generics / polymorphization which may need some backend interface changes, but that could just live in a rustc fork.

我主要问的是，专注于改进`rustc_codegen_cranelift`相反，由于其编译时间已经相当不错，这表明了采用率较低的其他原因。

我认为尝试Swift风格的泛型/多态化可能是有意义的，这可能需要一些后端接口更改，但这可能只是存在于rustc分叉中。

messages.en: cg_clif uses an external assembler for inline asm by wrapping it inside a function that can be called as usual from Cranelift IR. In practice this is invoking a separate rustc instance with the LLVM backend to compile a `global_asm!()` block inside a `#![no_core]` crate as there may not be a system wide installation of an assembler.
messages.zh: cg_clif通过将其包装在可以像往常一样从Cranelift IR调用的函数内，为内联asm使用外部汇编程序。在实践中，这是使用LLVM后端调用单独的rustc实例来编译`global_asm!()`block inside a`#![no_core]`板条箱，因为可能没有在系统范围内安装装配器。

messages.en:
Hi together,
as part of my master thesis I'm currently creating a backend that's using TPDE with a custom IR. (Under supervision of @**Alexis Engelke** , one of the creators of TPDE)
This should lead to noticeably better compile time performance compared to LLVM and also the TPDE version over LLVM—IR.

The current version supports Linux with x64 and is built against the rustc version nightly-2026-10-28.
Currently not supported are inline assembly, debug-info (not in TPDE so far) some rare LLVM intrinsics, which I haven't encountered so far.

Otherwise it supports most of Rust code, namely all compile and runtime tests of rustc-perf can be compiled (except with asm, but all intrinsics work).
The ABI is fully compatible to Rust and C according to ABI Cafe. Also the tests run for the basic versions.

Tested with rustc-perf I get the following average over all compile time tests (once without inline: rustc_tpde, and with inline: rustc_tpde_inline)
```text
+-------------------------+------------+------------+-------------------+-----------------+
| Compiletime (wall-time) | rustc_llvm | rustc_tpde | rustc_tpde_inline | rustc_cranelift |
+-------------------------+------------+------------+-------------------+-----------------+
| 64 cores                |  1223.5 ms |      -2.6% |             -2.5% |           -1.0% |
| 8 cores                 |  1228.0 ms |      -2.7% |             -2.7% |           -1.1% |
| 4 cores                 |  1245.9 ms |      -3.6% |             -3.6% |           -1.9% |
| 64 cores, cgu = 1       |  1361.4 ms |      -9.2% |             -9.3% |           -3.1% |
+-------------------------+------------+------------+-------------------+-----------------+
```
The inline version inlines all functions that are marked as always inline.
To pick some specific compile tests on 4 cores: cranelift-codegen-0.119.0: -17,5%, ripgrep: -15.1%. 
The tpde-llvm-ir version does not support all compile time tests so I don't have full numbers here, but as an example on compile test "regression-31157" we have -9.3% ± 2.2% for tpde-llvm-ir, while it's -12.6% ± 2.3% with the custom ir.

Looking at the runtime, with inlining the always inline functions we can get a better performance compared to LLVM, far better than Cranelift:
```text
+----------+------------+------------+-------------------+-----------------+
| Runtime  | rustc_llvm | rustc_tpde | rustc_tpde_inline | rustc_cranelift |
+----------+------------+------------+-------------------+-----------------+
| Average  |  1059.4 ms |      -0.6% |             -7.9% |          +18.7% |
+----------+------------+------------+-------------------+-----------------+
```

Main gains are from Obj generations which take roughly 93% less time and the IR generation which takes around 25% less time.
You can find the current state of the repository here [1]. The extensive performance numbers can be found here [2].


[1] https://github.com/jonastahl/RustcTpde
[2] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jonastahl/RustcTpdeBenchmarking/779b08822a1b61938ffdca7bb30d3a2abb309c29/results3.txt

topics.name: Using -T for target modifiers and forwards compatibility
topics.name_zh: 使用-T实现目标修饰符和向前兼容性
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：部分编译选项是否属于 target modifier 并不明确。若保守地将其稳定为 `-T`，未来可能希望通过 `-C` 使用，但无法撤回已经允许的 `-T` 用法，从而影响 forwards compatibility；`-C` 与 `-T` 的混用及整个 crate graph 的一致性检查也较复杂。
- **主要方案**：允许部分或全部 `-C` 选项也通过 `-T` 传递；一旦使用 `-T`，相关选项就必须在整个 crate graph 中一致，而通过 `-C` 使用时可以只对局部生效。错误信息应提示：如果该选项也可用 `-C`，可改用 `-C` 避免一致性限制。
- **语义讨论**：倾向于将 `-C` 和 `-T` 视为同一个选项池的不同设置方式，而不是完全独立的选项结构。可合并的值（如 sanitizer）应分别跟踪子选项；需要单一值一致的选项则要求值相同。若同一选项同时以 `-C`/`-T` 设置，简单的 `-T` 优先级可能不足以处理合并语义。
- **一致性难点**：需要明确 `-T` 与 `-C` 混用时的 mismatch 行为，以及哪些值应记录到 crate metadata；此外，`-Tllvm-target-features` 可能要求 `-Codegen-backend` 一致，ABI 相关 target features 还可能被 `-Ctarget-cpu` 或 `-Ctarget-feature` 间接启用。
- **当前结论/进展**：实现该方案后，David 和 lqd 认为复杂度、测试及用户影响相对于收益可能不值得，因此倾向于不合入 PR #160167，也可能不推进 compiler-team issue #980；这使得 #160593 可以继续采用现有方案。
- **仍未解决的问题**：target modifiers 后续如何整理、是否保持现有接口，以及像 `-Ctarget-cpu` 这类“有时是 target modifier、有时不是”的选项如何在 UI 上处理，尚无明确计划；有人提出依据 `--target` 判断其是否为 target modifier，但实现仍需较多工作。

messages.en:
See https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/980 for context.

I have one concern/question: For some flags it is unclear whether the flag is a target modifier or not, so we might conservatively make it into a target modifier. One example from the original target modifiers RFC is `-Zpatchable-function-entry` or `-Zfixed-x18`. If we classify stable flags into `-C` or `-T` like this, does this mean that we cannot stabilize flags without resolving this question?

Consider the hypothetical scenario where we are unsure if `-Zfoo` should be stabilized as `-Cfoo` or `-Tfoo`. To be conservative we say "let's stabilize as target modifier for now" and then we figure out whether it can be relaxed in the future. But this means that it was stabilized as `-Tfoo`, and now needs to be usable as `-Cfoo`. But we cannot take back the ability to use it as `-Tfoo`.

I suppose one way we could handle this is to allow using `-T` for all flags, and apply the whole-crate-graph check for any flag for which `-T` is used, even if not a target modifier. And then only non-target-modifiers are usable as `-C` flags.

The above also works somewhat nicely with exploit mitigations. If you want rustc to check that you are using your exploit mitigation everywhere, just pass it as `-T`.

Or conversely, it could be a way you explicitly opt-out of the target modifier check for a target modifier. Once you pass `-Cunsafe-allow-abi-mismatch`, you are allowed to pass a target modifier flag as `-C` instead of the usual `-T`.

Thoughts?
messages.zh:
参阅https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/980上下文。

我有一个疑虑/问题：对于某些标记，目前尚不清楚该标记是否是目标修饰符，因此我们可能会保守地将其设置为目标修饰符。 原始目标修饰符RFC的一个示例是`-Zpatchable-function-entry` 或 `-Zfixed-x18`。如果我们将稳定标志分类为`-C` 或 `-T`像这样，这是否意味着我们不能在不解决这个问题的情况下稳定旗帜？

考虑一下假设的场景，在这种情况下，我们不确定`-Zfoo`应稳定为`-Cfoo` 或 `-Tfoo`。为了保守起见，我们说“让我们暂时稳定下来作为目标修饰符” ，然后我们会弄清楚将来是否可以放松。但这意味着它被稳定为`-Tfoo`，现在需要可用作`-Cfoo`。但我们不能收回将其用作`-Tfoo`.

我想我们可以解决这个问题的一种方法是允许使用`-T`对所有旗帜进行检查，并对任何旗帜应用全箱图检查，`-T`使用，即使不是目标修饰符。然后只有非目标修饰符可用作`-C`旗帜。

上述方法在利用漏洞缓解方面也能很好地发挥作用。 如果您希望rustc检查您是否在任何地方使用漏洞缓解，只需将其传递为`-T`.

或者相反，这可能是您明确选择退出目标修饰符检查目标修饰符的方式。通过后`-Cunsafe-allow-abi-mismatch`，您可以传递目标修饰符标记为`-C`而不是通常的`-T`你觉得怎样？

```

and which part of that is recorded as a "must be consistent across crates" modifier?
````

I think the meaning we'd want for this is pretty clear. Fail the build if any compilation units disagree on whether kcfi is enabled. But divergence in whether address sanitizer is enabled is fine.

So `-Csanitizer=foo,bar` behaves like `-Csanitizer-foo -Csanitizer-bar` in that each option on the RHS is a completely separate flag tracked independetly.

Yes, other `-Cflag=value` flags need different behavior where the right hand side is the *value* that must be equal. But I think it's ok to simply allow some flags to have the RHS expand into several "sub flags", and to have other flags treat the RHS as a single value that must be equal. We can make this determiniation on a flag-by-flag basis.

```

````我认为我们想要的意义非常明确。 如果任何编译单元不同意是否启用kcfi ，则生成失败。 但是，在是否启用地址消毒剂方面存在分歧是可以的。

We can make this determiniation on a flag-by-flag basis.

hello, visiting #160167 during triage. I noticed that this is somewhat "blocking" #160593. Just mention if it helps get the discussion rolling again :)
```

I've recently been helping to make progress on https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/160167, rebasing it, discussing with Vadim about their questions and review comments and how they can be addressed, what additional work we need to do in the PR vs future PRs, and so on.

David has implemented the approach described here (to be able to use most -C options as -T), and I've also expanded this forward compatibility to the current unstable target modifiers (so -Z in addition to -C/-T).

However, after doing the work, David and I discussed some of our conclusions about this plan, and the tradeoffs we saw made us feel like the idea of using -T for target modifiers may not be worth it in practice. From the experience of implementing it, seeing the complexity, the impact on tests and users, etc versus the perceived usefulness of it, it makes us think we probably wouldn't want to actually land #160167 (or https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/980 in general, not even with the first implementation before implementing Alice's suggestion from this thread).

So @**apiraino** overall I think we can "unblock" #160593, it can keep using the approach it's using now -- that would have initially conflicted with #160167, so it's fine now IMO. I will leave comments on the GH PRs and issues.

topics.name: New t3 target: SerenityOS
topics.summary:
- Andrew Kaster 提交了为 `rustc` 添加 `x86_64-unknown-serenity` 和 `aarch64-unknown-serenity` target 的 PR，计划从头重做此前为 SerenityOS 启用 `std` 的 out-of-tree 补丁。
- 讨论确认实施顺序应为：先让 `rustc` 识别该 target，再添加 `libc` bindings，最后提交 Rust 仓库中启用 `std` 所需的补丁。Andrew 也在确认 `cc-rs` 是否会自动获取 target 定义，以及如何避免 `libc` port 文件包含未使用的声明。
- 关于流程，bjorn3 认为可能需要创建 MCP，说明已接受 Tier 3 target policy 的全部要求；Andrew 指出文档称是否需要 MCP 由 compiler team reviewer 决定，Tier 3 target 通常只需提交 PR 等待 `compiler_leads` 审核。
- Trevor Gross 表示，若 2–3 周没有 reviewer 响应，可以礼貌 ping 或 reroll；`compiler-leads` 团队规模较小，相关流程可能需要改进。他个人倾向于所有新 target 都要求 MCP，并取消单独的 `compiler-leads` 审核。
- 目前未明确 SerenityOS target 是否必须创建 MCP；PR 的审核仍在等待中。

messages.en:
If folks want an MCP in that repo I'm happy to make one, but the docs I found and was linked to suggest it's not required for a new t3 target.

The docs for the tier 3 [target-tier-policy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/target-tier-policy.html#tier-3-target-policy) say that whether an MCP is needed at the compiler team reviewer's discretion.

> A proposed new tier 3 target must be reviewed and approved by a member of the compiler team based on these requirements. The reviewer may choose to gauge broader compiler team consensus via a [Major Change Proposal (MCP)](https://forge.rust-lang.org/compiler/proposals-and-stabilization.html#how-do-i-submit-an-mcp). 

And the linked stabilization docs for [promoting a target](https://forge.rust-lang.org/compiler/proposals-and-stabilization.html#promoting-targets) state that the requirement is simply to open a PR for compiler_leads to review.

I'll try to stay patient for sure though. But if I'm missing a component of the process it'd be good to know before waiting for the first round of review :sweat_smile:

>拟议的新3级目标必须由编译团队成员根据这些要求进行审核和批准。 审阅者可以选择通过[重大变革提案（ MCP ）]来衡量更广泛的编译团队共识（https://forge.rust-lang.org/compiler/proposals-and-stabilization.html#how-do-i-submit-an-mcp).以及用于[推广目标]的链接稳定文档（https://forge.rust-lang.org/compiler/proposals-and-stabilization.html#promoting-targets)说明要求只是为compiler_leads打开PR以进行审核。

不过，我会尽量保持耐心。 但是，如果我缺少流程的某个组成部分，最好在等待第一轮审核之前先了解： sweat_smile:

messages.en: For anything, if you haven't heard from a reviewer in 2-3 weeks it's fine to ping or reroll
messages.zh: 对于任何问题，如果您在2-3周内没有收到审核人员的消息，则可以ping或重新滚动

messages.en: compiler-leads is a small team, there's probably some process improvement we could have there. Personally I think all new targets should require an MCP then not require a compiler-leads review
messages.zh: compiler-leads是一个小团队，我们可能会有一些流程改进。就我个人而言，我认为所有新目标都应该需要MCP ，然后不需要编译领导审核

topics.name: Checking reproducibility of rustc
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论围绕 `rustc` 及其产物的可复现构建展开，重点是如何检测和处理因构建路径、临时目录、调试信息、链接器、LLVM、并发线程（`-Zthreads`）及元数据差异导致的哈希不一致。Yocto、Debian 等发行版既关注工具链自身，也关注工具链产物的可复现性。

- **检测工具与维护方式**：PR #149888 提出的 `repro-check` 旨在自动化比较构建产物并生成详细报告。讨论过将其接入 `toolstate`、CI 阻塞任务或可失败的可选任务，但主要意见是先作为实验性、非 CI 阻塞、可在树外快速迭代的工具；Sermsity 表示愿意维护工具并协助调查问题。`diffoscope` 可提供递归差异和 HTML 报告，但速度较慢，专用工具可能更适合 `.rlib` 等对象类产物。

- **已定位或推进的具体问题**：
  - WSL 的 ext4 与 NTFS 差异最初被误判为可复现性问题，最终确认是两次构建使用了不同 commit；相同 commit 下哈希一致。
  - Windows CodeView 的 `S_OBJNAME` 会嵌入 `.rcgu.o` 的绝对输出路径，导致 `.rlib` 不一致；该行为可追溯到 LLVM/clang 的 CodeView 生成，`-fdebug-compilation-dir=.` 可使路径变为相对路径。
  - Windows MSVC 构建缺少 `/Brepro` 会导致 COFF 时间戳等差异；加入 `/Brepro` 后显著减少不匹配。
  - `compiler_builtins` 中的 compiler-rt archive 成员名和 CodeView 调试信息曾包含绝对路径；通过重新归档、使用裸文件名及相关路径处理，已使该 `.rlib` 可复现。
  - `rustc` 的随机 `invocation_temp` 后缀会进入 archive member names、`lib.rmeta-link` 以及 LLVM 的 `ObjectFilenameForDebug`，导致 `.rlib` 哈希变化；相关修复正在 PR #165202 中推进。
  - Linux 下 `std`、`rustdoc`、`clippy`、`rustfmt`、`cargo-fmt` 等在一次测试中共 83/83 个文件通过；Windows 仍有 `.exe`、`.pdb` 和部分 `.rlib` 差异需要处理。

- **路径重映射与测试结论**：`rust.remap-debuginfo = true` 比仅设置 `RUSTFLAGS` 的路径重映射更完整。现有 `remap-path-prefix-std` 测试可检查标准库 `.rlib` 是否泄漏 checkout 路径，讨论中同意扩展到 `libcore`、其他标准库 `rlib` 及 `rustc` 产物；vendored crates 使用 `/rust/deps` 重映射，测试应同时考虑 `/rustc/` 和 `/rust/deps/`。

- **仍未解决的问题**：`toolstate` 自身曾连续数月失效而无人发现，是否适合作为长期机制仍有疑虑；CI 中如何可靠、低成本地运行可复现性检查尚未最终确定。Windows 的 PDB、部分 `.exe`、CodeView/链接器路径处理，`rustdoc`/`mdbook` 偶发不确定性、BPF/LLVM bitcode、PGO 构建以及 `-Zthreads` 引起的非确定性仍需要进一步调查。

messages.en:
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/149888 introduces a new tool for checking if Rust(c) builds are reproducible. If we take such a tool in, it will have to be maintained (by t-bootstrap, most likely). For that to make sense, there would have to be some "appetite" to resolve [reproducibility bugs](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/129080) when they appear. Especially if we make it required on CI.

Do we have someone interested in that? It might also be an interesting GSoC project, for that matter.
messages.zh:
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/149888引入了一个新的工具，用于检查Rust (c)构建是否可重现。如果我们使用这样的工具，则必须对其进行维护（很可能是通过t-bootstrap ）。为此，必须有一些“胃口”来解决[可重现性错误] （https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/129080)当它们出现时。特别是如果我们在CI上要求它。

我们有人对此感兴趣吗？ 就此而言，这也可能是一个有趣的GSoC项目。

messages.en: I've been speaking to some people who work on distros/yocto and I believe they might have interest in this type of thing
messages.zh: 我一直在和一些从事发行版/yocto工作的人交谈，我相信他们可能对这类事情感兴趣

messages.en: but not sure yet, I've got a call scheduled to learn more about their needs in a week or so
messages.zh: 但我还不确定，我已经安排了一通电话，以便在一周左右的时间内进一步了解他们的需求

messages.en:
@_**davidtwco|116107** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Checking.20reproducibility.20of.20rustc/near/566227599):
```quote
I've been speaking to some people who work on distros/yocto and I believe they might have interest in this type of thing
```

they are definitely interested, but are they willing to put in the resources? in work, or even in understanding.

yocto in particular has previously aggressively patched the compiler in ways that make it hard to (heh) reproduce their bugs, because they've exposed themselves to entirely new risk categories the compiler doesn't normally allow.
messages.zh:
@_* * davidtwco | 116107 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Checking.20reproducibility.20of.20rustc/near/566227599):
```quote
I've been speaking to some people who work on distros/yocto and I believe they might have interest in this type of thing
```他们肯定感兴趣，但他们是否愿意投入资源？在工作中，甚至在理解中。

特别是yocto以前积极地修补编译器，使其难以（嘿）重现其错误，因为他们已经将自己暴露在编译器通常不允许的全新风险类别中。

messages.en: my understanding is that yocto's build system works in such a way that this makes a sort of bizarre sense: they *rely* on reproducibility for certain features of the build system. however, when they remove random hashes from rustc's output because it's not reproducible anymore, they expose themselves to various interesting sorts of bad behavior from the compiler.
messages.zh: 我的理解是， yocto的构建系统的工作方式有点奇怪：他们*依赖*构建系统的某些功能的可重现性。但是，当他们从rustc的输出中删除随机哈希时，因为它不再具有可重现性，他们会暴露于编译器中各种有趣的不良行为。

messages.en:
this means that bug reports from them lately will stall out quickly on "I'm not entirely sure where you're hitting this bug but the trace brings us through several patches that are individually questionable but combine into something incredibly bad."

I mean, it's not that big of a deal if you remove our codegen datalayout consistency checks with LLVM... if you never add custom targets, which they do.
messages.zh:
这意味着他们最近的漏洞报告会很快停滞不前，因为“我不完全确定你在哪里遇到这个漏洞，但这个痕迹让我们通过了几个单独有疑问但组合成令人难以置信的坏东西的补丁。”

我的意思是，如果您删除我们与LLVM的codegen数据布局一致性检查，这没什么大不了的……如果您从不添加自定义目标，他们会这样做。

messages.en: I've not looked into it myself but I assumed it was things like that, but will see what the Yocto developer I've got a call with brings up. Arm has some teams that work on distros/Yocto and so depending on the issues, I might be able to get some time in my team to look into them from the Rust side to help our internal teams, but not committed to anything yet, so just trying to learn more at the moment.
messages.zh: 我自己还没有研究过，但我以为是这样的，但我会看看我接到电话的Yocto开发人员提出了什么。ARM有一些团队在开发发行版/Yocto ，因此根据问题的不同，我可能会在团队中抽出一些时间从Rust方面研究它们，以帮助我们的内部团队，但还没有承诺任何事情，所以现在只是想了解更多信息。

messages.en: @**Jakub Beránek** how do you feel about using toolstate for this? that doesn't impose too much additional maintenance burden, but it makes it much easier to tell when reproducibility has regressed if someone wants to fix it
messages.zh: @ * * Jakub Beránek * *您对此使用工具状态的感受如何？这不会带来太多的额外维护负担，但如果有人想要修复它，它可以更容易地判断可重复性是否已经退化

messages.en: we only *really* care about reproducibility on each 6-week release, which lines up well with how toolstate works
messages.zh: 我们只*真正*关心每个6周版本的可重复性，这与toolstate的工作原理非常吻合

messages.en: I don't think that the system for testing this is that important, tbh. I think that we can easily make this be blocking in CI without too many issues. my question was more about "who cares about reproducibility" and "who would be willing to go fix it if it breaks"
messages.zh: 我不认为测试这个的系统是那么重要， tbh。我认为我们可以轻松地在CI中阻止它，而不会出现太多问题。我的问题更多的是关于“谁关心可重复性”和“如果它坏了，谁愿意去修复它”

messages.en:
do we only care about rustc being reproducible or also about rustc building things other than itself in a reproducible way?
do we know how much code coverage we are getting during bootstrap is? it more like 40% or more like 70%? 

while fuzzing around reproducibility a bit, I saw cases (mostly related to -Zthreads) where a single test would have checksum A 70% of the time, checksum B 20% of the time and checksum C 10% of the time, indicating that CI might not immediately "break" if something broke reproducibility  
of course building the entire compiler has more coverage than a 20 lines testcase :) 
but I would be worried that we might get a bunch of "spurious" looking reproducibility failures which would be very hard to track down
messages.zh:
我们只关心rustc的可重复性，还是也关心rustc以可重复的方式构建除自身之外的东西？
我们是否知道我们在引导期间获得了多少代码覆盖率？它更像是40 ％或更像是70 ％ ？在模糊重现性的同时，我看到了一些情况（主要与-Zthreads有关） ，其中单个测试的校验和A有70 ％的时间，校验和B有20 ％的时间，校验和C有10 ％的时间，这表明如果有什么东西破坏了重现性， CI可能不会立即“中断”  
当然，构建整个编译器比20行测试用例具有更多的覆盖范围:)但我担心我们可能会遇到一堆“虚假”的再现性故障，这很难追踪到

messages.en: I think you have only highlighted the importance of identifying who if anyone is going to be addressing reproducibility issues.
messages.zh: 我认为您只是强调了确定谁将解决可重复性问题的重要性。

messages.en: speaking for Ferrous Systems: we would like to have a reproducible compiler, but we can't commit to maintaining the tool or fixing reproducibility bugs. we might be able to maintain the tool itself in the future once we've had a chance to use it and verify it works for our use cases, but we don't want to be on the hook for fixing the bugs it discovers.
messages.zh: 代表Ferrous Systems ：我们希望有一个可重现的编译器，但我们不能承诺维护工具或修复可重现性错误。一旦我们有机会使用它并验证它适用于我们的用例，我们就可以在将来维护工具本身，但我们不想成为修复它发现的错误的钩子。

messages.en: speaking for myself: i really do think that toolstate will make this much easier. i think there's value to recording what bugs exist even if they don't get fixed right away.
messages.zh: 代表我自己说：我真的认为工具状态会让这更容易。我认为记录存在的错误是有价值的，即使它们没有立即得到修复。

messages.en: recently we found out that toolstate itself was broken for >6 months and no-one noticed, lol
messages.zh: 最近我们发现toolstate本身被破坏了> 6个月，没有人注意到，哈哈

messages.en: no one is using toolstate currently except for the books!
messages.zh: 目前没有人使用toolstate ，除了书籍！

messages.en: and the books themselves have very little maintenance time
messages.zh: 书籍本身的维护时间很短

messages.en: would that change if we added rustc to it?
messages.zh: 如果我们添加rustc ，这种情况会改变吗？

messages.en: @**matthiaskrgr** yocto's reports suggest they care about reproducibility of the artifacts we generate, as well, *but* I think there's an obvious tiering of the concern. making it so rustc can always be built with the same bytes is the starting point.
messages.zh: @ * * matthiaskrgr * * yocto的报告表明，他们也关心我们生成的工件的可重复性， *但是*我认为这个问题有明显的分层。让rustc始终可以用相同的字节构建是起点。

messages.en: i'm not saying you will suddenly get more people to maintain toolstate, i'm saying that this gives the people who want reproducible builds a) a place to collaborate upstream rather than patching downstream, and b) an incentive to fix toolstate rather than running their own reproducible builds downstream
messages.zh: 我并不是说您会突然让更多的人维护工具状态，我是说这给了想要可重现构建的人a ）上游协作的地方，而不是下游修补， b ）修复工具状态的激励，而不是下游运行自己的可重现构建

messages.en: I don't think that they care about "building with 2+ threads reduces reproducibility" though.
messages.zh: 不过，我认为他们并不关心「使用2个以上的线程构建会降低可重复性」。

messages.en: and that's useful *even if* toolstate remains broken for a few months
messages.zh: 即使* toolstate在几个月内仍然损坏，这也是非常有用的*

messages.en: I think they care about "it's possible to set the compiler so it can be made reproducible" more.
messages.zh: 我认为他们更关心“可以设置编译器，使其可重现”。

messages.en:
@_**jyn|232545** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Checking.20reproducibility.20of.20rustc/near/566422446):
```quote
and that's useful *even if* toolstate remains broken for a few months
```

wouldn't that be better served by a CI job that runs on auto builds, but is allowed to be red? toolstate seems like a maintenance burden to me, and I would love to get rid of it one day
messages.zh:
@_* * jyn | 232545 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Checking.20reproducibility.20of.20rustc/near/566422446):
```quote
and that's useful *even if* toolstate remains broken for a few months
```在自动构建上运行但被允许为红色的CI作业不是更好吗？ toolstate对我来说似乎是一个维护负担，我希望有一天能摆脱它

messages.en: sure, that seems like a separate question though? i don't care if this uses toolstate in particular, just the idea of an optional job
messages.zh: 当然，这似乎是一个单独的问题？我不在乎这是否特别使用工具状态，只是一个可选工作的想法

messages.en:
@_**workingjubilee|281757** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Checking.20reproducibility.20of.20rustc/near/566422470):
```quote
I think they care about "it's possible to set the compiler so it can be made reproducible" more.
```

this is because yocto, afaict, uses a fairly "totalizing" build system for many elements, which means that having to pass `-Cwork-like-yocto-expects` would be very normal to them.
messages.zh:
@_* * workingjubilee | 281757 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Checking.20reproducibility.20of.20rustc/near/566422470):
```quote
I think they care about "it's possible to set the compiler so it can be made reproducible" more.
```这是因为yocto ， afaict ，对许多元素使用相当“总计”的构建系统，这意味着必须通过`-Cwork-like-yocto-expects`对他们来说是非常正常的。

messages.en: If that means they always have to set the thread count to 1, that's probably fine by them tooo.
messages.zh: 如果这意味着他们总是必须将线程数设置为1 ，那么他们也可以这样做。

messages.en:
hi! i’m testing reproducible builds on windows/wsl as part of exploring [#129080](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/129080)

i noticed that `x.py build library` produces different hashes when built in a normal wsl directory (ext4) vs a windows-mounted directory (`/mnt/c`, ntfs), even with 
`RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$PWD=/rust".`

two linux/ext4 builds produced identical hashes. `diffoscope` shows differences in internal symbol hashes.
is this a known limitation of windows/ntfs builds, or something still worth investigating?
messages.zh:
嗨！我正在测试windows/wsl上的可重现构建，作为探索的一部分[# 129080] （https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/129080)我注意到`x.py build library`在普通wsl目录（ ext4 ）中构建时与在windows装载的目录中构建时产生不同的哈希（`/mnt/c`， ntfs ） ，即使`RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$PWD=/rust".`两个linux/ext4版本生成了相同的哈希。`diffoscope`显示内部符号哈希的差异。
这是否是windows/ntfs构建的已知限制，还是仍然值得研究的问题？

messages.en: If it is a known limitation, there should be an A-reproducibility issue about it. If there is no such issue, I think it makes sense for you to write it. Having the symbols that are changing is a solid start to the issue discussion.
messages.zh: 如果这是一个已知的限制，则应该存在A重现性问题。如果没有这样的问题，我认为你写它是有道理的。让符号发生变化是问题讨论的坚实开端。

messages.en: Is the difference because of different `-Cmetadata`? If so this is either a cargo or bootstrap issue.
messages.zh: 是不是因为不同`-Cmetadata`?如果是，这要么是货物问题，要么是引导问题。

messages.en: In any case have you tried `rust.remap-debuginfo = true` in `bootstrap.toml` instead of setting `RUSTFLAGS`?
messages.zh: 无论如何，您是否尝试过`rust.remap-debuginfo = true` 在 `bootstrap.toml`而不是设置`RUSTFLAGS`?

messages.en: Using `rust.remap-debuginfo` also ensures that rustc itself knows about the correct path to remap back the standard library sources to the on-disk location of the rust-src component.
messages.zh: 使用`rust.remap-debuginfo`还确保rustc本身知道将标准库源重新映射回rust-src组件的磁盘位置的正确路径。

messages.en:
thanks for the pointers, i haven't tried `rust.remap-debuginfo = true` yet,
i have not explicitly checked whether the differences are due to `-Cmetadata`. 
i’ll rerun the experiment using `rust.remap-debuginfo` and see if that eliminates the divergence, and also check whether metadata differs between the two builds.

i’ll report back once i’ve tested these.
messages.zh:
谢谢你的提示，我还没有尝试过`rust.remap-debuginfo = true`然而，
我没有明确检查差异是否归因于`-Cmetadata`. 
我将重新运行实验，使用`rust.remap-debuginfo`看看这是否消除了分歧，并检查两个构建之间的元数据是否不同。

一旦我测试了这些，我会报告。

makes sense, elf stores only the file name while CodeView includes full path. 
i wanted to ask whether embedding the full object path in CodeView `S_OBJNAME` on windows is considered expected behavior, or if rustc should aim to avoid or remap this for `.rlib` reproducibility when `-Zremap-cwd-prefix` is used.
messages.zh:
@_* * bjorn3 | 133247 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Checking.20reproducibility.20of.20rustc/near/568245523):
```quote
On ELF there is a filename symbol in every object file, but that only stores the filename, not the full path.
```有道理， ELF仅存储文件名，而CodeView包含完整路径。 
我想知道是否在CodeView中嵌入完整的对象路径`S_OBJNAME`在窗口上被认为是预期的行为，或者如果rustc应该旨在避免或重新映射`.rlib`再现性，当`-Zremap-cwd-prefix`被使用。

messages.en: here im mostly looking at path-independent reproducibility (e.g. changing build directories with `-Zremap-cwd-prefix`), where the object path in `S_OBJNAME` currently isn’t remapped like source paths are, leading to `.rlib` differences.
messages.zh: 在这里，我主要关注与路径无关的可重现性（例如，使用`-Zremap-cwd-prefix`） ，其中对象路径在`S_OBJNAME`当前没有像源路径那样重新映射，导致`.rlib`差值

messages.en: https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/definition/ is what most distros  settled on. in Debian we generate [buildinfo](https://manpages.debian.org/testing/dpkg-dev/deb-buildinfo.5.en.html) files when building the package, and there is a [snapshot archive of the repositories](https://snapshot.debian.org/) that can be used to re-create the build environment recorded in those buildinfo files to reproduce the build. it is one of the goals of the current Debian release cycle to forbid regressions ins reproducibility and get the list of remaining non-reproducible packages down to a small set.
messages.zh: https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/definition/是大多数发行版所依赖的。在Debian中，我们生成[buildinfo] （https://manpages.debian.org/testing/dpkg-dev/deb-buildinfo.5.en.html)文件，并且有一个[仓库的快照存档] （https://snapshot.debian.org/)可用于重新创建这些buildinfo文件中记录的构建环境以重现构建。当前Debian发布周期的目标之一是禁止回归不可重现性，并将剩余的不可重现软件包列表缩小到一小部分。

messages.en: there is a separate, earlier effort that tried to vary the environment (while keeping the build dependencies frozen), that included things like build path randomizing between the two builds: https://tests.reproducible-builds.org/debian/reproducible.html
messages.zh: 有一个单独的早期尝试尝试改变环境（同时保持构建依赖关系冻结） ，其中包括两个构建之间的构建路径随机化：https://tests.reproducible-builds.org/debian/reproducible.html

messages.en: that effort helped with finding, classifying and eventually fixing a lot of common sources of indeterminism
messages.zh: 这一努力有助于发现、分类并最终修复许多常见的不确定性来源，

messages.en:
i was checking whether this behavior is rustc-specific or coming from LLVM, compiling a minimal C file with `clang-cl /Z7` and dumping CodeView with `llvm-readobj --codeview` shows the same `S_OBJNAME` behavior, with the full object output path embedded in the record (`cout1` vs `cout2`). 
this could suggest the path leakage comes from LLVM’s CodeView emission rather than rustc logic, and differs from ELF targets where typically only the filename is stored.
messages.zh:
我正在检查此行为是rustc特定的还是来自LLVM ，使用`clang-cl /Z7`并转储CodeView ，`llvm-readobj --codeview`显示相同`S_OBJNAME`行为，将完整的对象输出路径嵌入到记录中（`cout1`对比`cout2`). 
这可能表明路径泄漏来自LLVM的CodeView发射而不是rustc逻辑，并且与通常仅存储文件名的ELF目标不同。

messages.en:
Thanks everyone for the thoughtful discussion and feedback.
(https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/149888)

I want to clarify my intent with this tool. I’m not proposing it as a CI-blocking change or as something that must always be enabled. The main goal of repro-check is to make it easier to investigate and understand reproducibility issues when people want to look into them, rather than to gate development.

I’m happy to take responsibility for maintaining the tool itself and to help with investigations by running it, narrowing down differences, and collaborating with the relevant teams when issues are found.

I’d be very comfortable treating this as an experimental, non-CI tool initially, with the understanding that it can be re-evaluated or removed later if it doesn’t see enough use or turns out to be too costly to maintain.

I’m open to following whatever next steps the maintainers think make the most sense here.
messages.zh:
感谢大家的深思熟虑的讨论和反馈。
(https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/149888)我想用这个工具来澄清我的意图。 我并不是建议将其作为阻止CI的变更或必须始终启用的东西。 再检查的主要目标是在人们想要调查时更容易调查和理解可重复性问题，而不是入门开发。我很乐意负责维护工具本身，并通过运行工具、缩小差异以及在发现问题时与相关团队合作来帮助进行调查。

最初，我非常乐意将其视为一种实验性的非CI工具，但有一项谅解，即如果没有足够的使用或维护成本太高，可以稍后重新评估或删除它。我愿意遵循维护人员认为在这里最有意义的任何后续步骤。

update on #129117 confirmed after multiple clean rebuilds, `stage1 std` deterministically crashes at core on `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with `0xc0000005.`
`stage1` compiler builds fine.
the failing invocation includes `+crt-static`, `prefer-dynamic`, `split-debuginfo=packed`, and MIR inlining; disabling `prefer-dynamic` avoids the crash. this lines up with the previous `.rlib` nondeterminism traced to CodeView `S_OBJNAME` embedding output paths.
what would be the best next step here?

while investigating the differing hashes on x86_64-linux-gnu, found that
`anon.*.llvm.<hash>` non-determinism extends to `librustc_driver` under default bootstrap settings, not only `rustdoc` from #126976. 
the anon symbol prefix is stable across builds but the llvm suffix differs, consistent with build path leaking into thin-local-lto.
messages.zh:
在调查x86_64-linux-gnu上的不同哈希时，发现`anon.*.llvm.<hash>`不确定性延伸到`librustc_driver`在默认引导设置下，不仅`rustdoc`来自＃ 126976。 
anon符号前缀在构建过程中是稳定的，但llvm后缀不同，这与构建路径泄漏到thin-local-lto一致。

messages.en: also, ci-llvm include paths from the build workspace are also leaking into the binary, which seems like a distinct remapping gap similar to the OUT_DIR issue fixed earlier.
messages.zh: 此外，来自构建工作区的ci-llvm include路径也会泄漏到二进制文件中，这似乎是一个明显的重新映射间隙，类似于之前修复的OUT_DIR问题。

messages.en:
picking up where i left off, `llvm-config --cxxflags` emits absolute `-I` paths pointing into the build workspace, (e.g. `build/repro_workspace/build-a/.../ci-llvm/include/...`) which was getting embedded in the `librustc_driver` via c++ debug info. 
`remap-debuginfo = true` doesn't cover this as `rustc_debuginfo_map` only applies to rustc and not to the c++ compiler building `rustc_llvm` 

approach: passed `-fdebug-prefix-map` flags from `rustc_debuginfo_map` to `cc::Build` in `rustc_llvm/build.rs` .

this is the report: 
[repro_report.html](/user_uploads/4715/JAUhYKIhGGiHNliF0Ow4pBAX/repro_report.html)

> Hey, I encountered a PR that doesn't change anything relevant (only tests) but the artifacts are different and compile time, too: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/156044

That is probably just the version string changing as that includes the commit hash. The version string is intentionally hashed into symbol names to prevent ABI causing conflicts when including libraries compiled by different rustc versions. This does however affect symbol order (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/152910), which in turn can affect performance. And of course it causes hashmap order to differ.
messages.zh: >嘿，我遇到了一个PR ，它不会更改任何相关内容（仅测试） ，但工件也不同，而且编译时间也不同：https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/156044这可能只是版本字符串更改，因为其中包括提交哈希。 版本字符串被有意散列到符号名称中，以防止ABI在包含由不同rustc版本编译的库时引起冲突。 然而，这会影响符号顺序（https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/152910),这反过来又会影响性能。当然，这会导致哈希映射顺序不同。

messages.en:
reduced this further outside rust.
minimal repro:
```
clang-cl /c /Z7 t.c /Fo:a\t.obj
clang-cl /c /Z7 t.c /Fo:b\t.obj
```

`llvm-readobj --codeview` shows
```
- ObjectName: C:\rust3\a\t.obj
+ ObjectName: C:\rust3\b\t.obj
```
inside the S_OBJNAME CodeView record, and the resulting object hashes **differ**.

i also tried `/clang:-ffile-prefix-map=C:\rust3=.`but the `S_OBJNAME` path is still emitted as the absolute `/Fo` output path and continues to be different between the two builds.
`compiler_builtins.rlib` mismatch appears to reduce to a clang/LLVM CodeView issue.

- ObjectName: C:\rust3\a\t.obj
+ ObjectName: C:\rust3\b\t.obj
```s_OBJNAME CodeView记录中，生成的对象哈希* *不同* *。

我也试过`/clang:-ffile-prefix-map=C:\rust3=.`但是...`S_OBJNAME`路径仍然作为绝对路径发出，`/Fo`输出路径，并且在两个构建之间继续不同。`compiler_builtins.rlib`不匹配似乎减少到clang/LLVM CodeView问题。

messages.en:
clang's `addDebugObjectName()` converts the object output paths to absolute paths and emits them via `-object-file-name`. these paths are then embedded into `S_OBJNAME` by llvm's CodeView backend. 
existing `-ffile-prefix-map` / `-fdebug-prefix-map` does not remap `-object-file-name`, 
so differences leak into debug info, making it non-reproducible.
messages.zh:
叮叮的`addDebugObjectName()`将对象输出路径转换为绝对路径，并通过`-object-file-name`.然后将这些路径嵌入到`S_OBJNAME`llvm的CodeView后端。 
现有`-ffile-prefix-map` / `-fdebug-prefix-map`不重新映射`-object-file-name`, 
因此差异会泄露到调试信息中，使其不可重现。

messages.en: the r-b.o folks now basically do both kinds of testing in parallel - test *with* intentionally added variance to shake out issues, and test with a build env as close to the original to find potential supply chain issues (in built/distributed packages)
messages.zh: r-b.o人员现在基本上并行进行两种测试-测试*与*故意添加方差以解决问题，并使用构建环境进行测试，尽可能接近原始环境以发现潜在的供应链问题（在内置/分布式包中）

messages.en: since at distro scale, the first is basically a seemingly never ending battle. the latter is within reach (Debian forky, the next stable release sits at >98% reproduced packages atm - there's a few hundred packages left that have issues)
messages.zh: 因为在发行版规模上，第一个基本上是一场看似永无止境的战斗。后者触手可及（ Debian forky ，下一个稳定版本位于> 98 ％的再现包atm -还有几百个包有问题）

is there any general idea of how we want to tackle [this](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/242791-t-infra/topic/meeting.202026-07-20/near/611674498)? 
i have been working on a repro-crate, & it got me thinking on its integration. 
(a) if something like this was ever to get used in ci, would we want ci to depend on external crates at all? 
(b) or maybe vendor it.
(c) writing a ci job from scratch seems to be plausible because we can scope tight, avoiding the "800 LOC" situation.
curious if any of them is on the table.
messages.zh:
我们希望如何解决[这个]是否有任何大致的想法（https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/242791-t-infra/topic/meeting.202026-07-20/near/611674498)?我一直在研究一个复制箱，这让我想到了它的整合。

（ c ）从头开始编写ci作业似乎是合理的，因为我们可以缩小范围，避免“800 LOC”的情况。
好奇他们中是否有人在桌子上。

messages.en:
a separate crate probably makes sense if it is for general Rust programs. if it needs integration with bootstrap or is otherwise special-cased to how rustc it built, then it would make sense to live in-tree, *provided that we have someone to maintain it*

to clarify, having 800 lines of code in the repo is not a problem. but it should be demonstrated that it is useful, and it should be ideally merged incrementally in smaller chunks
messages.zh:
如果是针对一般的Rust程序，则单独的crate可能是有意义的。如果它需要与bootstrap集成，或者其他特殊情况下如何构建rustc ，那么生活在树中是有意义的， *前提是我们有人维护它*

澄清一下，在存储库中有800行代码不是问题。但应该证明它是有用的，并且它应该理想地以较小的块逐渐合并

messages.en:
is there a way to force it to use a specific known-good upstream commit's llvm artifacts? 
e.g. via a config override, rather than relying on the (seemingly unreliable-on-forks) auto-detection?
messages.zh:
有没有办法强制它使用特定的已知良好的上游提交llvm工件？ 
例如，通过配置覆盖，而不是依靠（看似不可靠的分叉）自动检测？

messages.zh: 不是真的，没有修补代码。但是如果你有一个针对上游提交打开的PR ，它应该只是工作

messages.en: pushing to main on the fork will break it
messages.zh: 将叉子推到主叉子上会损坏叉子

或者不需要做任何事情，无论如何它都会重新触发？

messages.en: not sure if I understand, but running anything on your fork's CI of course won't upload anything to our S3 servers :P so it won't be cached further
messages.zh: 不确定我是否理解，但是在您的分叉的CI上运行任何内容当然不会将任何内容上传到我们的S3服务器: P ，因此它不会被进一步缓存

messages.en: you have to downloaded the LLVM builds that are produced from the upstream CI if you want caching
messages.zh: 如果需要缓存，则必须下载从上游CI生成的LLVM构建

i went a bit deeper into the S_OBJNAME issue and found that clang actually has a dedicated `-object-file-name` option for controlling the filename used in debug info.

i tested it directly with clang-cl:
```
/FoC:\...\a\absvdi2.o
    -> S_OBJNAME = C:\...\a\absvdi2.o
```
```
/FoC:\...\b\absvdi2.o -object-file-name=absvdi2.o
    -> S_OBJNAME =
```
so the flag surely reaches the relevant `CodeView` machinery, although interestingly clang emits an empty `S_OBJNAME` rather than the bare filename in this case.

while tracing where this comes from in rustc, i also found that rustc already explicitly passes an `output_obj_file` through `TargetMachineFactoryConfig`, with the [comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/main/compiler/rustc_codegen_ssa/src/back/write.rs#L294) that it's used so LLVM can emit the `CodeView S_OBJNAME` record. that gets passed through `LLVMRustCreateTargetMachine` into LLVM's `ObjectFilenameForDebug`.

i'm now following that rustc -> LLVM path to see exactly where/how `ObjectFilenameForDebug` is consumed, and whether the existing rustc path-remapping machinery can/should be applied there instead of fixing this specifically in compiler-builtins/cc-rs

messages.en:
found another `.rlib` reproducibility issue while testing compiler-rt

rustc's random `invocation_temp` suffix ends up in archive member names and `lib.rmeta-link` (from #154861), so identical object bytes can produce different `.rlib` hashes.
tried stable archive member names while keeping temp filenames unchanged. rebuilt stage1 and got byte-identical `.rlib`s with 1 and 16 CGUs, including with `-Cdebuginfo=2` (incremental off).

haven't pushed yet

update: also found that rustc passes the absolute temporary object path to LLVM's `ObjectFilenameForDebug`, which ends up in CodeView `S_OBJNAME`.
tried using the stable archive member name there too. with both changes, the final `.rlib` is now identical

fixing in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/165202
messages.zh:
找到另一个`.rlib`测试compiler-rt时的可重复性问题

rustc的随机`invocation_temp`后缀以存档成员名称结束，`lib.rmeta-link`（来自# 154861 ） ，因此相同的对象字节可以产生不同的`.rlib`哈希值。
尝试稳定的存档成员名称，同时保持临时文件名不变。重建阶段1并获得字节相同`.rlib`具有1和16个CGU的，包括`-Cdebuginfo=2`（增量关闭）。

尚未推送

update:还发现rustc将绝对临时对象路径传递给LLVM的`ObjectFilenameForDebug`，它最终会出现在CodeView中`S_OBJNAME`.
也尝试在那里使用稳定的存档成员名称。经过两次更改，最终`.rlib`现在是相同的

topics.name: Some outdated comments and misleading names in compiler code
topics.name_zh: 编译器代码中的一些过时的注释和误导性名称
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：qouteall 认为编译器代码中存在误导性的命名和过时注释，给不熟悉 compiler code 的读者造成理解障碍，计划通过 PR 改进注释。
- **主要观点**：Zalathar 认为其中不少质疑较弱；teor 支持修正明显错误的文档，但认为大规模修改基本正确的名称可能不值得带来代码变动。qouteall 澄清，重点不是侵入性较强的重命名，而是通过注释解释名称与实际含义的偏差，并可逐项讨论。
- **具体澄清与方案**：
  - `GccLinker` 指使用 GCC（或命令行兼容的 clang）作为 linker driver；即使 `uses_lld` 为 `true`，仍由 GCC 作为 driver，只是让其调用 `ld.lld`。
  - `OutputType::Exe` 在 `define_output_types!` 中表示正常编译 crate，而不单纯表示 executable；有人建议改名为 `OutputType::Link`，以匹配 `--emit link`。
  - `AttrTokenStream` 和 `LazyAttrTokenStream` 的含义并非“attribute tokens 的 stream”，相关问题已通过 PR 165022 移除。
- **结论与未决事项**：对明显错误注释的更新基本得到认可；对于仅名称可能引起困惑的情况，更倾向补充解释性注释而非重命名。`OutputType::Exe` 是否改名，以及其他条目是否值得修改，聊天中尚未形成统一结论。

messages.en:
> `GccLinker`: it's not limited to gcc linker. It can represent gcc-flavor linkers. lld is also treated as `GccLinker` but with field `uses_lld` be true.

GccLinker refers to using GCC (or something cli compatible like clang) as linker driver. If uses_lld is true, then GCC will still be used as linker driver. We just tell GCC to use ld.lld as actual linker rather than for example ld.bfd (which is not a part of GCC, but a part of binutils).
messages.zh:
>`GccLinker`：它不限于gcc链接器。它可以表示gcc-flavor接头。lld也被视为`GccLinker`但带有字段`uses_lld`是真的。

GccLinker是指使用GCC （或cli兼容的东西，如clang ）作为链接器驱动程序。 如果uses_lld为true ，则GCC仍将用作链接器驱动程序。 我们只是告诉GCC使用ld.lld作为实际链接器，而不是例如ld.bfd （它不是GCC的一部分，而是binutils的一部分）。

messages.en:
> `OutputType::Exe` (in `define_output_types!` macro) it doesn't mean executable. It means compiling crate normally.

Perhaps it should be called `OutputType::Link` to match the cli flag (`--emit link`)
messages.zh:
>`OutputType::Exe` 在 `define_output_types!`宏）并不意味着可执行文件。 这意味着正常编译板条箱。

或许应该称之为`OutputType::Link`匹配cli标志（`--emit link`)

messages.en:

Removed by https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/165022
messages.zh:

topics.name: crate disambiguator drops leading zeroes in demangling
topics.name_zh: crate 消歧义器在反修饰名时会去掉前导零
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：v0 demangling 在输出 crate disambiguator（crate hash）时没有进行零填充，导致部分 16 位十六进制值显示为 15 位；问题最先在 x86_64-gnu-gcc CI 中暴露，但并非 `rustc_codegen_gcc` 特有。
- **触发条件**：只有特定 UI 测试使用 v0 demangling，并通过自定义 normalization regex 要求恰好 16 个十六进制字符时才会失败；每次 crate hash 变化时大约有 `1/16` 的概率出现该情况。此前测试覆盖不足，且 compiletest 对 crate disambiguator 的通用匹配通常不要求长度。
- **重要观点与方案**：`LowerHex` 在未指定 padding 时本来就会省略前导零，因此问题主要在 `rustc-demangle` 的 v0 实现依赖外部 `Formatter` 设置宽度和零填充。已提出修复 `rustc-demangle` 的 PR，并将相关的 splat legacy demangling 修复拆分为独立 PR；不应通过修改 `rustc_codegen_gcc` 解决。
- **当前结论与未解决问题**：已确认这是 `rustc-demangle` 的 bug，修复 PR 仍在等待 review；另有 `rustc-demangle` release PR，尚未决定是否应在发布前合并该修复。

messages.en:

Until we fix it, I think ~~that job~~ all jobs will fail on roughly 1/16 of ~~PRs~~ code changes to a few specific UI tests.

messages.en:
The CRATE_HASH regex in compiletest doesn't care about the length, so it's only triggered in specific circumstances:
- the compiletest regex doesn't match
  - compiletest seems to match the UI test "crate" disambiguator reliably, but not other positions like Type<alloc[hex chars]::Box>
- the UI test uses v0 demangling
- the UI test uses a custom normalization regex that expects exactly 16 hex characters
- the crate disambiguator is 15 characters (happens on 1/16 changes to each crate hash)

It's possible it was dismissed as a spurious failure, and then a subsequent rollup modified the crate hash so it had 16 characters again. It's also possible no tests existed that triggered it until I added this line:
https://github.com/teor2345/rust/blob/511d2920c48fac1afc67b628a5b5125c880f243b/tests/ui/splat/splat-mangling.rs#L185

It's also possible we changed LowerHex formatting to omit leading zeroes at some point. Or omit a single leading zero. (If it was only omitting leading zero *bytes*, then it would only happen in 1/256 changes to the crate hash.)
