topics.name: `trivial_consts` without MIR
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：nnethercote 提出一个 draft PR（#165112），让 `trivial_consts` 不再构建 MIR，而是直接基于 HIR 工作，初步观察到性能提升；但该代码仍需清理。
- **相关性与区分**：讨论提到 `trivial_consts` 可能存在争议，以及“direct consts”和 const generics 是否相关。Boxy 认为，const generics 的关联主要在于某些常量出于语义原因目前没有 HIR/MIR body；但将这种机制复用于 `trivial_consts` 优化并不可行，因此两者基本是正交的。
- **已有方案与历史背景**：此前曾讨论过使用类似 GCA 的 heuristic 优化 `trivial_consts`，也尝试过在 AST 层面判断，但效果不太理想。`#149468` 和 “Non-Type Trivial Consts” 相关讨论被认为与当前问题不太相关。
- **仍未解决的问题**：需要进一步厘清没有任何 body 的常量机制与基于 HIR 的 `trivial_consts` 检查之间的关系，以及该优化是否会引发争议。Ben Kimock 看过现有实现后认为代码较难理解，正在继续了解相关背景；目前没有形成明确结论。

messages.en:

It feels like I've wandered into a tricky area and I want to do a general vibe check before spending more time on this. Any thoughts?

topics.name: `become` failing compilation inside `cfg(feature = "...")`
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`become` 即使写在关闭的 `cfg(feature = "...")` 分支中，仍会导致编译失败。这是预期行为，因为相关语法会在宏展开（expansion）之前被拒绝；并非编译器 bug。
- **可行方案**：可以将使用 `become` 的代码放入单独的模块或文件中进行条件编译，也可以对宏本身使用 `cfg`。讨论者确认拆分到独立模块后可以正常工作。
- **性能观察**：在 Verilog 字节码解释器中用显式尾调用替代字节码求值循环，初步测试约提升 8%；在更快 CPU、`codegen-units=1` 和设置 `target-cpu` 后，墙钟时间提升约 35.5%。`rust-preserve-none` 及枚举判别值优化也引发了代码生成讨论；相关优化问题可能是 LLVM 的 missed optimization，建议提交 LLVM issue，期间可使用 `transmute`。
- **`become` 设计方向**：讨论认为仅依赖特殊调用约定（如 `extern "rust-tail"`）会带来可移植性问题；有人希望同时提供一种可移植、即使效率较低的尾递归保证，用于避免递归栈溢出。另一方向则是面向解释器等场景的、目标平台相关且更高效的 `extern "tail"`/`rust-tail`。
- **实现方案与进展**：有人提出将 `become` 转换为循环或 trampoline，处理自递归及互递归；讨论涉及 MIR shim、`ControlFlow`、函数参数打包以及函数指针支持。对于互递归是否需要强连通分量分析、如何表达带参数的 continuation 等仍有疑问。Folkert de Vries 最后提供了该思路的 PoC PR（#165044），但说明仍需完善并处理边界情况。

messages.en:
Question / observation? Does rust-preserve-none block a bunch of optimizations from LLVM? Looking at the codegen, I am frankly a bit surprised at what it is doing, which it is getting right without the rust-preserve-none.

For instance, it turned an `match` statement mapping from discriminant to enum repr (which is just a mov) into a jump table. It doesn't do this in the normal evaluation loop. It also doesn't seem to inline almost any functions not marked with `inline(always)`. Fixing these codegen issues manually, led to a 20% speedup and a 8% respectively.
messages.zh:
问题/观察？ rust-preserve-none是否阻止了LLVM的一系列优化？ 看着codegen ，坦率地说，我对它的作用有点惊讶，它在没有防锈保护的情况下是正确的。

例如，它变成了`match`将判别式映射到枚举repr （这只是一个mov ）的语句映射到跳转表中。它不会在正常评估循环中执行此操作。它似乎也没有内联几乎所有未标记的函数`inline(always)`。手动修复这些codegen问题，分别导致20%和8%的加速。

messages.zh: 如果您的小函数优化不佳，那么这将会有所帮助

wanna review an LLVM PR that implements `tailcc` `byval` for `aarch64` lol https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/206718? 

Using `become` with just `extern "Rust"` turns out to have really hard portability questions. The current idea is to focus on `extern "tail"` instead, which we specify a big vaguely as "do whatever makes tail calls efficient" and is explicitly target-specific (like e.g. `asm!`)

but it would be neat if at least `aarch64` also supported it, LLVM 23 will have good support on x86_64 (as in, I've found no further issues with it so far)
messages.zh:
想审查实施LLVM PR`tailcc` `byval`针对`aarch64`大笑https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/206718?使用`become`只需`extern "Rust"`事实证明，有非常困难的可移植性问题。目前的想法是专注于`extern "tail"`相反，我们模糊地将其指定为“do whatever makes tail calls efficient” ，并明确针对特定目标（例如，`asm!`)

但如果至少`aarch64`也支持它， LLVM 23将在x86_64上获得良好的支持（例如，到目前为止，我没有发现任何进一步的问题）

messages.en: I remember you mentioning something at RustNL about maybe making it a MIR (or one of the other Rust IRs) concept. Essentially guaranteeing it by using gotos. Is that completely off the table because it is too complex?
messages.zh: 我记得你在RustNL提到过将其作为一个MIR （或其他Rust IR之一）概念。基本上通过使用gotos来保证它。这是否因为过于复杂而完全不在考虑范围之内？

messages.en: there is an approach somewhere, but the issue with it really is that even in the best case, it's not what true users of tail calls want: they want the extra registers for passing arguments
messages.zh: 在某个地方有一种方法，但它的问题在于，即使在最好的情况下，它也不是真正的尾调用用户想要的：他们需要额外的寄存器来传递参数

messages.en: like I suspect you get some good use out of `preserve-none`, `extern "tail"` is supposed to be that and more (lifting the same-signature restriction)
messages.zh: 我怀疑你可以很好地利用`preserve-none`, `extern "tail"`应该是这样和更多（解除相同的签名限制）

@_**Gijs Burghoorn|644446** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60become.60.20failing.20compilation.20inside.20.60cfg.28feature.20.3D.20.22.2E.2E.2E.22.29.60/near/610901509):
```quote
Essentially guaranteeing it by using gotos. Is that completely off the table because it is too complex?
```

Personally, at least, I really want the answer to be "here's the subset of `become` that we can always do so you can write at least basic tail-recursive loops if you like that better than `for`/`loop` in some situation".

But that will need to be somewhat restricted.  That's ok, though!  If someone could find a reasonable set of restrictions that we can actually implement, great -- it intentionally wouldn't support the tricky things like the interpreter tricks.

I just don't want to [edit: only] ship "well we have `become` but only with a weird calling convention so you shouldn't use it if you care about portability".  I want at least "yes, you can write your functional programming TCE homework in portable rust".
messages.zh:
@_* * Gijs Burghoorn | 644446 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60become.60.20failing.20compilation.20inside.20.60cfg.28feature.20.3D.20.22.2E.2E.2E.22.29.60/near/610901509):
```quote

messages.en:
It'd be really good to avoid needing SCC for this, because that works poorly with queries and such.  (Notably even inlining doesn't use SCC, and that's sorta the poster child for obvious place that the SCC would be good.)

I was thinking that you can probably avoid the SCC because all you care about are functions that themselves use `become` -- if I mutally-recurse through something where one of the steps *isn't* `become` that doesn't need to work well.

So maybe:
- For anything using `become`, we always include the MIR in the rlib
- We used that MIR to on-demand emit a shim version of the MIR that (rather than actually making a tail call) returns `ControlFlow<T, fn()>` instead of `T` where the `fn` is the shim of the callee.
  - Hmm, that kinda wants a recursive type `ControlFlow<T, fn() -> ControlFlow<T, fn() -> ...>>` so I'm not sure what the type should actually be.
- Any non-`become` call into a `become`-using function emits a loop of calling the continuation until `Break`.

Which I think is thus doable in isolation.

That allows a rule of something like "you can `become` any *static* call with the same signature", which is also sufficient for `musttail` on targets with LLVM support.  And it's trivially true for tail-self-recursion.
messages.zh:
避免为此需要SCC真的很好，因为这对于查询等工作效果不佳。  （值得注意的是，即使是内联也不使用SCC ，这有点像是SCC会很好的明显位置的海报。）

我想你可能可以避免SCC ，因为你只关心自己使用的功能`become`--如果我相互递归某个步骤*不是*`become`不需要很好地工作。

因此，可能：
-对于任何使用`become`，我们始终将MIR包含在rlib中
-我们使用MIR按需发出MIR的垫片版本（而不是实际进行尾部调用）`ControlFlow<T, fn()>`而不是`T`在哪里`fn`是被叫方的垫片。
  -嗯，那有点想要一个递归类型`ControlFlow<T, fn() -> ControlFlow<T, fn() -> ...>>`所以我不确定实际上应该是什么类型。
-任何非`become`呼入`become`-using函数发出调用Continuation的循环，直到`Break`.

因此，我认为这是孤立可行的。

这允许这样的规则： “你可以`become`任何具有相同签名的*静态*调用"，这也足以`musttail`在LLVM支持的目标上。对于尾部自递归来说，这几乎是正确的。

topics.name: What session state is hashed for incremental?
topics.name_zh: 哪个会话状态为增量哈希？
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论围绕增量编译中哪些 `Session` 状态会被哈希/跟踪，以及 AST lowering 从 AST 生成 HIR 时依赖 `lint store` 是否安全。`lint store` 目前似乎没有被增量系统直接哈希，但其变化可能影响生成的 HIR。
- **已跟踪的状态**：标记为 `TRACKED` 或 `TRACKED_NO_CRATE_HASH` 的选项发生变化时，会使增量编译会话目录失效；`StableCrateId`（crate 名称、`is_lib`、`-Cmetadata`）变化时会切换到不同的增量编译会话目录。其他状态只有在通过 `eval_always` 或可 feed 的 query 访问时才会被跟踪。
- **关于 `lint store`**：当前已经在缓存 query 中使用 `lint store` 生成 HIR，因此这些 query 相对于 `lint store` 的变化并非纯函数；但现阶段假定自定义 `rustc` driver 不会在未使缓存失效的情况下改变其提供的 `lint store`，否则属于 driver 的错误。
- **对 PR #164918 的结论**：AST lowering 目前总是执行，因此让它依赖 `lint store` 是可以接受的，PR #164918 不会额外引入问题。若未来希望让 `cargo clippy` 和 `cargo check` 共享产物，就需要将 `lint store` 纳入跟踪；届时这一问题需要进一步处理。
- **仍未解决/改进项**：有人认为应将“哪些 session state 会被增量系统跟踪、哪些状态可安全访问”的规则补充到 `rustc-dev-guide`；此外，未来更多流程进入 query 系统后，`lint store` 依赖是否仍然安全需要重新评估。

messages.en:
I've made a PR (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/164918) that uses the lint store during AST lowering to HIR.

@**mejrs** pointed out in review that he's not sure that is correct. If the lint store changes between incremental sessions, for example because a hypothetical rustc driver only sometimes register lints, this could affect the outputted hir. And the lint store does not seem to be hashed anywhere for incremental. I think this specific case is fine (at least until more parts become querified), because AST lowering is before the query system becomes active.

However this did make me realize that one can also just access the lint store later in the compiler where the query system is active, and this would not be correctly tracked by the query system. So I guess my questions are: 

1. Is it documented anywhere what parts of the session state are tracked by the query system, and are safe to access for incremental purposes?
2. Is it fine for AST lowering to depend on the lint store, both now and in the future?

cc @**Alejandra González** @**Jack Huey** as you have worked on https://goals.rust-lang.org/2026/incremental-system-rethought.html and might know this?
messages.zh:
我已经做了公关（https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/164918)在AST降至HIR期间使用棉绒商店。

@ * * mejrs * *在评论中指出，他不确定这是否正确。 如果lint存储在增量会话之间发生变化，例如因为假设的rustc驱动程序有时只注册lint ，这可能会影响输出的hir。 而且， lint商店似乎没有在任何地方进行增量哈希处理。我认为这种特殊情况是可以的（至少在更多的部分被查询之前） ，因为AST降低是在查询系统变为活动之前。

然而，这确实让我意识到，人们也可以稍后在查询系统处于活动状态的编译器中访问lint存储，而查询系统将无法正确跟踪。 所以我想我的问题是： 

1.它是否在任何地方记录了会话状态的哪些部分由查询系统跟踪，并且可以安全地进行增量访问？
2.现在和将来，降低AST是否可以依赖于棉绒店？

topics.name: Things missing from rustc internal API docs?
topics.name_zh: Rustc内部API文档中缺少的内容？
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`rustc` 内部 API 文档存在不完整或异常情况。搜索 `InstanceKind` 时能看到部分结果，但对应的实际类型页面似乎缺失或显示不正常。
- **具体表现**：文档页面显示的是正确类型的 re-export，但链接指向 `use` 而非原始定义；相关 `use` 甚至不是公开项。尽管启用了记录私有项的选项，这种展示仍然很奇怪。
- **更广泛影响**：讨论者指出这类“文档合并”问题很多，例如搜索 `rustc_middle::traits::ImplSource` 也可能难以找到目标，并表示通常会自行生成文档来规避。
- **关于原因的讨论**：有人猜测问题可能与 PR #163582 的文档合并变更有关；Michael Howell 认为这不像该 PR 引起的问题，因为完整路径搜索仍能找到条目，且 beta 文档中没有复现同样问题。
- **当前结论与未解决事项**：Michael Howell 随后表示发现了问题，并指向 PR #165024，但聊天记录没有进一步说明该 PR 的具体原因、修复内容或最终解决状态。

topics.name: GEP constant 0 in `gpu_offload.rs`
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/builder/gpu_offload.rs` 中多处使用了常量偏移为 `0` 的 `gep`/`inbounds_gep`；由于这在 LLVM 中通常是 no-op，Bee 询问是否存在特殊用途、能否安全移除。
- **地址空间因素**：workingjubilee 询问这些 GEP 是否涉及特殊的 address space；Bee 检查后表示，相关指针看起来都是普通的 `alloca`，没有发现这一因素。
- **可能的历史原因**：scottmcm 推测这可能是 typed pointers 时代的遗留写法，例如对 `[4 x u32]*` 做 GEP 可以得到 `u32*`，当时可能比 `bitcast` 更清晰。
- **当前判断**：Manuel 表示 Offload 开始得较晚，已经是在 typed pointers 之后；这些 GEP 很可能只是最初参考 Clang 生成 LLVM IR 时保留下来的写法，之后尚未彻底清理。
- **未解决事项**：Manuel 尚未仔细确认是否可以移除这些常量 `0` 的 GEP；他表示可以提交 PR 并指定他参与审查。

topics.name: ✔ optimize_for_size
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`optimize_for_size` 是供标准库/`compiler-builtins` 使用的 `cfg`，可让代码在“快速实现”和“小体积实现”之间选择；而 `-Os`/`-Oz` 是编译器整体优化级别，不能直接替代这种源码级选择。讨论认为可以考虑在启用 `-Os` 或其他 size 优化级别时自动启用相关 `cfg`，但会改变标准库算法，需谨慎。

- **`-Os` 与 `-Oz` 并非简单的“温和/激进”关系**：实际效果高度依赖目标平台和代码，尤其在嵌入式平台上，`-Oz` 可能因极低的 inlining threshold 阻止后续优化，最终比 `-Os` 更大或更慢。Rust 代码依赖内联实现良好 codegen，而 LLVM 当前 `-Oz` 的 inline threshold（5）被认为对 Rust 过于保守。

- **优化范围存在分歧**：现有 `optimize_for_size` 主要通过 `no_builtin_lookup_tables` 等方式移除会膨胀二进制的 lookup table；而 `compiler-builtins` 中更小但明显更慢的 `memcpy`/`memset`/`memcmp` 实现属于更激进的 size-for-speed 权衡。有人建议增加 `optimize_for_size_aggressive`，也有人倾向拆分为更具体的 `slim_mem_ops` 等 feature/cfg，以避免一个总开关隐含过多不可预测的优化。

- **嵌入式使用场景与标准库默认值**：不同嵌入式项目对 flash、性能、向量化和中断时限的需求差异很大，不能简单地为整个 target tuple 更改标准库默认优化级别。用户可能希望使用 `-O3` 保留 vectorizer，同时选择小型 `memcpy`。标准库实现是否随 opt-level 自动切换，也可能造成难以预期的性能下降。

- **结论与未解决问题**：讨论推动了为更激进优化建立 ACP；后续曾改为 `slim_mem_ops` 方案，并建议将讨论转移到 libs ACP `#907`，但该 ACP 后来被关闭，话题标记为 resolved。仍未解决的问题包括：应采用通用的 `optimize_for_size_aggressive` 还是具体的 `slim_mem_ops`、如何制定和测试 size 优化准则，以及 Rust 对 `memcpy` 等 compiler-builtins 的覆盖机制、weak linking 和 externally implementable items（EII）仍存在文档和实现限制。

messages.en: Why is `optimize_for_size` a feature, rather than picking up -Os/-Oz?
messages.zh: 为什么`optimize_for_size`一个功能，而不是拿起-Os/-Oz ？

messages.en: First of all, it’s important to note that -Oz increases binary size over -Os in many scenarios. It really depends on the target and the specific code you are compiling, and the overall experience has been that you should try both and use whichever is better (at the moment). I think there was a RustWeek talk discussing this as well (will look it up in a moment)
messages.zh: 首先，重要的是要注意-Oz在许多情况下会增加二进制大小超过-Os。这实际上取决于目标和您正在编译的特定代码，总体体验是，您应该尝试两者并使用（目前）更好的代码。我认为RustWeek也在讨论这个问题（稍后会查找）

messages.en: Secondly, I am not aware of any way of detecting `-C opt_level` from code, and I’m not sure that’s a good idea in general?
messages.zh: 其次，我不知道有任何方法可以检测`-C opt_level`从代码中，我不确定这是否是一个好主意？

messages.en: This feels like something that has wide ramifications.
messages.zh: 这感觉就像是具有广泛影响的东西。

messages.en: opt-levels are for the compiler, optimize_for_size is for the standard library.
messages.zh: opt-levels用于编译器， optimize_for_size用于标准库。

@_**kleines Filmröllchen|1174750** [schrieb](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/629921868):
```quote
First of all, it’s important to note that -Oz increases binary size over -Os in many scenarios. It really depends on the target and the specific code you are compiling, and the overall experience has been that you should try both and use whichever is better (at the moment). I think there was a RustWeek talk discussing this as well (will look it up in a moment)
```

This means that we can’t just go to the more aggressive size optimization mode (e.g. using my much slower but 10x more compact memcpy versions) on -Oz, since e.g. in my use case with PebbleOS, other parts of the code increase in size more than the savings we get from this. It is really not as simple as that, unfortunately

@_**Kevin Reid (kpreid)|608145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/629932955):
````quote
@_**Jonathan Keller|887758** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/optimize_for_size/near/629928744):
```quote
-Oz turns the inlining threshold very low, which prevents a lot of optimizations that could have happened after inlining
```

This feels like a thing that’s just fundamentally incorrect for Rust, due to the frequency of supposed-to-be-zero-cost-wrappers in Rust code. Could this be fixed somehow?

* If the inlining threshold were *not* lowered, would `-Oz` still mean something?
* If libraries routinely marked trivial functions `#[inline(always)]`, would this work better?
* Could we have an `#[inline(almost_certainly_inlines_to_almost_nothing)]` that expresses the thing that optimizing-for-size needs to know while having fewer negative effects on other cases?
````

I think ideally we'd have an optimizer that speculatively inlines, performs a bunch of optimizations and then checks if the overall size went down, if yes try inlining some more, otherwise roll back to the previous results.

Java Hotspot's C2 compiler does this, but that's a JIT which can afford burning a lot of CPU-time on small areas of code (it's called hotspot for a reason). Doing this for an AOT compiler would probably be prohibitive in most cases... but for a constrained embedded device the total amount of code to crunch through has to be fairly small in the first place...

messages.en:
The basic engineering problem IMO is that you first need an IR that can efficiently represent “rolling back” changes or otherwise support exploring multiple possibile rewrites. This ends up being fairly expensive both in engineering effort and compile time compared to only representing the current state. And it’s not clear that this is very useful and thus worth it, compared to the status quo of greedy rewrites with possibly quite involved heuristics for profitability.

For the kinds of optimizations that Cranelift does in its e-graph, it [turned out](https://cfallin.org/blog/2026/04/09/aegraph/) that the “explore multiple possibilities and pick best” part wasn’t actually useful in their context, but other aspects (sea of nodes approach, unifying many traditionally distinct passes) were.

On the other hand, loop vectorization in LLVM does have a little bit of “IR with ability to explore multiple options” (VPlan, Sandbox IR) because that optimization is arguably to complex to implement as single-shot IR rewrite. Although I’m not sure if there is any consensus yet about how successful the “try multiple rewrites and pick best one” part. (I’m not even sure if that part is used in the default pipeline yet)

✔ &NonZero<T> -> &T
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：目前从 `&NonZero<T>` 获取 `&T` 缺少访问方式；虽然根据 `NonZero` 的布局保证，使用 `unsafe` 进行转换是 sound 的，但用户认为标准库应提供相应接口。
- **讨论方案**：此前 PR #133255 因倾向采用 `AsRef` 而非 `From` 被关闭；Valerio Lomanto 原计划基于 `AsRef` 提交新的 PR。
- **重要信息**：Fon 指出已有 PR #129036，相关实现已经合并；目前虽然尚未实现 `AsRef`，但已有相应 impl，并计划在 Rust 1.101 稳定。
- **结论**：提议者确认此前遗漏了 PR #129036；话题随后被标记为已解决。

topics.name: Adding `<A: Allocator = Global>` to String, ByteString, ...
topics.name_zh: 增加 `<A: Allocator = Global>`to String, ByteString,...
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：讨论是否应为 `String`、`ByteString` 以及其他基于 `Vec` 或堆存储的集合添加 `Allocator` 类型参数（如 `<A: Allocator = Global>`）。`HashMap` 已经支持 allocator 参数。
- **主要阻碍**：为原本非泛型的 `String` 添加参数会影响类型推断；`String` 会从表示 `String<Global>` 变为 `String<_>`，导致现有代码和泛化后的 impl（例如涉及 `Borrow<str>` 的 impl）出现推断问题。有人指出这类改动可能需要语言/编译器支持，并提到等待 edition redirects（#160227）。
- **`ByteString` 方案**：普遍倾向于在 `ByteString` 稳定化前就加入 allocator 参数，以避免重蹈 `String` 的覆辙。对于 `ByteString<A != Global>` 转换为当前不带 allocator 参数的 `String`，无法像 `Global` 情况下一样直接复用内部 `Vec`；暂时可仅为 `ByteString<Global>` 提供相关方法。
- **已知进展/结论**：`ByteString` 的 allocator 支持 PR（#146219）已经准备就绪，因此建议不要在该 PR 之外重复修改 `ByteString`。新增方法本身可在 `String` 获得 allocator 参数后再添加，但事后新增泛型参数会造成 breaking change。
- **仍未解决的问题**：尚未确定如何为 `String` 安全加入 allocator 参数，以及未来新的 trait solver 或默认类型参数改进是否能缓解类型推断问题。

topics.name: splatting primitive `mem::splat` or `ptr::fill`
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：Rust 目前没有将单个值按位广播到整个 slice/未初始化区域的通用 primitive。现有方案包括 `ptr::write(ptr::read)`、`ptr::copy_nonoverlapping`、循环，以及可能使用 `write_bytes`；`<[T]>::fill` 通过 `Clone`，对 `T: TrivialClone` 的按位复制只是优化而非保证。Voxell 提议在 `core::mem` 或 `core::ptr` 中增加 `splat`。
- **接口与语义仍在讨论**：候选形式包括 `T -> T` 或 `Src -> Dst`，接收 raw slice pointer 或 `ptr + len`。其设想的 `unsafe fn splat<T>(value: T, target: *mut T, len: usize)` 要求目标可写、对齐且有效，并要求 `T` 的值可依据 `Drop` 语义进行按位复制；即使 `T: !Copy`，在 `T: TrivialClone` 情况下也会执行按位复制。
- **关于性能依据的讨论**：Voxell 最初比较了循环变量形式、寄存器数量、代码大小等差异；Hanna Kruppe 指出 LLVM 优化后的寄存器压力和 copy 指令数量不一定能直接代表实际收益，相关差异可能只是启发式和上下文造成的随机波动。因此 Voxell 同意不再把寄存器压力/代码大小作为主要动机。
- **更明确的动机是复用实现、避免代码重复**：`Vec::<T>::extend_with` 的 `T: TrivialClone` 特化需要操作 `Vec` 的未初始化区域，不能直接复用要求安全 `&mut [T]` 的 `<[T]>::fill`。两者的特化类型集合和底层广播操作相同，因此可以考虑用基于 raw pointer 的 `splat` 同时实现它们；Hanna 认为共享代码比复制特化逻辑更合理。
- **intrinsic 方案的限制与未决问题**：如果 LLVM 存在适合的特定构造，可以考虑 intrinsic；`llvm.experimental.memset.pattern` 仅支持最多 16 字节的重复模式，且是否有利取决于目标平台，因此若加入 Rust intrinsic，可能只限于 16 字节模式，其余类型使用 library 实现。`splat` 的最终 API、放在 `core::mem` 还是 `core::ptr`、特化范围，以及是否确实应引入该 primitive，仍未确定；为消除 unrolled loop 尾部而根据向量宽度调整长度的方案也被认为复杂且缺乏依据。

messages.en:
My first thought after skimming the comment you linked is that I don't understand why we'd be interested in code size, stack frame size, register pressure, etc. under `-Copt-level=3 -Cno-prepopulate-passes`. When people compile with opt-level=3 they are asking for LLVM optimizations. It can be useful to look at initial LLVM IR to understand if we do something very silly in rustc's codegen, or as part of investigating why LLVM optimizations don't go the way we want. But anything that LLVM can reliably optimize well seems fine for optimized builds.

A library function might still make sense to reduce code duplication, especially for tricky tweaks like specializations or selectively dropping unnecessary UB checks for better debug-mode codegen. But I'd need to take more time to look at all the code in context to form an opinion. Sometimes there are reasons to e.g. skip UB checks in one code path but not in another, even though they mostly do the same operation.
messages.zh: 浏览您链接的评论后，我的第一个想法是，我不明白为什么我们会对下面的代码大小、堆栈帧大小、寄存器压力等感兴趣`-Copt-level=3 -Cno-prepopulate-passes`。当人们使用opt-level = 3进行编译时，他们要求LLVM优化。 查看最初的LLVM IR以了解我们是否在rustc的codegen中做了一些非常愚蠢的事情，或者作为调查为什么LLVM优化没有按照我们想要的方式进行的一部分，可能会很有用。 但是， LLVM可以可靠地优化的任何内容似乎都适合优化构建。库函数对于减少代码重复可能仍然有意义，特别是对于棘手的调整，如专业化或有选择地删除不必要的UB检查以获得更好的调试模式代码生成。但我需要花更多的时间在上下文中查看所有代码才能形成意见。有时有理由跳过一个代码路径中的UB检查，但不在另一个代码路径中，即使它们大多执行相同的操作。

messages.en:
the register pressure point applies to `-Copt-level=3`, not `-Copt-level=3 -Cno-prepopulate-passes`.

the stack copy concerns were raised by mark simulacrum over a version using `ptr.write(ptr::read)`. that can be ignored.

the loop prologue is the main difference between variations that use a pointer induction variable vs an index induction variable. they both vectorize and unroll appropriately and have identical hot loops
messages.zh:
校准压力点适用于`-Copt-level=3`不`-Copt-level=3 -Cno-prepopulate-passes`.

堆栈副本问题是由Mark Simulacrum针对使用`ptr.write(ptr::read)`.这是可以忽略的。

循环序幕是使用指针感应变量与指数感应变量的变体之间的主要区别。它们都适当地矢量和展开，并且具有相同的热循环

messages.en: An actual intrinsic might make sense if LLVM has some specific construct or intrinsic that we'd like to emit from rustc instead of open-coding the operation and hoping LLVM recognizes it. There is [`llvm.experimental.memset.pattern`](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#llvm-experimental-memset-pattern-intrinsic) but I think it's target-dependent whether it's a good idea (at least some LLVM passes check target info to decide whether to introduce calls to it). It's also limited to short repeating patterns up to 16 bytes, and we shouldn't add an intrinsic to rustc that has to emit very complicated LLVM IR for some types `T`, so if we add an intrinsic it should probably be limited to 16 byte patterns and everything else stays library code.
messages.zh: 实际的内在可能是有意义的，如果LLVM有一些特定的结构或内在的，我们希望从rustc发出，而不是开放编码的操作，并希望LLVM识别它。有[`llvm.experimental.memset.pattern`](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#llvm-experimental-memset-pattern-intrinsic)但我认为这是否是一个好主意取决于目标（至少一些LLVM通过检查目标信息来决定是否引入调用）。它也仅限于最多16个字节的短重复模式，对于某些类型，我们不应该为必须发射非常复杂的LLVM IR的rustc添加固有的`T`，因此，如果我们添加一个内部函数，它可能应该限制为16个字节模式，其他所有内容都将保留库代码。

I don't know if the former number is meaningful or not, it might be correlated with register pressure to some extent, but there's lots of confounding factors, so I don't know what to make of this. Skimming the source code and generated code, I think the actual register pressure is a wash with random fluctuations in heuristics and insofar it's different that's downstream of different choices in how to optimize the loop.

messages.en: (Usually the start/end pointer pair approach is better for register pressure than pointer + index up to length, because it only needs two live values for the loop itself instead of three. But either way it’s not a lot of register pressure, small enough and sensitive enough to surrounding context that I don’t see the point of reading tea leaves here.
messages.zh: （通常，开始/结束指针对方法对于寄存器压力比指针+索引长度更好，因为它只需要循环本身的两个实时值，而不是三个。但无论哪种方式，它都不是很大的压力，足够小，对周围环境足够敏感，我看不到在这里阅读茶叶的意义。

messages.en: that changes depending on autovectorization. i've observed that when pointer induction is used (start ptr and end ptr), llvm just calculates the trip count by subtracting the pointers, leaving 3 values that are alive. for fallibly iterative fills (`<[T]>::fill where T: Clone`), pointer induction might be the better choice as it might not be vectorized, but for the constraints of `splat` (which is strictly bitwise copying), i think it's better to lean on the pointer + index variation.
messages.zh: 这取决于自动矢量化。我观察到，当使用指针感应（ start ptr和end ptr ）时， llvm只是通过减去指针来计算行程计数，留下3个有效的值。对于易出错的迭代填充（`<[T]>::fill where T: Clone`） ，指针归纳可能是更好的选择，因为它可能不会被矢量化，但对于`splat`（严格按位复制） ，我认为最好依靠指针+索引变化。

messages.en: Yeah the pointer pair approach needs more work to compute the length, e.g., for checking if the unrolled (including, but not limited to, vectorized) loop can be entered and when it can be left. But usually that is a short-lived temporary, not another value live across the entire loop, so it doesn't necessarily increase register pressure
messages.zh: 是的，指针对方法需要更多的工作来计算长度，例如，用于检查是否可以输入展开（包括但不限于矢量化）循环以及何时可以离开。但通常这是一个短暂的临时值，而不是整个循环中的另一个值，因此不一定会增加寄存器压力

messages.en: Of course that's the idealized setting, in reality LLVM does silly things all the time, but I don't think the silliness in these cases is predictable enough to make bikeshedding and extensive experiments useful. If a real application spends enough time in splat loops that it's worth worrying about, then either the loops run enough that any spills in surrounding code are a good trade-off, or it's a lot of tiny splats, in which case it's more important to look at everything else other than the loop.
messages.zh: 当然，这是理想化的设置，实际上LLVM一直在做愚蠢的事情，但我不认为这些情况下的愚蠢是可预测的，足以使自行车脱落和广泛的实验有用。如果一个真正的应用程序在splat循环中花费了足够的时间，值得关注，那么循环要么运行得足够多，以至于周围代码中的任何溢出都是一个很好的权衡，要么就是很多微小的splat ，在这种情况下，更重要的是查看循环之外的其他所有内容。

messages.en: (Also, in the latter case the splat code really ought to be inlined and not in its own function, in which case any experiments on the splat operation in isolation are unlikely to be representative.)
messages.zh: （此外，在后一种情况下， splat代码实际上应该是内联的，而不是其自身的功能，在这种情况下，任何关于单独的splat操作的实验都不太可能具有代表性。）

messages.en: i see. then i'll drop the register pressure/code size claims as the motivating evidence, and focus more on the code duplication part. currently, my PR cannot reuse the `<[T]>::fill` primitive as that requires a safe `&mut [T]` and in `Vec::<T>::extend_with` specialized for `T: TrivialClone` i'm operating over the uninitialized part of a vector. could that serve as a motivating use case to pursue `splat`, implementing both `<[T]>::fill` and `Vec::extend_with` in terms of it?

topics.name: hashbrown/backtrace subtrees
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`hashbrown` 因依赖 `alloc`/`core` 内部实现，无法作为普通 Cargo 依赖直接用于 `std` 构建；讨论了使用 git submodule、git subtree，或将代码直接纳入 `rust-lang/rust` 的方案。`backtrace` 也存在类似的仓库与 `std` 集成问题。
- **`hashbrown` 方案**：最终倾向于仿照 `stdarch`，将 `hashbrown` 放在 `library` 下作为子目录，并通过 `#[path]` 以模块方式包含，而不是作为 Cargo 依赖。Trevor Gross 认为对大型仓库使用实际的 `git subtree` 不可行；相关实现可先在 subtree 分支上测试，再单独提交 PR。
- **`backtrace` 方向**：多数参与者支持取消 `backtrace` submodule，将其开发完全移入 `rust-lang/rust`，甚至归档原 `backtrace-rs` 仓库；这样可以统一处理方式、改善 in-tree 开发和 CI 协调，并减少 `libc → std → backtrace` 的同步延迟。
- **已达成的条件与迁移安排**：迁移后仍需支持按需发布 crates.io 版本，不能绑定到 Rust 发布周期；等待已获批准的 PR 进入队列被认为可以满足“随时发布”。计划保留现有 issue，在切换前处理完现有 PR，之后将新 issue/PR 导向 `rust-lang/rust`，并在 README、可能的 Rust 博客文章及 crate 仓库链接中明确迁移。
- **仍未解决的问题**：`backtrace` 完全移入主仓库后的发布、CI 和测试负担仍需具体落实；从 `rust-lang/rust` 发布 crate 不能与仓库内依赖新版本原子完成，虽然目前实际需要这种同步的主要是 `ui_test`。此外，`backtrace` 当前 CI 经常因目标平台、工具链或测试环境变化而损坏，如何在迁移后维持或改善覆盖率仍有讨论。

Two thoughts on this:
- If we do this, we should put a big fat warning into backtrace's README that the crate just moved places (and ideally also post a Rust blog post about it in advance), otherwise people might be worried that the crate stops being maintained when its repo got archived (we should also repoint the repo of the crate to `rust-lang/rust`, ofc)
- I remembered now what was one of the issues with having crates.io crates published from `rust-lang/rust`. You can't atomically publish a new release and depend on that version in-tree. So either bumping the version and depending on it needs a PR -> merge -> PR -> merge cycle, or library (and everything in-tree that wants to have `backtrace` atomic updates) would have to depend on backtrace via `path = "..."`.

topics.name: Miri vs tests in std
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：当前 `rust-lang/rust` CI 只运行部分 `std` 测试，且测试中零散使用 `cfg(miri)`/`cfg(not(miri))`，导致 Miri 难以准确发现哪些 `std` API 缺少 shim；不同平台覆盖范围也不一致：Linux 排除 `fs::`、`net::`、`process::`、`sys::`，macOS/Windows 仅运行 `time::`、`sync::`、`thread::`、`env::` 的部分测试。
- **主要区分**：因 Miri 运行过慢而缩小循环或跳过的测试可以长期保留；因缺少 shim（如 `unlinkat`、Unix domain socket 等）而跳过的测试则应视为 Miri 的待支持事项，不应被普通 `cfg(miri)` 隐藏。随机添加 `cfg(not(miri))` 还会掩盖本来可以在 Miri 中运行的测试。
- **讨论中的方案**：一是减少甚至取消 `rust-lang/rust` CI 中的 `std` Miri 测试，仅保留 `core`/`alloc` 或少数稳定模块，同时由 `miri-test-libstd` 负责更广泛测试；二是引入独立于 `cfg(miri)` 的 cfg（讨论过 `miritest`、`skip_unsupported_miri_shims` 等名称），只在需要避免缺少 shim 的默认 CI 配置中跳过测试，而让其他 Miri 测试暴露失败。也有人建议使用带理由的 `ignore`、tidy 检查或外部 skip list。
- **阶段性结论/进展**：倾向于使用单独的 cfg 来区分“缺少 shim”和“过慢”，并在 `std-dev-guide` 中记录规则；`cfg(miri)` 应主要用于全局排除或调整过慢的测试。相关 PR 已将部分原先基于 `--skip` 的模块级排除改为更细粒度的 cfg，TCP 测试已重新启用，UDP 支持预计完善后再启用。
- **仍未解决的问题**：尚未最终确定独立 cfg 的名称、启用位置及完整基础设施；`std` doctest 如何按需跳过仍有实现问题，但 RalfJ 认为可以跳过这些 doctest（它们仍会在 `miri-test-libstd` 中运行）。另外，如何在不增加维护负担的情况下保持 `rust-lang/rust` CI 的 Miri 失败信号，以及如何确保新增 compiler 特性暴露到 `std` 时得到 libs/Miri 方面的审查，仍需进一步明确。

messages.en:
The current situation around Miri and tests in std is not great. Tests randomly get `cfg`d away under `miri`, but not consistently so, making it quite hard for me to track which features miri is missing. Some subset of std tests gets executed in miri by CI, but apart from me probably nobody knows which subset. And even if they do, it becomes unclear what to do with a test failure.

The status quo is that we run the following std tests in Miri under CI:
- on Linux: everything except for `fs::`, `net::`, `process::`, `sys::`
- on macOS and Windows: only the parts in `time::`, `sync::`, `thread::`, `env::`

If possible, I'd like to avoid `cfg`d tests in std as it becomes hard to keep track of them. (I mean tests that are disabled for "miri does not have the shim" reasons. tests that are disabled because Miri is too slow are entirely fine.) But obviously new features shouldnt be blocked on Miri support. So it would probably be better to reduce the test coverage so that CI still allows new features to land.
I can imagine two variants of that:
- We reduce std test coverage to just `time::`, `sync::`, `thread::`, `env::` in general. new things seem rare there.
- We entirely remove std testing from CI, only keeping alloc and core. Those extremely rarely need Miri patches and when they do (new intrinsics) it's probably good to get a Miri implementation early to help figure out the spec.

Either way, miri-test-libstd will still run all the tests CI currently runs. And the miri test suite runs in CI so for existing features that miri covers, we'd notice when they stop working.

Thoughts, ideas?
Cc @**The 8472|330154**, @*T-miri*  as we just ran into this with the fd-views PR.
messages.zh:
Miri周围的现状和STD中的测试不太好。测试随机获取`cfg`d离开以下`miri`，但并非始终如一，因此我很难跟踪miri缺少哪些功能。 一些std测试的子集由CI在miri中执行，但除了我之外，可能没有人知道哪个子集。 即使他们这样做了，也不清楚如何处理测试失败。

现状是，我们在CI下在MIRI中运行以下STD测试：
-在Linux上：除了`fs::`, `net::`, `process::`, `sys::`-在macOS和Windows上：仅`time::`, `sync::`, `thread::`, `env::`如果可能的话，我想避免`cfg`在STD中进行测试，因为很难跟踪它们。 （我的意思是由于“miri没有垫片”原因而被禁用的测试。由于Miri太慢而被禁用的测试完全没有问题。） 但显然， Miri支持不应阻止新功能。 因此，减少测试覆盖范围可能更好，以便CI仍然允许新功能登陆。
我可以想象有两种变体：
-我们将性病测试的覆盖范围缩小到`time::`, `sync::`, `thread::`, `env::`一般来说，那里的新事物似乎很少见。
-我们从CI中完全移除STD测试，只保留ALLOC和CORE。 那些极少需要Miri补丁的人，当他们这样做（新的内在因素）时，尽早获得Miri实现以帮助找出规格可能是件好事。

无论哪种方式， miri-test-libstd仍将运行当前运行的所有测试。Miri测试套件在CI中运行，因此对于miri覆盖的现有功能，我们会注意到它们何时停止工作。

想法，想法？
Cc @ * * The 8472 | 330154 * *, @ * T-miri * ，因为我们刚刚在fd-views PR中遇到了这个问题。

messages.en:
I'm not familiar with std-specific issues here, but instead of writing `#[cfg]`s you can write conditional ignores:
```rust
#[test]
#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore = "slow-under-miri")]
fn foo() {
```
The advantages of this are:
* the reason is attached to the test in the syntax tree, not just a commenting convention, so it is preserved under reformatting and refactoring
* the test harness output reports that ignored tests exist, so it isn’t a silent lack of coverage
* the current number of each kind of ignored tests can be measured by examining the test harness output
* if desired, the test can be run despite the `ignore`, without changing the source code
* it's not the same thing as an `allow(reason = ...)` but it's close, and thus more familiar
messages.zh:
我不熟悉这里的性病特定问题，但不是写`#[cfg]`您可以编写条件忽略：```rust
#[test]
#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore = "slow-under-miri")]
fn foo() {
```这样做的好处是：
*原因附加到语法树中的测试，而不仅仅是注释约定，因此它在重新格式化和重构下保留
*测试线束输出报告存在被忽略的测试，因此它不是无声的缺乏覆盖
*可以通过检查测试线束输出来测量每种被忽略测试的当前数量
*如果需要，可以运行测试，尽管`ignore`，无需更改源代码
*它与`allow(reason = ...)`但它很近，因此更熟悉

so far two options came up for resolving this:
- running fewer / no std tests in miri so that people dont have to add as many cfg (and make it more consistent so its easier to document & remember where cfg is needed)
- add a separate cfg for these tests so its easier to track separately and so it doesnt interfere with miri-test-libstd. cfg(miri) would only be used for tests that we want to exclude everywhere, e.g. as they are just too slow.

Fourth back-to-back question, trying to understand things: is this effectively the proposal?

1. We stop testing parts of `std` with Miri in r-l/r CI
2. We delete any `cfg(miri)` in modules that are now no longer tested
3. `miri-test-libstd` still tests all of `std`, including those modules that aren't tested in r-l/r anymore
4. Many of those tests are missing shims, so `miri-test-libstd` keeps an xfail list (? unclear on this point)

topics.name: Capping float strings to a sane value
topics.name_zh: Capping float strings to a sane value
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：浮点字符串解析（`dec2flt`）在输入长度极端大时会触发一些小 bug；需要在“略微减慢数学计算”与“限制输入长度”之间取舍。截断输入并不总是正确，因为很深处的非零数字可能影响舍入结果，尤其是恰好处于 halfway 的情况。
- **主要方案**：PR #165163 提议对可解析的字符串长度设置上限，默认上限为 `1 << 50`（约 1 PB），超出则返回错误。该方案保留正常输入的快速路径，避免为极端输入维护更复杂或更慢的算法；已有观点认为 `dec2flt` 即使只保留足够计算舍入的数字，也仍可能在极端十进制位数相关计算中溢出。
- **关于上限大小的讨论**：有人倾向更小的 `2^16`、`2^32`、`i32::MAX` 或 `i32::MAX >> 1`；支持较大上限的一方认为 `2^50` 基本属于“除非主动制造，否则现实中不可触及”的边界，能减少合法用户输入因限制而失败的可能。代码据 PR 作者称可正确处理到 `2^58`，因此 `2^50` 也被视为留有算法调整余量。
- **重要兼容性考量**：过去曾存在更小、实际可触及的浮点解析限制，后来被修复；很多代码默认“通过浮点词法检查后，`std` 就能解析”，而输入可能来自不可信用户，因此过小的新增限制可能导致 `parse::<f64>().expect(...)` 因合法词法输入而 panic。也有人建议明确记录限制并提供专用错误变体，但这可能带来兼容性和使用预期问题。
- **当前状态与未决事项**：讨论中没有人明确反对采用长度上限，整体对 PR 的方向较认可；但具体应采用 `2^50` 还是更小的 `i32` 级别上限，以及是否需要文档说明或专用错误变体，仍未形成明确结论。

messages.en: Note that these kinds of inputs can be handled correctly by looking at all input digits but only actually parsing/calculating with enough digits to determine the right result modulo such half-way cases, and remembering whether you truncated non-zero trailing digits (which means it's not a halfway case). However, that's already what the dec2flt slow path is doing. The problem is that even the truncated representation still requires some calculations in units of "number of decimal digits" (i.e., log10 scale) and those calculations can still overflow if the input is excessive enough, unless you go out of your way to use otherwise excessive precision and/or complicate the logic. Making sure you caught all such problems and handle them correctly is a huge hassle, for no real world benefit.

topics.name: bti in compiler-builtins' aarch64 outline-atomics
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：AArch64 `compiler-builtins` 的 outline atomics 使用 `naked_asm!`，需要在函数入口加入 BTI（Branch Target Identification）提示指令（`hint #34`），否则在启用 `-Zbranch-protection=bti` 时，作为间接调用目标可能触发异常。由于 naked function 不应由编译器随意修改，且 BTI 不是 `target_feature`，现有 `cfg(target_feature = "bti")` 无法直接使用。
- **主要方案讨论**：倾向于暴露一个可供代码查询的 `cfg`，类似 panic strategy；候选形式包括与选项一一对应的 `cfg(branch_protection = "bti")`，或更通用的 target modifier cfg。也讨论过无条件加入 BTI 指令，但虽然不支持 BTI 的 CPU 会将其视为 nop，仍会带来代码尺寸和指令缓存开销，且自动修改 naked function 令人不安。
- **扩展观点**：多个 target modifiers 可能改变 ABI，naked asm、甚至普通 inline asm 可能需要知道这些配置；Alice Ryhl 和 Jacob Lifshay 认为，许多 target modifiers 都可能受益于 cfg 查询能力。不过目前尚未决定是否为所有 target modifiers 提供通用机制，相关方向由 `#152038` 提交给了 t-lang 讨论。
- **阶段性结论**：outline-atomics 的启用一度计划回滚，等待 cfg 机制落地，因为在 `compiler-builtins` 中解析 rustflags 并不理想。随后 `compiler-builtins` commit `f626afc2fc1fec64f205dda3e016eefe79d06066` 已落地，相关实现应已解决。
- **验证结果**：使用 `RUSTFLAGS=-Zbranch-protection=bti` 检查生成的汇编时，`__aarch64_cas1_relax` 入口出现了 `hint #34`；LLVM IR 中虽然看不到该指令，但汇编输出确认 BTI 提示已生成。

messages.en:
I'd like to be able to add a hint instruction to the `naked_asm!` in the compiler-builtins implementations for outline-atomics (e.g. [in this body](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/94a0cd15f5976fa35e5e6784e621c04e9f958e57/library/compiler-builtins/compiler-builtins/src/aarch64_outline_atomics.rs#L183)). This hint instruction is for BTI, which is a hardware feature that guards against the execution of instructions that aren't the intended target of a branch. The hint instruction we want to add here indicates that this is expected to be the target of a call, as otherwise an exception is thrown and we don't want that.

The compiler normally adds these automatically when `-Zbranch-protection=bti` is enabled, but it wouldn't be appropriate to do this for naked functions. We also only want to add this when BTI is enabled, not unconditionally, but only the compiler knows that. LLVM does this conditionally when they generate their implementations ([here](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/737db63fafa273a840d84594ca7c96fef113c8f2/compiler-rt/lib/builtins/assembly.h#L104-L108)), because they have a define they can check. BTI isn't a target feature, so there's no `cfg(target_feature = "bti")` that we could use to cfg this in compiler-builtins.

This is a bit of a #**t-libs** question and a bit of a #**t-compiler** question, so asking here and will cross-link. I'm not especially familiar with `naked_asm!` and compiler-builtins, so unsure is this the type of issue you've come across before and have a solution to that I could re-use, or  if I'll need to go find a way to expose this as a cfg in the language to use here? (or add a perma-unstable attribute or some other mechanism that the compiler could pick up on and do this in the naked function codegen)

topics.name: `clippy::wrong_self_convention` doesn't check return type
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`clippy::wrong_self_convention` 目前不检查返回类型，而 `as_`、`to_`、`into_` 的命名约定本身并不完全一致。API Guidelines 提到成本、所有权和抽象层级等因素，但成本无法仅从方法签名判断，标准库中也存在多个反例。
- **主要观点**：`as_` 通常表示仅重新解释或提取数据，`into_` 表示消耗 `self` 的转换，`to_` 的语义最宽泛，可进行更复杂或成本更高的转换。不过，`as_secs`、`f64::to_radians`、`Ipv6Addr::to_bits`、`u8::to_ascii_lowercase` 等例子表明这些规则会相互冲突；尤其不能仅依据方法签名或函数体可靠判断命名是否正确。
- **关于可能的 Clippy lint**：讨论认为可以增加检查缺少返回类型的方法，例如 `{as,into,to}_*(&self)` 或 `(&mut self)`，并考虑检查名称中包含 `mut` 但返回值不包含可变引用、可变拥有值或相应 guard 的方法。
- **已达成的结论**：提议的 `missing_return_type` 和 `misleading_mut_method_name` 得到了认可；后者应检查 `*_mut`、`*_mut_*`、`mut_*` 等 snake_case 单词边界，并考虑递归检查 `Option`、`Result` 等嵌套容器中的返回类型。`wrong_as_return_type` 因规则复杂、容易产生误报，暂时放弃。
- **仍未解决的问题**：无法确定一套普遍适用且低误报的规则来判断 `as_` 返回非引用类型是否错误；函数体分析也很难建立明确标准。`as_`、`to_`、`into_` 的 API conventions 仍较模糊，且相关 API Guidelines 已多年未更新。

messages.en:
@**Frank (CommanderStorm)** We are fallible and thus do not get it right all the time, that much is inevitable.

To add to what @**Thom Chiovoloni** said, and somewhat restate the API guidelines which are already being referenced in that issue:
- `as_` is supposed to be something that is achievable by merely "reexamining" the data. It should not really be generating additional data, merely giving you a different view of it.
- `into_`  is a conversion that must be consuming (it essentially is trying to match intuitions from use of `From` and `Into::into`... so it should be going from `T` to `U`), and generally is not a significant modification... `into_inner` is a common function in `std`, where it just yields  `T` from `WrapperType<T>`, so yeah, not doing jack.
- `to_` is the most... wibbly of these, where as mentioned, it is a "full conversion" to a possibly very different type and possibly very different view of the data, so it's allowed to chop it up and rearrange it and do complex mathematical formulae.

I think it's Not That Surprising that `as` is often used with a `Copy` return type when the operation is basically a copy of data (as in `Duration::as_secs`) and returns an owned `Copy` of the inner data, because it's adhering to the more important idea: "nothing significant happened to get you this data, it's just basically what is behind this type".

messages.en:
basically it's not surprising that this happened:
> * `f64::to_radians(self) -> f64` violates the cost convention. Looking into the source code, it only divides and multiples which is cheap. However, it follows the "same abstraction level different representation" convention. So these conventions can clearly contradict with each other.
> * `u8::to_ascii_lowercase(&self) -> u8` violates the "borrowed -> owned (non-Copy types)" convention.
> * `Ipv6Addr::to_bits(self) -> u128` violates the cost because it is a cheap `from_be_bytes` conversion.

because `to_` is the most "it can do whatever" here.

I would say that generally it's wrong to have `as_` for `T -> U` where it isn't `&T -> &U` if the types involved are not Copy, though, and I don't think that people should really be in the habit of it for Copy types either.

From the issue:

> The [C-CONV](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/naming.html#ad-hoc-conversions-follow-as_-to_-into_-conventions-c-conv) API guideline suggests a number of conventions:
> - **Cost**: Free (`as_`), expensive (`to_`), variable (`into_`) cost. This cannot be determined using the method signature.
> - **Ownership**: Borrowed (reference) or owned (copy vs non-copy) type. This can be determined. However, there are several counter example in the std library.
> - **Abstraction**: The `as_` and `into_` *typically* decrease abstraction while the `to_` *typically* stays at the abstraction level but change its representation. I am not sure how to enforce this or worth enforcing it.
> - **Qualifiers**[+types]: If the `mut` in the conversion name, then the return type should be mutable. This is the most straightforward from the conventions. (Although, it could be more complicated if we add the `ref`, `slice`, `vec` and other qualifiers.)

Of those, clippy can reason about ownership, mutability/types, but cost is subjective and context dependent.

From what was written in this thread, could we for example say as a subset of things that we can agree on are:
- no return type -> lint
- `as_` with `Result<T>` or `Option<T>`-> lint,
- (maybe controversial) `as_` with an non-reference Copy type?
- `mut` in the conversion name, but return type not mutable -> lint

Some of this  under "don't break public API" setting by default I think, so would not lint on std, unless std opts into this :wink:.

I don't think we're in the habit of running clippy on std without being selective about lints we choose to enforce anyways?

1. well yes, "obviously".
2. see [`Option::as_ref`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html#method.as_ref) for a counterexample that is... probably not a mistake ^^;
3. I would personally say `as_` with a sig that isn't `&T -> &U` should be something that something like *clippy*, which is allowed to take a stronger normative stance, should feel comfortable linting on regardless of whether the signature is instead `fn(T) -> U where U: Copy`, and yes it is pretty clearly not something that should happen when `U: !Copy` (barring, like, `&mut` for `as_mut`, obviously, but that's... look, just because we can't be generic over `&` and `&mut` easily doesn't mean I'm not gonna speak like we can)
4. On the last one, "return type not mutable or owned"... owned implies mutable, but sometimes folks forget! I'm just noting that because it shouldn't lint on returning a custom `RefMut<'a, T>` handle.

topics.name: on_broken_pipe eii to fix SIGPIPE
topics.summary:
- 该话题围绕通过 `std::io::on_broken_pipe() -> std::io::OnBrokenPipe`（EII）解决 `SIGPIPE` 问题；当前 EII 在部分目标平台上因 weak linkage 不工作而存在问题。
- 讨论指出，如果 `on_broken_pipe` 不放在 `std::os::unix` 中，就必须能在 Windows 等平台上定义。一个方案是仅在 Unix 目标上使用 `#[eii(on_broken_pipe)]`，其他平台提供无法被覆盖的普通函数。
- 有观点认为不应直接忽略 Windows（尤其是 MinGW）的链接问题：新版 Binutils 可能已修复部分 weak symbols 处理，LLD 也可能已经支持或较容易支持，因此相关情况需要重新评估。
- Zack Weinberg 指出示例 API 中 `SIG_IGN` 与 `SIG_DFL` 对应的枚举项文档效果写反了：应明确区分忽略 `SIGPIPE` 后通过 `ErrorKind::BrokenPipe` 报错，以及保留默认行为导致进程终止。
- 目前已在 tracking issue 的 Steps 中加入处理跨平台默认实现/链接支持的事项，但 Windows/MinGW 等目标上的 EII 支持及最终 API 方案仍未解决。

Maybe we can do something like this?

```rs
#[cfg_attr(target_family = "unix", eii(on_broken_pipe))]
pub fn on_broken_pipe() -> OnBrokenPipe {
    OnBrokenPipe::Default
}
```

topics.name: Looking for reviewer for an OsStr + Pattern related change
topics.name_zh: Looking for reviewer for an OsStr + Pattern related change
topics.summary:
- 该工作旨在恢复并扩展一个已停滞数年的 PR：一部分将 `core::str::Pattern` 参数化/泛化，使其可用于更多类型；另一部分基于此为 `OsStr` 增加类似 `&str` 的 pattern API，并适配新的不稳定 `OsStr` API。
- 主要待讨论的设计问题包括：是否不必将全部 API gate 在 `pattern` feature 下，以便先稳定与稳定版 `&str` API 对应的部分；`OsStr` 无法直接使用闭包形式的 `Pattern`，目前考虑通过 `predicate` 函数绕开 `OsString` 位于 `std` 的限制；字符数组/切片 matcher 是否需要公开内部 trait，或改用 sealed trait、迁移部分实现到 `std`、以及使用 `AsRef<[char]>`（可能有性能代价）。
- 多位参与者认为原始 PR 过于庞大，建议按逻辑上的独立变更拆成 stacked pull requests，而不是简单保留一个巨型 PR；代码移动最好单独放在只包含移动的 commit 中，以便 review。作者已拆分出多个相互依赖的 PR，并确认各 commit 的测试曾通过，但部分中间 commit 会暂时引入性能回归，后续 commit 再恢复优化。
- 关于 PR 流程曾出现混淆：建议只有当前可 review 的首个 PR 保持 ready，其余依赖尚未合并的 PR 标为 draft；某个 PR 准备接受 review 时再 rebase 并取消 draft，否则 draft PR 通常不会进入 review 队列。作者已根据意见处理格式、缺失注释、代码移动和 `Pattern<str>` 等修改，收到过部分 review。
- 目前仍未解决的是后续 PR 的完整 review 和合并。`libs` 团队说明 reviewer 资源比预期更紧张，大型变更需要较长时间；社区 review 是否适用于 `libs` 也被提出，但由于涉及 API stability，不能直接照搬 Clippy 的模式。作者仍在等待对较早未合并 PR（尤其从 #161606 开始）的进一步 review，并询问还能做什么来推动进展。

Anyway, open questions:
1. Right now it gates everything into "pattern" feature even though API closely maps what you get on `&str` in stable. I think it can use something else that it can be stabilized before the pattern stuff.
2. &str gives a way to access patterns with closures (s.strip_prefix(|c| c == 'x')). This works because Pattern, &str and FnMut all living in core. For OsStr you have to use `predicate` function `(os.strip_prefix(predicate(|c| c == 'x')))` to get around the fact that OsString lives in std.
3. I added matchers by array/slice/etc of chars, this required to make an internal trait public. Can make it sealed/whatever, can probably do some shenanigans to move some of the code into std (right now it all lives in one place), or get rid of the custom trait, use AsRef<[char]> - this costs some performance, I have benchmark results somewhere.

topics.name: Request releasing new version of backtrace
topics.name_zh: Request releasing new version of backtrace
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：Windows 上运行 Rust 仓库的 `.\x check` 时，`backtrace 0.3.76` 在 `--cfg=windows_raw_dylib` 下出现函数调用约定类型不匹配错误：期望 `unsafe extern "C" fn`，实际为 `unsafe extern "system" fn`。该问题通常编译 Windows 版本的 `backtrace 0.3.75` 时不会触发。
- **重要观点与方案**：该问题已在 `backtrace-rs` 的 PR #744 中修复，但修复后尚未发布到 crates.io。使用 `[patch.crates-io]` 指向 backtrace Git 仓库可以绕过编译错误；相关发布请求也已有 issue #770。
- **已达成结论**：`backtrace 0.3.77` 已发布。手动将锁定版本更新为 `0.3.77` 后，`.\x check` 可以正常运行。
- **补充情况**：最新的 `priroda` 重构后使用了 Miri 的 `Cargo.lock`，默认锁定 `backtrace 0.3.75`；因此首次验证成功主要使用的是旧版本，手动更新到 `0.3.77` 后仍能正常工作。

That compile error only triggers under rustflags `--cfg=windows_raw_dylib`. It's added by bootstrap. Normally compiling backtrace 0.3.75 in windows is fine. 

After adding 
```
[patch.crates-io]
backtrace = { git = "https://github.com/rust-lang/backtrace-rs" }
```
to priroda `Cargo.toml` that compile error vanished.

So it seems that backtrace should release a new version to crates.io . (there is already an issue asking for that https://github.com/rust-lang/backtrace-rs/issues/770 )

topics.name_zh: Some UEFI and Command security bugs
topics.summary:
- 有人提交了多个与 UEFI 和 `Command` 相关的问题：UEFI 问题主要涉及行为异常的 UEFI drivers；`Command` 问题涉及攻击者可控制传给 `Command::new` 的可执行文件路径。Manish 认为它们不属于私下安全报告范围，风险也不算特别高，但可以进行加固。
- 讨论者认为这些问题不应按 security issue 处理。`Command` 问题曾由旧的 libs-api 讨论过，未来可能接受改进 patch 作为 QOL（quality of life）改进，也可能因负担过大而拒绝；该问题目前的安全性表述不恰当。
- 对提交内容的质量存在批评：部分建议可能有细微错误，例如主张静默忽略用户请求的参数，而不是 panic 或返回错误；另一个问题虽然看起来合理，但严重性和优先级尚不明确。`unimplemented!()` 加 `fixme` 也被认为缺乏说服力。
- 相关人员已要求提交者遵守 LLM policy，但对方没有听从，导致额外的审查时间浪费；团队认为后续在转交此类报告时可能需要更明确、更谨慎地强调该政策。提交者的 GitHub 用户名似乎也已从 `JoelBinu` 改为 `cueballcipher`。

topics.name: Impl Partial/Ord for Discriminant
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：是否应为 `Discriminant<T>` 提供排序能力。直接实现 `PartialOrd`/`Ord` 可能过于隐式，且会暴露枚举变体顺序等未稳定的实现细节。
- **主要方案**：提供显式的 `UnstableOrd` 包装类型，或增加类似 `f32::total_cmp` 的 `Discriminant::unstable_cmp` 方法；包装类型便于放入结构体并派生排序。有人建议可通过 `unstable_ord()` 获取，但不应设为 `unsafe`，因为这不涉及内存安全。
- **语义与限制**：文档应明确说明，第三方 crate 若调整变体顺序导致使用方代码行为变化，责任在使用方。`Discriminant<T>` 对任意 `T` 都可用；当前 rustc LLVM 后端中，非枚举类型的 discriminant 实际为 `0`。讨论倾向于将 `struct` 视为只有一个 variant 的类型，而不是读取其内部字节；后者还可能遇到未初始化字节。
- **进展与未决事项**：与会者认为显式方法或包装类型较为合理，并可能推进相关 FCP。Zac Harrold 已提交实现 PR `#164231`，并按要求创建 ACP `libs-team/issues/925`；聊天记录中尚未给出最终批准或稳定化结论。

messages.en: Was reading through some old `proposed-final-comment-period` PRs and came across https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/106418. I couldn't find it suggested, but how do people feel about providing an `UnstableOrd` wrapper which can be used to add ordering to `Discriminant<T>` for all `T`? Similar to how `std::path::Display` adds a `Display` implementation to `Path` and `bevy::math::FloatOrd` adds `Ord` to `f32` and `f64`. Could even make its construction `unsafe` if we're *really* concerned about exposing private implementation details?

Similar to how `std::path::Display` adds a `Display` implementation to `Path` and `bevy::math::FloatOrd` adds `Ord` to `f32` and `f64`. Could even make its construction `unsafe` if we're *really* concerned about exposing private implementation details?

topics.name: ✔ Weird (unreachable) alignment check in `subslice_range`
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`subslice_range` 文档称，当 `subslice` 未与 `self` 中的元素对齐时会返回 `None`。asquared31415 起初认为这条件不可能发生，因为两者都是 `&[T]`，都满足 `T` 的对齐要求。
- **重要澄清**：元素对齐不等同于类型对齐。即使指针满足 `T` 的对齐要求，子切片的起始位置仍可能落在元素中间，例如相对于元素边界偏移 `0.25`。实现检查的是字节偏移是否为 `size_of::<T>()` 的倍数，而不是 `align_of::<T>()`。
- **文档方案**：讨论认为现有措辞容易引起误解；`element_offset` 的文档表述“未指向切片中某个元素的起始位置”更清楚，且已有相关示例。asquared31415 同意据此改写并补充示例。
- **结论与状态**：asquared31415 提交了 PR #164937，并将话题标记为已解决；聊天记录未说明该 PR 是否已合并。

messages.en:
[subslice_range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.subslice_range) says:
> Returns `None` if `subslice` does not point within the slice **or if it is not aligned with the elements in the slice**.

(emphasis mine)

I think that that second condition is unreachable and potentially confusing to include in documentation, and should be removed. `self` and `subslice` are both `&[T]` for the same `T`, and there's a **validity** invariant on references that they must be well aligned. Given that both `self` and `subslice` must be aligned to at least the align of `T`, then `subslice` will always be well aligned compared to `self`.

Is there something that I'm missing, or some other reason to keep this around? LLVM appears to optimize out the check anyway, so it seems unlikely to me that anyone could be accidentally relying on this returning `None` with arguments that were already UB to construct.

(emphasis mine)

I think that that second condition is unreachable and potentially confusing to include in documentation, and should be removed. `self` and `subslice` are both `&[T]` for the same `T`, and there's a **validity** invariant on references that they must be well aligned. Given that both `self` and `subslice` must be aligned to at least the align of `T`, then `subslice` will always be well aligned compared to `self`.

Is there something that I'm missing, or some other reason to keep this around? LLVM appears to optimize out the check anyway, so it seems unlikely to me that anyone could be accidentally relying on this returning `None` with arguments that were already UB to construct.

topics.name: skipping ACP in obvious cases?

- 核心问题：对于像 #164848 这样明显属于疏漏、实现直接且团队大概率会接受的改动，是否可以跳过 ACP（API Change Proposal）流程。
- Jacob Pratt 倾向于在补充测试后直接接受该 PR，认为无需 ACP；他指出该改动是 unstable implementation，因此不涉及相应担忧。
- Max 以 #161531 为例指出，ACP 的适用规则似乎较为主观：该 PR 虽被告知可以跳过 ACP，但仍在 `proposed-fcp` 阶段停留了两个月。
- Fon 澄清：ACP 严格来说是可选流程，reviewer 可以自行判断是否有必要，因此不同 reviewer 可能作出不同决定。

topics.name: Pushing `breakpoint` over the finish line?
topics.name_zh: 正在推送`breakpoint`冲过终点线了？
topics.summary:
- **核心问题**：`breakpoint` intrinsic 的语义长期未能统一，主要分歧是继续执行后出现 UB 时由谁负责。讨论中的 `yeet1` 认为默认应将其视为不会继续执行，继续操作由 debugger 用户承担风险；`yeet2` 则要求程序本身必须在 `breakpoint()` 返回后保持无 UB，等价于程序应能承受 `breakpoint()` 被替换为 NOP。
- **编译器与优化行为**：目前普遍认为 `yeet1` 与 `yeet2` 在普通编译器优化和代码生成上没有区别（除 `const-eval`/Miri 行为外）；两者都应是至少和“可能退出程序”的操作一样强的 barrier，不能让后续 UB 向 `breakpoint()` 之前“时间旅行”。真正差异主要是 soundness 责任归属，以及 Miri/CTFE 如何处理。
- **主要倾向与方案**：多数参与者倾向 `yeet2`，认为名为 `breakpoint` 的操作应类似 debugger 中设置的断点，继续执行不应天然被视为 UB；若需要绝对终止，应使用 `abort_immediate()` 或循环。支持 `yeet1` 的观点则强调需要一个与底层 `int3`/debug-break 指令一一对应、默认中止但允许 debugger 用户强行继续的原语，尤其用于紧凑的 assert-like 调试代码。
- **可移植性与实现问题**：不同架构和环境对 breakpoint 指令的行为不同；某些目标（如旧 ARM、AVR、Wasm 以及部分 bare-metal 环境）可能在无 debugger 时继续、成为 NOP、只能循环或无法可靠触发调试器。因此 `yeet1` 可能无法在所有目标上实现，`yeet2` 更容易提供可移植语义，但“仅在 debugger 存在时暂停、否则 NOP”的行为需要 OS 支持，不能由 `core` 普遍保证。
- **当前结论与未解决事项**：尚未达成最终稳定化结论。讨论中形成的共识是应尽快选择并发布某种方案，且 `t-lang` 需要参与确定 intrinsic 的 opsem；可能的方向包括先稳定 `yeet2`（名称可为 `resumable_breakpoint` 或 `breakpoint`），以后再增加 `yeet1`，或同时提供两个明确命名的函数。仍未解决的问题包括最终的 soundness 规则、Miri/CTFE 默认应 abort 还是继续、不同目标的 fallback，以及两个相近 API 带来的命名和使用困惑。

messages.en: I feel like at this point, the only thing worse than picking the "wrong" one of these two is not picking either, and leaving Rust without an official way to trigger a breakpoint for another year. I have a clearly expressed preference that I will keep arguing for, but I would prefer the outcome of "t-libs picks the option I dont like" over "we dont pick anything".
messages.zh: 我觉得到了现在这个阶段，唯一比在这两个选项中选错更糟糕的事，就是一个都不选，让 Rust 再过一年仍然没有官方触发断点的方式。我确实有明确表达过自己的偏好，也会继续为此争论，但相比“什么都不选”，我更愿意接受“t-libs 选择了我不喜欢的那个选项”。

````
sorry i am new to this conversation, but the way i see it, `yeet1` and `yeet2` should probably have different type signatures. 
after all few things make behavior more clear than good typing.

`yeet1` should return a `FakeInhabited` type, with a safe `ex_nihilo::<T>(self) -> T` method that calls  `unreacheable_unchecked`, but would not otherwise register as uninhabited to the compiler, meaning producing it would not immediately mark the following code as unreacheable.
that would properly enshrine the fact that the following code is unreacheable (it is not possible to have `FakeInhabited` in safe reacheable code) but the compiler isn't aware of it unless we tell it.

`FakeInhabited` is actually a quite convenient type to have when one whishes to check ghost branches of code without having the borrow checker go "oh, an uninhabited type was produced, let's just ignore everything that follows"
messages.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622575547)：
````quote
`yeet1` 或 `yeet2`——因为 `trap` 显然有所不同，它的类型签名也不同
````
抱歉，我刚加入这个讨论，不过在我看来，`yeet1` 和 `yeet2` 可能本来就应该有不同的类型签名。

毕竟，很少有什么东西能比良好的类型设计更能让行为变得清晰。

`yeet1` 应该返回一个 `FakeInhabited` 类型，并提供一个安全的 `ex_nihilo::<T>(self) -> T` 方法，该方法会调用 `unreacheable_unchecked`；但它本身不应被编译器视为无 inhabitant 的类型，这意味着生成它不会立即让后续代码被标记为不可达。

这样就能恰当地确立这样一个事实：后续代码是不可达的（在安全且可达的代码中不可能存在 `FakeInhabited`），但除非我们明确告知编译器，否则编译器并不知道这一点。

当你想检查代码中的幽灵分支，又不希望借用检查器看到“哦，生成了一个无 inhabitant 的类型，那我们直接忽略后面的所有内容吧”时，`FakeInhabited` 实际上是一个相当方便的类型。

I think it would be very weird for us to have something called `breakpoint` which doesn't match what other languages do. And I think even if we want a breakpoint with special ub semantics, we'd still want the underlying thing that others use (aka yeet2 in the summary).

I don't love the longer name (`breakpoint_assume_noop`) for it but I'd live with it if it means we can stabilise something.

我不太喜欢更长的名称（`breakpoint_assume_noop`），但如果这意味着我们可以先稳定化某个东西，我也能接受。

messages.en:
It is in `core::arch` so I would kind of expect it to just follow platform semantics (although I guess it should really be in `core::os` since it's OS dependent). My problem with the longer names is they should ideally encapsulate that what it does can vary by platform, even if, the most common behaviour is consistent. We could also guard it with `is_debugger_attached()` but I don't think that's a good idea for the more primitive thing (and some platforms may not have a way to test for debugger presence).

But again, I'd be happy with any proposal that can gain consensus even if I think it less than ideal. We can stabilise whatever we call `yeet2` today but `yeet1` hasn't been implemented yet so we don't have to finalise its name (although having some idea would be good).
messages.zh:
它位于 `core::arch` 中，所以我多少会期待它直接遵循平台语义（不过我猜它实际上应该位于 `core::os`，因为它依赖操作系统）。我对较长名称的担忧是，它们理想情况下应该体现出该功能的行为可能因平台而异，即使最常见的行为是一致的。我们也可以用 `is_debugger_attached()` 对它进行保护，但我不认为这对于更底层的功能来说是个好主意（而且有些平台可能根本没有办法检测调试器是否存在）。

不过话说回来，只要某个提案能获得共识，即使我觉得它不够理想，我也会接受。我们今天就可以稳定化我们给 `yeet2` 取的任何名称，但 `yeet1` 还没有实现，因此我们不必现在就敲定它的名称（不过如果能有个大致想法就更好了）。

messages.en:
yeet2: whenever you write `breakpoint()` you have to make sure that it's okay for that to be a NOP, and the code that runs after `breakpoint()` returns (if it returns) has to run without UB.
or, equivalently: if your code becomes unsound when I replace `breakpoint()` by a NOP, then your code was already unsound before I did that.
messages.zh:
yeet2：每当你写下 `breakpoint()` 时，都必须确保即使它实际上是个 NOP 也没问题；并且 `breakpoint()` 返回之后运行的代码（如果它返回的话）必须能够在不触发 UB 的情况下运行。  
或者等价地说：如果把 `breakpoint()` 替换成 NOP 后你的代码就会变得不健全，那么在我这么做之前，你的代码就已经是不健全的。

messages.en: yeet1: whenever you write `breakpoint()`, you can if you want treat whatever comes after that function as dead code (but the code can make the choice that its okay to continue if it wants -- which means that the compiler will not treat it as dead code, it'll pretend that the code may actually run, so the asm you get is the same as for yeet2)
messages.zh: yeet1 ：每当你写`breakpoint()`，如果您想将该函数后面的任何内容视为死代码（但代码可以做出选择，如果需要，可以继续--这意味着编译器不会将其视为死代码，它会假装代码实际上可能运行，因此您获得的asm与yeet2相同）

messages.en: I think that in my head I had a similar summary. But what is the compiler allowed to do with this distinction, if it must be a fence in either case?

messages.en: I'm also in favor of yeet2. yeet1 would not be sound for systems where breakpoint instructions are automatically resumed if no debugger is attached (I don't know if such native systems exist, but it is more logical to me than aborting when no debugger is attached and matches how javascript handles `debugger;`)

messages.en:
For reference, C++ merely says the semantics of `std::breakpoint` is "implementation-defined". There is a note though:

> *Note 1*: When invoked the execution of the program temporarily halts and execution is handed to the debugger until such a time as: the program is terminated by the debugger or, the debugger resumes execution of the program as if the function was not invoked.  — *end note*
messages.zh:
供参考，C++ 只说 `std::breakpoint` 的语义是“由实现定义的”。不过有一条注释：

> *注 1*：调用时，程序的执行会暂时暂停，并将执行权交给调试器，直到发生以下情况之一：程序被调试器终止，或调试器恢复程序的执行，就好像从未调用过该函数一样。——*注释结束*

messages.en: I think it should be only `yeet2`. It doesn't make sense to me to tell people it's okay to pretend debuggers don't have a continue button. If you want things to be guaranteed to stop after the breakpoint, put an abort call there.
messages.zh: 我认为应该只有 `yeet2`。在我看来，告诉人们可以假装调试器没有继续执行按钮，是没有道理的。如果你希望断点之后一定停止，那就在那儿放一个 abort 调用。

messages.en: This means that `yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked()` isn't "sound", e.g. it won't save you from the effects of `unreachable_unchecked()` if it's all that's between your code and it,  but that doesn't mean it isn't useful. I could imagine writing a macro that expanded to `#[cfg(something)] yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked();` or something, so that you could get a breakpoint in a case when you thought was impossible.
messages.zh: 这意味着 `yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked()` 并不“安全”，例如，如果你的代码与它之间只有这一段代码，它也无法保护你免受 `unreachable_unchecked()` 影响；但这并不意味着它没有用。我可以想象写一个宏，展开成 `#[cfg(something)] yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked();` 之类的形式，这样在某个你认为不可能发生的情况下，也能触发断点。

messages.en: I don't think you can put this onto a user and say 'they should know it's UB to hit continue'. That's very strange. But if that's *really* what you want, it's not like you can't "outside the model" this for cases where you control the program, and put in your documentation "if you run my program in a debugger, pressing the continue button on any breakpoints is unsafe and unsupported". It would be very strange to do this, for sure, but that's why I think it's strange for Rust to have this as an invariant in a stdlib function.
messages.zh: 我不认为你可以把这件事推给用户，然后说“他们应该知道点击继续会导致 UB”。这非常奇怪。不过，如果这确实是你想要的，也不是不能在你控制程序的情况下把它置于“模型之外”，并在文档中写明：“如果你在调试器中运行我的程序，按下任何断点上的继续按钮都是不安全且不受支持的。”这么做当然会非常奇怪，但这正是我认为 Rust 不应该把它作为标准库函数不变量的原因。

messages.en:
Are these the rules we'd want for yeet2 semantics?

1. The only guarantee is that `breakpoint` will act as either a nop or an abort
2. If a debugger is attached, it should pause on `breakpoint()` but allow resuming (net nop)
3. If a debugger is not attached or if we have no way to do (2), `breakpoint()` *should* abort, but it is also defined behavior to be a nop
4. In Miri and CTFE (if we add that), `breakpoint` is a nop
messages.zh:
以下这些是我们希望采用的 yeet2 语义规则吗？

1. 唯一的保证是，`breakpoint` 将表现为 NOP 或 abort 二者之一
2. 如果连接了调试器，那么它应该在 `breakpoint()` 处暂停，但允许继续执行（实际效果等同于 NOP）
3. 如果没有连接调试器，或者我们没有办法做到第 2 点，那么 `breakpoint()` *应该* abort，但表现为 NOP 也属于有定义的行为
4. 在 Miri 和 CTFE 中（如果我们加入这一支持），`breakpoint` 是 NOP

messages.en:

or, equivalently: if your code becomes unsound when I replace `breakpoint()` by a NOP, then your code was already unsound before I did that.

I'm wondering if the recent discussions about "time-traveling UB" might be able to help here. Writing something like `breakpoint(); possible_ub();`, in the course of debugging `possible_ub()` is a lot like writing `eprintln!("about to maybe crash"); possible_ub();`, but stronger. In both cases, the UB of `possible_ub()` can't time-travel to before the previous statement, it can only happen after the breakpoint/eprintln. If you continue after the breakpoint, the program executes UB, and whatever that UB causes to happen will happen. If you *don't* continue after the breakpoint, the program didn't execute UB. (Just as, for instance, if you write "if the pointer is not null, dereference it", you aren't dereferencing a null pointer.)

或者，等价地说：如果把 `breakpoint()` 替换成 NOP 会让你的代码变得不健全，那么在我进行替换之前，你的代码就已经是不健全的。
```

我在想，最近关于“会穿越时间的 UB”的讨论也许能在这里帮上忙。在调试 `possible_ub()` 的过程中，写下类似 `breakpoint(); possible_ub();` 的代码，很像写下 `eprintln!("about to maybe crash"); possible_ub();`，但前者的保证更强。在这两种情况下，`possible_ub()` 的 UB 都不可能穿越时间回到前一条语句之前；它只能在 breakpoint/eprintln 之后发生。如果你在 breakpoint 之后继续执行，程序就会执行 UB，而这个 UB 导致发生的一切都会发生。如果你*不*在 breakpoint 之后继续执行，那么程序就没有执行 UB。（例如，如果你写下“如果指针不为空，就解引用它”，那么你并没有解引用空指针。）

messages.en: Nobody is claiming that the program *doesn't* have UB in it. But the no-time-traveling requirement makes the breakpoint still meaningful in that case: the program doesn't *execute* UB if you abort at the breakpoint and don't continue. Which is not the same thing as *not having* UB, but I'm hoping we broadly agree that it's still important in for breakpoints to be able to help you debug things.
messages.zh: 没人声称程序中*不存在* UB。但“不能穿越时间”的要求在这种情况下仍然让断点有意义：如果你在断点处 abort 而不继续执行，那么程序就不会*执行* UB。这和*不存在* UB 不是一回事，但我希望我们大体上都同意，对于断点来说，能够帮助你调试仍然很重要。

messages.en: I feel like the notion of somehow knowing, when you write the breakpoint, what you *want* to have happen (e.g. the user being able to continue or not) is implying a known-to-not-be-buggy program, which is somewhat incongruous with the idea of trying to debug it.
messages.zh: 我觉得，认为你在写下断点时就能以某种方式知道自己*希望*发生什么（例如用户能否继续执行），这实际上意味着你已经知道程序没有 bug；而这和尝试调试程序的想法多少有些矛盾。

My argument is that it's perfectly valid for someone to define a version of assert that uses a breakpoint instruction rather than a panic. Which is useful if you want something compact and usable in a no_std context, and as a bonus is convenient for getting a backtrace about the "shouldn't happen" condition that just happened. If you continue from that point without thinking about it, you may encounter the code the assert guarded against.
```

I'm not sure I agree that it's perfectly valid. It can be fine in some cases I suppose, but the reality is that this *is* a feature that exists and it's so intrinsic to the functionality of the debugger that I think it falls on the program that wants to do it to contend with (and document) the fact that they're doing something odd.

To be clear: People can do this if they want, but as I suggested above, they're taking it upon themselves to apply and document this extra safety requirement for running their program: you must not use a debugger to continue past a breakpoint. There's nothing wrong with a given program having additional safety requirements beyond what Rust provides (we often call this "outside the model"); this is how programs like ripgrep can support mmaping files without it being a violation of Rust's rules. If you do something like this, you are just supposed to communicate to the user what your additional requirements are, such as not truncating certain files, or not stepping in a debugger.

You can already use the unstable `std::process::abort_immediate()` for crash explosively. A debugger should catch the SIGILL and allow you to inspect the state of the process.

I'd love to see that stabilized *too*, but the difference with `breakpoint` is that *if the particular call site allows*, you have the option of *trying* to continue without even more invasive things. I think both permit lowering to `abort_immediate()` or `loop {}` (in practice `yeet2` probably permits lowering to a noop if that's *truly* all that can be done).

The fact that `yeet2` permits lowering to a no-op is precisely why I'm arguing against it. I'm not saying I've *never* seen an architecture that has no way to crash, but I've never seen one we're likely to port Rust to. And if you have a way to crash, you have a way to implement `breakpoint()`, as a fallback if there's no explicit breakpoint instruction.

messages.en: Here is an example where SIGTRAP is intentionally ignored to avoid crashing the program when there is no debugger attached: https://github.com/r-lyeh/tinybits/blob/2a735d9717c9da30fa7eb60c2cc158dee46f8d40/tinyassert.c#L34 Same here, but permanently sets the ignore (which would not be sound with yeet1): https://github.com/gan74/Yave/blob/1b37349d4f048884e461b82b39d0faf5c9d55b97/y/y/utils.cpp#L54, and another one: https://github.com/shacklettbp/madrona/blob/86457089d677d94e2826613c8ba62d180b50ab41/src/common/crash.cpp#L60-L62 Also https://github.com/roothide/Bootstrap-basebin/blob/c66454cdeb9c1c4dfefd62500fc54e5f458e1a61/launchdhook/main.m#L269 and https://github.com/tiwai/hda-emu/blob/38272fc445344d5ce9eea7341f6a06a04e3d21e3/hda-emu.c#L1528 Also some anti-debugger methods seem to rely on ignoring SIGTRAP.
messages.zh: 下面是一个示例，其中SIGTRAP被故意忽略，以避免在没有附加调试器的情况下导致程序崩溃：https://github.com/r-lyeh/tinybits/blob/2a735d9717c9da30fa7eb60c2cc158dee46f8d40/tinyassert.c#L34此处相同，但永久设置忽略（使用yeet1不会发出声音） ：https://github.com/gan74/Yave/blob/1b37349d4f048884e461b82b39d0faf5c9d55b97/y/y/utils.cpp#L54,另一个：https://github.com/shacklettbp/madrona/blob/86457089d677d94e2826613c8ba62d180b50ab41/src/common/crash.cpp#L60-L62你可能还喜欢…https://github.com/roothide/Bootstrap-basebin/blob/c66454cdeb9c1c4dfefd62500fc54e5f458e1a61/launchdhook/main.m#L269和https://github.com/tiwai/hda-emu/blob/38272fc445344d5ce9eea7341f6a06a04e3d21e3/hda-emu.c#L1528此外，一些反调试器方法似乎依赖于忽略SIGTRAP。

messages.en: @**bjorn3** Interestingly (and I'm currently trying to track down why this is), if you ignore SIGTRAP, int3 will *still* abort the program with SIGTRAP.
messages.zh: @ * * bjorn3 * *有趣的是（我目前正在尝试追踪原因） ，如果您忽略SIGTRAP ， int3将*仍然*使用SIGTRAP中止程序。

messages.en: Found it. At least on Linux, int3 will send a SIGTRAP using `force_sig`, which forcibly resets an ignored signal to `SIG_DFL` when sending it.
messages.zh: 找到了。至少在Linux上， int3将使用`force_sig`，强制将忽略的信号重置为`SIG_DFL`发送时。

messages.en: You *can* write a handler that explicitly ignores it, though. But it's a bad idea unless you know it's valid for all breakpoints in your program. Anti-debugger methods, to the extent they're legitimate, are essentially saying "we assert that there should never be a breakpoint instruction in this program (because if one is there it means someone's trying to debug us, which we don't want to allow)".
messages.zh: 不过，您*可以*编写一个明确忽略它的处理程序。但是，除非您知道它对程序中的所有断点都有效，否则这是一个坏主意。反调试器方法在合法的范围内基本上是说“我们断言这个程序中不应该有断点指令（因为如果有断点指令，则意味着有人试图调试我们，这是我们不希望允许的）”。

messages.en: Leaving aside race conditions on signal dispositions, `signal(SIGTRAP, SIG_IGN); raise(SIGTRAP);` is a valid way to spell "let this breakpoint be explicitly ignorable".
messages.zh: 撇开信号处理的竞争条件不谈，`signal(SIGTRAP, SIG_IGN); raise(SIGTRAP);`是拼写“let this breakpoint be explicitly ignorable”的有效方法。

messages.en: `raise(SIGTRAP)` is not the same as a breakpoint instruction.
messages.zh: `raise(SIGTRAP)`与断点指令不同。

messages.en:
@_**bjorn3|133247** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622847189):
```quote
And I disagree that it is a bad idea. With yeet2 it would be completely fine.
```

Even if we provided a function with that semantic, you have no guarantee that *every invocation of a breakpoint everywhere in your program* follows that semantic. You are free to assume that's the case, but that assumption is not *guaranteed* to be valid.
messages.zh:
@_* * bjorn3 | 133247 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622847189):
```quote
And I disagree that it is a bad idea. With yeet2 it would be completely fine.
```即使我们为该语义提供了一个函数，您也不能保证*程序中任何地方的每次断点调用*都遵循该语义。 您可以自由地假设情况确实如此，但这种假设并不能*保证*有效。

messages.en: Someone can always write their own `we_have_breakpoint_at_home()` function.
messages.zh: 有人可以随时自己写`we_have_breakpoint_at_home()`功能。

messages.en: I don't see someone somewhere using yeet1 in another language as reason to make breakpoint() in rust unsound to resume by defining our version as yeet1 too rather than as yeet2.
messages.zh: 我没有看到有人在某个地方使用另一种语言的yeet1作为理由，通过将我们的版本定义为yeet1而不是yeet2 ，使rust unound中的breakpoint ()恢复。

messages.en: It's not "unsound to resume", it's "caller-determined whether it can be resumed".
messages.zh: 这不是“恢复不当” ，而是“来电者决定是否可以恢复”。

messages.en: It's up to the code invoking it whether that's okay or not.
messages.zh: 这取决于调用它的代码是否可以。

messages.en: A `breakpoint()` in isolation would be unsound to resume, but the surrounding context may make it safe. I didn't say it is UB to resume.
messages.zh: A`breakpoint()`不宜恢复，但周围环境可能会使其安全。我没有说恢复是UB。

messages.en: Then I'm not sure why you're saying "would be unsound" rather than "may be unsound, depending on surrounding context".
messages.zh: 那么我不知道为什么你说“不健全”而不是“可能不健全，取决于周围的背景”。

messages.en: The surrounding context is what determines if unsound functions are actually UB or not.
messages.zh: 周围的上下文决定了不健全的函数是否真的是UB。

messages.en: I see. You're treating it the same way you'd treat a function `fn dereference_pointer(ptr: *const T) -> T`, which can be called in a valid way but is unsound because it's doing something unsafe and exposing it as a safe operation?
messages.zh: 我明白了。你对待它的方式与你对待功能的方式相同`fn dereference_pointer(ptr: *const T) -> T`，它可以以有效的方式调用，但不健全，因为它正在做一些不安全的事情，并将其暴露为安全操作？

messages.en: The point of my reference to `/proc/self/mem` earlier is that, in the spirit of "if UB happened there must be *some* unsafe operation somewhere that did something wrong", the debugger and every mutating operation the user uses it to do is essentially `unsafe { debugger(); }`.
messages.zh: 我所指的是`/proc/self/mem`早些时候是，本着“如果UB发生在某个地方一定有*一些*不安全的操作做错了什么”的精神，调试器和用户用来做的每一个变异操作本质上都是`unsafe { debugger(); }`。

messages.en: Yeah, in this case it would be something like `fn breakpoint() { notify_debugger(); while !user_continued() {} } unreachable_unchecked()`, which is unsound as `user_continued()` may eventually return true.
messages.zh: 是的，在这种情况下，它会像`fn breakpoint() { notify_debugger(); while !user_continued() {} } unreachable_unchecked()`，其不健全为`user_continued()`可能最终返回true。

messages.en: That's only true if you put the soundness burden on the breakpoint operation rather than on the debugger, which is the point of disagreement here.
messages.zh: 只有当您将稳健性负担放在断点操作上而不是调试器上时，才是真的，这是这里的分歧点。

messages.en:
> the debugger and every mutating operation the user uses it to do is essentially `unsafe { debugger(); }`.

In my view only modifying memory and registers or manually changing the instruction pointer are unsafe operations in a debugger. Just single stepping or continuing is equivalent to the compiler inserting/removing a very slow nop loop at arbitrary points in the program (aka not observable at all from inside the rust abstract machine, and thus allowed just fine).
messages.zh:
>用户使用的调试器和每个变更操作本质上是`unsafe { debugger(); }`.

在我看来，只有修改内存和寄存器或手动更改指令指针才是调试器中的不安全操作。 单步或继续相当于编译器在程序中的任意点插入/删除一个非常慢的nop循环（也就是说，从Rust抽象机器内部根本无法观察到，因此可以很好地观察到）。

messages.en: Single stepping or continuing can be equivalent to changing the instruction pointer. (And, in fact, precisely are on arm, where the trap occurs with a resumption address at the breakpoint rather than after the breakpoint.)
messages.zh: 单步或继续可以等同于更改指令指针。（而且，实际上，正好在ARM上，其中陷阱发生时在断点处而不是在断点之后使用恢复地址。）

messages.en: That is changing it in a way that the compiler expects to happen. If it didn't expect it, it would treat breakpoints as aborts and skip codegen of all code after it.
messages.zh: 这正在以编译器期望发生的方式改变它。如果没有预料到，它会将断点视为中止，并跳过其后所有代码的codegen。

messages.en: I feel like we're stuck in a loop here. There is, in fact, a third option, other than "must always abort" and "must always be resumable". I appreciate that it's not the option you want. But it's a valid option.
messages.zh: 我觉得我们陷入了一个循环。事实上，除了“必须始终中止”和“必须始终可恢复”之外，还有第三个选项。我明白这不是您想要的选择。但这是一个有效的选择。

messages.en: If continuing after a breakpoint compiled into the executable was considered dangerous, debuggers should ask for confirmation, not silently accept it IMO.
messages.zh: 如果在编译到可执行文件中的断点被认为是危险的之后继续，调试者应该要求确认，而不是默默地接受IMO。

messages.en: If writing code in C is considered dangerous, C compilers should ask for confirmation, not silently generate machine code. But that's not the era that C compilers were written in and it's not the era that debuggers were written in.
messages.zh: 如果用C编写代码被认为是危险的， C编译器应该要求确认，而不是默默地生成机器代码。但这不是编写C编译器的时代，也不是编写调试器的时代。

messages.en: Running a debugger is inherently an unsafe operation.
messages.zh: 运行调试器本质上是不安全的操作。

messages.en: Gdb and lldb ask for confirmation when doing several dangerous things like detaching or killing a process.
messages.zh: Gdb和lldb在做一些危险的事情（如分离或杀死一个过程）时会要求确认。

messages.en: I hope you're not asserting that gdb is written to a standard of "if it doesn't ask for confirmation then it must be completely safe".

messages.en: I know there are dangerous commands like setting variables or writing to arbitrary memory. However I would certainly hope that gdb warns me when running a command that is normally safe, but not in this specific case. Gdb doesn't warn when you try to attach to a process, unless doing so would cause another process to be killed or detached from for example. And it will ask before downloading debug symbols from the internet by default. And by default it won't run python scripts embedded in the target executable.

messages.zh: 我认为*大多数程序员认为*使用调试器进行步进只会修改程序的时间。

messages.en:
All that said, it occurs to me that there are two different use cases for debuggers that may influence what one assumes about their operation:

1. "My program is behaving incorrectly in a way I do not understand. I need a debugger to slow it down and let me look at the individual states."
2. "My program is crashing, and I need to analyze the crash state better than a single backtrace (or nothing)."
messages.zh:
尽管如此，在我看来，调试器有两种不同的用例，可能会影响人们对其操作的假设：

1. “我的计划行为不正确，我无法理解。 我需要一个调试器来减慢速度，让我看看各个状态。”
2. “我的程序正在崩溃，我需要比单个回溯（或无）更好地分析崩溃状态。”

messages.en: And in case 2, continuing is empirically unsafe (it will rarely do anything useful), but in case 1, it is not usually empirically unsafe (the program will keep doing its thing).
messages.zh: 在案例2中，继续在经验上是不安全的（它很少做任何有用的事情） ，但在案例1中，它通常不是经验上不安全的（程序将继续做它的事情）。

messages.en: And I wonder if you are assuming work in case 2, while I and @**bjorn3** am assuming work in case 1.
messages.zh: 我想知道你是否在案例2中假设工作，而我和@ * * bjorn3 * *在案例1中假设工作。

messages.en: I am not assuming that, no. I've certainly used a debugger for both. I'm suggesting that even in case 1, "Program received signal SIGTRAP, Trace/breakpoint trap" is not a message to which `c` is a universally safe answer.

messages.en: Note, in particular, that debuggers will typically loudly distinguish between a breakpoint *they set themselves* and a breakpoint instruction.
messages.zh: 特别要注意的是，调试器通常会大声区分*他们自己设置的*断点和断点指令。

messages.en:
A breakpoint the debugger set and knows about will look like, for instance:
`Breakpoint 1, 0x000055555555516d in main ()`
messages.zh: 例如，调试器设置并识别的断点看起来会像这样：`Breakpoint 1, 0x000055555555516d in main ()`

messages.en:

messages.en: I'm trying to figure out the degree to which seeing "breakpoint instruction" and thinking "that's inherently resumable" can reasonably be described as "incorrect assumption".

messages.en: I very much appreciate and agree with that. But I'm also suggesting that a name doesn't have to supersede a doc comment.

messages.en: I am theorizing that *using the word “breakpoint”* in the name of `yeet1` is too misleading for the broader audience.
messages.zh: 我的理论是， *在名称中使用“断点”一词*`yeet1`对更广泛的受众来说太误导了。

messages.en: I’m *less* worried if it’s spelled with the scarier-overall name `core::arch::breakpoint_instruction`, but also, I feel like this is a footgun we don’t need to manufacture when we can just have `yeet2`.

messages.en: ...I feel like that's going to send us back into the loop in which we are arguing about what semantics people *should* want vs *do* want.

messages.en: I'm not trying to prolong it or go around in circles, here, but it's *not helpful* to keep saying "you should be happy with just yeet2 and shouldn't get to have the operation you actually said you want".
