
那么，如果我有一个使用旧 edition、由旧代码编写的 crate，而它接收了一个定义在新 crate 中的结构体，那么旧代码就需要遵守子对象 provenance 规则吗？

messages.en: This seems like it's not contained to the crate boundary which I feel like is part of the requirement for editions
messages.zh: 这似乎意味着规则并不局限在 crate 边界之内，而我觉得 edition 的要求之一就是应该以 crate 边界为界。

messages.en: Kind of, but I think at least in contexts like https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/using-fam.html subobject provenance violations are very tightly bound to the struct being passed in? Accessing beyond the subobject only makes sense for specific structures that are specifically designed with that usage in mind, not generically.
messages.zh: 某种程度上是这样，但我认为至少在 https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/using-fam.html 这类场景中，子对象 provenance 违规行为与所传入的结构体有非常紧密的联系。只有针对特意为这种用法设计的特定结构体，访问超出子对象的部分才有意义，而不是对所有结构体都适用。

messages.en: IMO the edition change should take effect at the point where the reference is created, not based on the type. So `&x.y` in 2024 returns a reference with whole-allocation provenance, but in 2027 edition returns a reference restricted to the `y` field.
messages.zh: 我认为，edition 变更应该在创建引用的地方生效，而不是取决于类型。因此，2024 中的 `&x.y` 会返回具有整个分配 provenance 的引用，而在 2027 edition 中则会返回一个 provenance 受限于 `y` 字段的引用。

messages.en: so then if you use a struct from a 3rd-party crate that is edition 2024 in edition 2027 code, there is no way to return a `&Header` with provenance for the data after the header since creating a reference causes sub-object provenance, but you can do that in edition 2024? that seems like the wrong way to me
messages.zh: 那么，如果你在 edition 2027 的代码中使用一个来自第三方 crate、且该 crate 使用 edition 2024 的结构体，就无法返回一个具有 header 之后数据 provenance 的 `&Header`，因为创建引用会导致子对象 provenance；但在 edition 2024 中却可以做到？这在我看来似乎不是正确的做法。

messages.en: it works much better if it's based on which edition the struct is defined in so `Header` from an edition 2024 crate still works when used in an edition 2027 crate, and when the struct definition is changed to edition 2027 it can have the opt-out of subobject provenance attribute, so keeps working
messages.zh: 如果根据结构体定义所在的 edition 来决定，效果会好得多：这样，来自 edition 2024 crate 的 `Header` 在 edition 2027 crate 中使用时仍然可以正常工作；而当结构体定义改为 edition 2027 时，可以通过属性选择退出子对象 provenance，从而继续保持正常工作。

messages.en: Making it based on the edition where the struct is defined means it's a breaking change for the defining crate to update its edition without opting every single one of its types out of subobject provenance
messages.zh: 如果根据结构体定义所在的 edition 来决定，那么定义该结构体的 crate 在更新 edition 时，如果不为它的每一个类型都选择退出子对象 provenance，就会构成破坏性变更。

messages.en: That only applies to types with public fields as you can't create a reference to private fields outside of the defining crate, right?
messages.zh: 不过，这只适用于字段为 public 的类型，对吧？因为在定义它的 crate 外部无法创建指向私有字段的引用。

messages.en: Suppose a crate provides `fn as_header(&self) -> &Header` and `unsafe fn from_header(&Header) -> &Self`.
messages.zh: 假设某个 crate 提供了 `fn as_header(&self) -> &Header` 和 `unsafe fn from_header(&Header) -> &Self`。

messages.en:
based on the discussion above and at the recent t-opsem meeting, it seems like at least 3 out of 5 opsem members would be fine with saying "there is no subobject provenance on types that currently exist in the language, except maybe for enums". The main arguments are
- a bunch of existing code assumes this already for arrays and slices
- a lot of code generated by bindgen assumes this at least for repr(C) structs
- `#[repr]` shouldn't affect the opsem in such subtle ways
- the benefits of this UB are unclear. there are optimizations one can sketch where this is useful, but the fact that LLVM has no way of even representing this makes it look like there's no that much to be had here in terms of practically useful optimizations.

@**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** you weren't at that meeting -- I wonder what your thoughts on this are?
messages.zh:
根据上面的讨论以及最近的 t-opsem 会议，至少 5 位 opsem 成员中的 3 位似乎都可以接受这样的说法：“对于语言目前已有的类型，不存在 subobject provenance；枚举或许例外。”主要论据如下：

- 大量现有代码已经假定数组和切片不存在这种 provenance
- bindgen 生成的大量代码至少对 `repr(C)` 结构体做了这样的假定
- `#[repr]` 不应该以如此微妙的方式影响 opsem
- 这种 UB 的收益并不明确。我们可以设想一些它有用的优化，但 LLVM 甚至没有办法表示这种信息，这让人觉得它在实际有用的优化方面并没有多少可发挥的空间。

@**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** 你们当时没参加那次会议——想知道你们对此有什么看法？

messages.en: SRoA is one of those optimizations that doesn't do much on its own but enables major optimizations since it allows the rest of the compiler to know when fields can be treated as independent variables so it knows that opaque function calls can't clobber or read them
messages.zh: SRoA 属于那种单独来看作用不大、但能启用重大优化的优化，因为它让编译器的其余部分知道哪些字段可以被当作相互独立的变量处理，从而知道不透明的函数调用不会覆写或读取它们。

无论我们如何处理 subobject provenance，Rust 中（对一个指向字段的指针会逃逸的结构体）执行 SRoA 基本上都没戏，因为即使是在完全安全的 Rust 中，也仍然可以观察到各种指针的地址彼此之间是什么关系。

messages.en: I don't think LLVM's SRoA currently does this, but it's possible to promote some fields of an aggregate to SSA values while still keeping the original local, if subobject provenance proves that the escaping pointers can only access a subset of fields. For example, for a local `pair: (u32, f32)` where only `&pair.0` escapes, all mentions of `pair.1` could be redirected to a separate local `pair_1: f32`. This effectively takes subobject provenance reasoning and recasts it into separate objects to help LLVM's object-based provenance reasoning.
messages.zh:
我不认为 LLVM 当前的 SRoA 会这样做，不过，如果 subobject provenance 能证明那些逃逸的指针只能访问字段的一个子集，那么就有可能在保留原始局部变量的同时，将聚合类型中的某些字段提升为 SSA 值。

例如，对于一个局部变量 `pair: (u32, f32)`，如果只有 `&pair.0` 会逃逸，那么所有涉及 `pair.1` 的地方都可以重定向到一个单独的局部变量 `pair_1: f32`。这样实际上就把 subobject provenance 的推理重新表述成了独立对象，从而帮助 LLVM 进行基于对象的 provenance 推理。

````quote
sorry I dont want to spend 10-20 minutes figuring out what you want to demonstrate with this entirely uncommented example. can you explain / add comments please?
````

In the Rust version LLVM can't prove that accesses through `elements` don't also access `start`, which means that on every loop iteration it must write `start` back to memory so that the access via `elements` sees the correct value. The C++ version with TBAA doesn't have this problem because the individual elements of `elements` and `start` have different types. If you change the C++ code to have an array of `size_t` instead of `double` then it also loses the optimization and has to write back `start` on every loop iteration.

在 Rust 版本中，LLVM 无法证明通过 `elements` 的访问不会同时访问 `start`，这意味着在每次循环迭代中，它都必须把 `start` 写回内存，以便通过 `elements` 的访问能看到正确的值。使用 TBAA 的 C++ 版本没有这个问题，因为 `elements` 和 `start` 的各个元素类型不同。如果把 C++ 代码改成使用 `size_t` 数组而不是 `double` 数组，它同样会失去这项优化，并且必须在每次循环迭代中写回 `start`。

C++ definitely has it also. There's a specific concept called pointer-interconvertible for union fields and the first field of a standard-layout struct (or the base classes of a fieldless standard-layout struct), that allows freely casting narrow-to-wide, then disallows leaving the bounds of an object otherwise, except to index other elements of the immediately enclosing array (std::lauder calls this "reachability")


C++ 肯定也有这个。对于联合体字段和标准布局结构体的第一个字段（或者无字段标准布局结构体的基类），有一个专门的概念叫作 pointer-interconvertible，它允许自由地进行从窄指针到宽指针的转换；除此之外，指针不能越出对象边界，唯一的例外是可以索引直接包含它的数组中的其他元素（std::lauder 将此称为“可达性”）

messages.en:
We could say that if a local of an SRoA-eligible struct type does not have its address taken at any point, then its individual fields are treated as separate locals and can have offsets that differ from what the struct layout would prescribe. ("Does not have its address taken at any point" would be defined syntactically; e.g. an `&local` anywhere in the source, even in dead code, amounts to "taking the address".)

There are plenty of reasons why this particular approach might not be a good idea—making `&local` have spooky-action-at-a-distance among them—but hopefully it demonstrates that this is *possible* to support, and maybe there's a cleaner way.
messages.zh:
我们可以规定：如果某个符合 SRoA 条件的结构体类型局部变量在任何时候都没有获取其地址，那么它的各个字段就被视为独立的局部变量，并且其偏移量可以不同于结构体布局所规定的偏移量。（“在任何时候都没有获取其地址”将通过语法来定义；例如，源代码中的任何位置出现 `&local`，即使位于死代码中，也算作“获取地址”。）

这种具体做法有很多理由可能并不是好主意——让 `&local` 产生令人难以预料的远距离影响就是其中之一——但希望这能说明，支持这一点是*可能的*，也许还存在更简洁的方式。

Yes, but for things like sroa across unknown functions you need to allow for char* (and uintptr_t) casts. And as that linked q&a mentions it is at most unclear if there is any subobject stuff going on in any of the old C specs. The original actual-provenance proposals that are intended to clarify things didn't have any subobject provenance.

And that q&a is really inconsistent about the situation in c2x proposals in general - it says "c2x proposal: yes", but then in the text says that while they could, their current proposal doesn't. And then their actual proposal doesn't seem like it would allow any of the optimizations anyway because "Then on any cast, we'd expand the subrange to that of the original allocation", so any escaped subobject pointer has to be considered an escaped allocation pointer.
messages.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607415902)：``````quote 它一直都是这样。C 只允许在数组内部进行指针算术运算。字段之间的算术运算是未定义行为。`````` 是的，但对于跨越未知函数进行 sroa 之类的情况，你需要允许 char*（以及 uintptr_t）转换。而且，正如那个链接中的问答所提到的，旧版 C 规范中是否存在任何子对象相关的内容，最多只能说是不明确。那些旨在澄清这一点的、最初提出的真实来源信息方案中，并没有任何子对象来源信息。 另外，那个问答对于 c2x 提案整体上的情况也说得非常不一致——它写着“c2x 提案：是”，但正文又说，虽然他们可以这么做，但当前的提案并没有这样做。而且，他们实际提出的方案似乎无论如何都不允许这些优化，因为“然后在每次转换时，我们都会将子范围扩展为原始分配的范围”，这样一来，任何逃逸的子对象指针都必须被视为逃逸的分配指针。

@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607108666):
```quote
based on the discussion above and at the recent t-opsem meeting, it seems like at least 3 out of 5 opsem members would be fine with saying "there is no subobject provenance on types that currently exist in the language, except maybe for enums". The main arguments are
- a bunch of existing code assumes this already for arrays and slices
- a lot of code generated by bindgen assumes this at least for repr(C) structs
- `#[repr]` shouldn't affect the opsem in such subtle ways
- the benefits of this UB are unclear. there are optimizations one can sketch where this is useful, but the fact that LLVM has no way of even representing this makes it look like there's no that much to be had here in terms of practically useful optimizations.

@**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** you weren't at that meeting -- I wonder what your thoughts on this are?
```

Well considering that my enum proposal depends on subobject provenance, you should expect I'm in favor of having it in at least those cases (with or without niche optimization, i.e. subobject provenance for `Option<u8>` too). I have already written extensively on the benefits to UB I perceive for this
messages.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607108666)：```quote 基于上面的讨论以及最近一次 t-opsem 会议上的讨论，看起来至少有 5 位 opsem 成员中的 3 位愿意接受这样的说法：“对于目前语言中已有的类型，不存在子对象来源信息，枚举类型或许除外。”主要理由如下：- 现有的一些代码已经假定数组和切片是这样的 - bindgen 生成的大量代码至少对 repr(C) 结构体作了这样的假定 - `#[repr]` 不应以如此微妙的方式影响 opsem - 这种未定义行为的好处并不明确。我们可以设想出一些在这种情况下有用的优化，但 LLVM 甚至没有办法表示这一点，这似乎说明从实际有用的优化角度来看，这里并没有太多可得之处。 @**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** 你们当时没参加那次会议——我想知道你们对此有什么看法？``` 考虑到我的枚举提案依赖于子对象来源信息，你们应该能预料到，我赞成至少在这些情况下保留它（无论是否进行 niche 优化，也就是说，`Option<u8>` 也应具有子对象来源信息）。我已经详细阐述过，我认为这种未定义行为有哪些好处。

messages.en: yes. how does that rely on array and struct field projections restricting the reference to only be allowed to access the field/element?
messages.zh: 是的。那这怎么依赖于数组和结构体字段投影限制引用，使其只能访问对应的字段或元素呢？

messages.en: and in a 2-field enum, how do you rely on pointers to one field not being allowed to access the other field?
messages.zh: 而对于一个有两个字段的枚举，你又是如何依赖于“不允许指向其中一个字段的指针访问另一个字段”这一点的呢？

messages.zh: 在我看来，目前还不清楚你说的是投影运算符，还是类型。

messages.en: the last messages sounds like projections but the discussion about repr(C) etc is about types
messages.zh: 你最后几条消息听起来像是在说投影，但关于 repr(C) 等内容的讨论说的是类型。

messages.en: subobject provenance is something that "happens" during projections -- the newly created reference gets a provenance that is restricted to just the bytes inside the field
messages.zh: 子对象来源信息是在投影过程中“产生”的——新创建的引用会获得一个来源信息，而这个来源信息被限制为仅涵盖字段内部的字节。

messages.en: I agree that this "should" be about projections
messages.zh: 我同意，这件事“应该”是关于投影的。

messages.en: since each projection has a base type we can talk about all projections to fields of repr(C) types etc
messages.zh: 由于每次投影都有一个基础类型，我们可以讨论对 repr(C) 类型字段的所有投影，等等。

messages.en: which is tedious to spell out and it seemed sufficiently obvious that that's what we mean when we talk about "subobject provenance for repr(C) types"
messages.zh: 只是把这些都明确说出来很麻烦；而且当我们谈论“repr(C) 类型的子对象来源信息”时，这样的含义已经足够明显了。

messages.en: I understand that's what you mean, but the framing suggested that we should be looking at classification of types into good and bad rather than projections
messages.zh: 我明白你的意思，但这种表述让人觉得我们应该关注的是把类型分类为好和坏，而不是关注投影。

messages.en: but, taking a step back -- your enum proposal adds a bunch of extra state and checks specifically for enum discriminants. that seems enough to achieve your goals even if we dont *also* set up the Tree Borrows state machine in a way taht it restricts access to certain bytes?
messages.zh: 不过退一步说——你的枚举提案专门为枚举判别式增加了一堆额外状态和检查。即使我们不以限制对某些字节的访问的方式来设置 Tree Borrows 状态机，这似乎也已经足以实现你的目标了，不是吗？

messages.en: so I dont understand how your poposal relies on subobject provenance -- where by "subobject provenance" I specifically mean "when creating a reference, mark only some bytes as being permitted to be read/written via this reference, and make it insta-UB to read/write any other bytes"
messages.zh: 所以我不明白你的提案是如何依赖子对象 provenance 的——这里我所说的“子对象 provenance”特指：创建引用时，只标记某些字节允许通过该引用进行读写，并且一旦读写其他任何字节就立即产生 UB。

messages.en: No, that *only* works on niche optimized enums. If you do it without subobject provenance, non-optimized enums are subject to the same problem
messages.zh: 不，那只对经过 niche 优化的枚举有效。如果不采用子对象 provenance，未优化的枚举也会遇到同样的问题。

messages.en: and the same solution, no?
messages.zh: 而且解决方案也是一样的，对吧？

messages.en: to make the enum thing work we need a solution for this that works without subobject provenance
messages.zh: 要让枚举这件事可行，我们需要一个不依赖子对象 provenance 的解决方案。

messages.en: we might as well use that solution for all enums then?
messages.zh: 那我们干脆把这个解决方案用于所有枚举，不就行了？

messages.en: It sounds like you are okay with subobj prov for enum downcast
messages.zh: 听起来你可以接受在枚举向下转型时使用子对象 provenance。

messages.en: that's all we need for the corresponding property to hold for the non-niched enums
messages.zh: 对于未使用 niche 的枚举，要满足相应的性质，我们只需要做到这一点。

messages.en: unclear if protectors yield this
messages.zh: 不确定保护器是否能实现这一点。

messages.zh: 再说一次，我考虑的是 Rust 更遥远的未来。

messages.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607624710) in #**t-opsem>Vibes on subobject provenance**:
```quote
I think we lack alternative mechanisms which make it easier to avoid the bad case
```
given 10 years of precedent I dont think the theoretical existence of such mechanisms is relevant
messages.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** 在 #**t-opsem>Vibes on subobject provenance** 中[说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607624710)： “我觉得我们缺少一些替代机制，让人更容易避开糟糕的情况。” 鉴于过去 10 年的先例，我不认为这类机制在理论上的存在具有什么相关性

messages.en: I understand there are problems at present
messages.zh: 我明白目前确实存在一些问题

messages.en: Im not going to sacrifice our current users on the altar of a hypothetical ideal future Rust
messages.zh: 我不会为了一个假想中的理想 Rust 未来，而牺牲我们当前的用户

messages.en: this is a "better things aren't possible" argument
messages.zh: 这是一种“做不到更好”的论证

messages.en: we're talking about an opsem for *current* Rust
messages.zh: 我们讨论的是针对*当前* Rust 的操作语义

messages.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607625177):
```quote
this is a "better things aren't possible" argument
```

no, it's a "the real world of existing code matters" argument
messages.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607625177)： “这是一种‘做不到更好’的论证。” 不，这是在说“现实世界中已有的代码很重要”

messages.en: I am okay with taking an opsem for current rust which lacks subobject provenance if we couple this with some amount of thinking on how we can get away from it in the next edition or w/e
messages.zh: 如果我们同时花些精力思考如何在下一个版本或之类的时机摆脱它，那么我可以接受采用一种缺少子对象来源的当前 Rust 操作语义

messages.en: I just worry that this will become part of the stable surface and it will become even more impossible to change in the future
messages.zh: 我只是担心它会成为稳定接口的一部分，以后就更加不可能改变了

messages.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607625390):
```quote
I am okay with taking an opsem for current rust which lacks subobject provenance
```
that is good to hear

> if we couple this with some amount of thinking on how we can get away from it in the next edition or w/e

various avenues for evolving this exist, though of course as you know evolving things around unsafe is particularly tricky. it pretty much has to be opt-in, or all "old" types would have to get the opt-out attribute during the transition which would be a gigantic amount of churn.
do you see any alternative option for the current opsem that would make future evolution easier without risking breaking tons of existing code? the only option I can imagine is to make it dependent on the `repr` of the struct that contains the projected field, but there are pretty good argument against that.
messages.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607625390)： “我可以接受采用一种缺少子对象来源的当前 Rust 操作语义。” 听到你这么说真不错。> 如果我们同时花些精力思考如何在下一个版本或之类的时机摆脱它，演进它的路径有很多，不过当然，正如你所知，围绕 `unsafe` 进行演进尤其棘手。它基本上必须是选择加入的；否则，在过渡期间，所有“旧”类型都得加上选择退出的属性，那将造成巨量的改动。对于当前的操作语义，你能想到什么替代方案，既能让未来的演进更容易，又不会冒着破坏大量现有代码的风险吗？我能想到的唯一方案，是让它取决于包含被投影字段的结构体的 `repr`，但反对这样做的理由也相当充分。

messages.en: are there any patterns which exist in the wild which weren't already dubious at best?
messages.zh: 现实世界中有没有什么模式，至少不是从一开始就很可疑的？

messages.en: whether they are dubious heavily depends on your PoV
messages.zh: 它们是否可疑，很大程度上取决于你的视角

messages.en: at the very least something that would be written after knowing that subobject provenance is a thing and failing to find a better option
messages.zh: 至少得是那种在知道子对象来源确实存在之后，找不到更好方案才会写出来的代码

messages.en: we never gave any indication to programmers that references should be considered to be "contained to their fields" even when turned into raw pointers
messages.zh: 我们从未向程序员暗示过：即使引用被转换成原始指针，也应该认为它们是“局限于各自字段之内的”

messages.en: rather than just "I thought this was C with better syntax"
messages.zh: 而不只是“我以为这就是语法更好的 C”

messages.en: you can't leap allocations using raw pointer offsets though
messages.zh: 不过，使用原始指针偏移也无法跨越分配

messages.en: it doesn't seem to be that different to me unless you are designing a formal checker
messages.zh: 在我看来，这似乎并没有什么不同，除非你是在设计形式化检查器

messages.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607626882):
```quote
various avenues for evolving this exist,
```

FWIW I quite like the idea of providing people extra tools they can use in hot loops to help the optimizer, rather than inflicting extra UB on everyone everywhere, so a dedicated `fn restrict_provenance<T>(x: &mut T) -> &mut T` (not even unsafe!) sounds like a pretty nice option to me
messages.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607626882)： “演进它的路径有很多，” 顺便说一句，我相当喜欢这样一种思路：提供一些额外工具，让人们可以在热点循环中使用它们来帮助优化器，而不是把额外的 UB 强加给所有人、所有地方。所以，提供一个专用的 `fn restrict_provenance<T>(x: &mut T) -> &mut T`（甚至不需要是 unsafe）对我来说听起来是个相当不错的选择

messages.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607627740):
```quote
it doesn't seem to be that different to me unless you are designing a formal checker
```

it's very different (at least when considering arrays and repr(C) types) since you cant predict the distance between allocations
messages.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607627740)： “在我看来，这似乎并没有什么不同，除非你是在设计形式化检查器。” 差别非常大（至少在考虑数组和 repr(C) 类型时），因为你无法预测各个分配之间的距离

messages.en: maybe this is the difference, I don't see it as inflicting extra UB on everyone everywhere, I see it as inflicting a weird model of validity on everyone everywhere
messages.zh: 也许这就是区别所在：我不认为这是把额外的 UB 强加给所有人、所有地方；我认为这是把一种奇怪的有效性模型强加给所有人、所有地方

messages.en: if anything the model with subobject provenance is "weird", it needs some extra state and complexities to generate the extra UB
messages.zh: 如果说有什么的话，带有子对象溯源的模型才是“怪异”的；它需要额外的状态和复杂性，才能产生额外的 UB

messages.en: certainly a flat model would be easier
messages.zh: 当然，扁平模型会更简单

messages.en: but we've already committed to that extra state anyway
messages.zh: 但反正我们已经决定采用那种额外状态了

messages.en: no? TB as-is has no subobject provenance
messages.zh: 不是吧？按现状来看，TB 没有子对象溯源

messages.en: TB is much harder than a flat memory model with bytes at positions
messages.zh: TB 比那种在各个位置存放字节的扁平内存模型要难得多

messages.en:
true. I never said it wasnt so... not sure why you're bringing this up.
but even compared to that we need to make it even weirded to get subobject provenance.
(that's obviously the baseline I was comparing with above.)
messages.zh: 没错。我从没说过不是这样……不太明白你为什么要提这个。即便与那种模型相比，我们还得把它弄得更怪，才能实现子对象溯源。（显然，我上面比较的基准就是那个。）

messages.en: I think this perspective is something that only a TB maintainer would have
messages.zh: 我觉得，这种视角恐怕只有 TB 维护者才会有

messages.en: I would rather explain TB in terms of the properties it ensures rather than by its mechanistic behavior
messages.zh: 我更愿意从 TB 所保证的性质来解释它，而不是从它的机制行为来解释

messages.en: like "if you take a reference you get access to those bytes"
messages.zh: 比如说，“如果你拿到了一个引用，你就能访问那些字节”

messages.en:
eh, happy to consider an alternative aliasing model as baseline.
but currently it just sounds like you trying to invalidate my arguments based on them being made by me :shrug:
messages.zh: 呃，我很乐意考虑把另一种别名模型作为基准。不过目前听起来，你只是因为这些论点是我提出来的，就想让它们失效 :shrug:

messages.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629059):
```quote
I would rather explain TB in terms of the properties it ensures rather than by its mechanistic behavior
```

that sounds like you're thinking about a type system and safety invariants. we're not in that world here though.
messages.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629059)：
```quote
我更愿意从 TB 所保证的性质来解释它，而不是从它的机制行为来解释
```

听起来你是在用类型系统和安全不变量的思路考虑问题。但我们现在讨论的并不是那个语境。

messages.en: I mean that TB vs TB+epsilon is not distinguishable to the outsider
messages.zh: 我的意思是，对于局外人来说，TB 和 TB+epsilon 是无法区分的

messages.en: it is if their code gets miscompiled / flagged by miri ;)
messages.zh: 如果他们的代码被错误编译，或者被 miri 标记出来，那当然能区分 ;)

messages.en: it's already got more moving parts than the average person can keep in their head
messages.zh: 它包含的组成部分已经比一般人能记住的还多了

messages.en: I don't think that optimizing that model is necessarily a primary goal, because explaining the model to a layman is not its primary purpose
messages.zh: 我不认为优化这个模型一定是首要目标，因为向外行解释这个模型本来就不是它的首要用途

messages.en: and subobject provenance is not an "epsilon" change to how much code gets flagged by miri, it's a pretty significant change
messages.zh: 而且，子对象溯源并不是对有多少代码会被 miri 标记这种情况做出的“epsilon”级别的改动，而是相当重大的变化

messages.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629614):
```quote
I don't think that optimizing that model is necessarily a primary goal, because explaining the model to a layman is not its primary purpose
```

very strong hard disagree on that. enough people will want to / have to dig to the bottom of our "tower of weakenings" that it's definitely important to keep this in mind.
messages.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629614)：
```quote
我不认为优化这个模型一定是首要目标，因为向外行解释这个模型本来就不是它的首要用途
```

对此我强烈不同意。会想要或不得不深入探究我们“层层弱化的塔”的人足够多，所以牢记这一点绝对很重要。

messages.en: it is rather intended to balance good properties for optimization with an easy mental model
messages.zh: 它的目标本来就是在有利于优化的良好性质和易于理解的心智模型之间取得平衡

messages.en: (also, here the simpler low-level model aligns with less UB on the high-level which means it's also easier to use even without knowing the details)
messages.zh: （而且，在这里，更简单的底层模型意味着高层的 UB 更少，这也意味着即使不了解细节，它也更容易使用）

messages.en: so I would rank ease of description at 2 or 3, it's important but not most important
messages.zh: 所以我会把易于描述排在第二或第三位；这很重要，但不是最重要的

messages.en: having a useful tower of weakenings is IMO even more important
messages.zh: 在我看来，拥有一套实用的弱化层级甚至更加重要

messages.en: every weaker tower floor that's valid on TB + subobject provenance is also valid on TB - subobject provenance, so "having a useful tower" cannot possibly ever be an argument for subobject provenance
messages.zh: 任何在 TB + subobject provenance 上有效的更弱层级，在 TB - subobject provenance 上也同样有效，因此“拥有一套实用的层级”不可能成为支持 subobject provenance 的论据

messages.en: I'm not sure I agree with that, at a higher level of the tower of weakenings how do you explain that the code I gave can fail?
messages.zh: 我不确定是否同意这一点。在弱化层级中处于更高层级时，你要如何解释我给出的代码为什么会失败？

messages.en: it's a pretty obvious theorem
messages.zh: 这是一个相当显然的定理

messages.en: because a weaker tower level can only ever say "dont do X", it can never say "X is definitely UB"
messages.zh: 因为更弱的层级只能说“不要做 X”，永远不能说“X 肯定是 UB”

messages.en: if my rule is "pointers can't access out of your region" then that code should not be able to fail
messages.zh: 如果我的规则是“指针不能访问你所在区域之外的内容”，那么那段代码就不应该能够失败

messages.en: that's not a weakening
messages.zh: 那不是弱化

messages.en: also that sounds like a safety invariant thing
messages.zh: 而且这听起来像是安全性不变量的问题

messages.en: it's an incomplete explanation of what is happening
messages.zh: 这是对实际发生情况的不完整解释

messages.en: so yes it is a weakening IMO, although I understand that I'm basically exploiting a contravariance issue here
messages.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这确实是弱化，尽管我明白自己基本上是在利用这里的一个逆变问题

messages.en: but I think programmers do both kinds of reasoning (what can I do, what can I trust others will not do)
messages.zh: 但我认为程序员会进行这两种推理（我能做什么，以及我可以相信别人不会做什么）

messages.en: we dont use the opsem to restrict what others will do
messages.zh: 我们不会用操作语义来限制别人会做什么

messages.en: that's not even valid reasoning since we always can remove UB from the opsem
messages.zh: 这种推理甚至不成立，因为我们始终可以从操作语义中移除 UB

messages.en: only the type system can restrict what others will do, so it's not really part of this discussion
messages.zh: 只有类型系统才能限制别人会做什么，所以这其实不属于本次讨论的内容

messages.en: I don't see how types help here
messages.zh: 我看不出类型在这里能提供什么帮助

messages.en: the code I wrote is 100% safe
messages.zh: 我写的代码是 100% 安全的

messages.en: ~~maybe they dont, but the opsem surely doesnt^^~~
messages.zh: ~~也许类型系统不会，但操作语义肯定不会这样做^^~~

messages.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607631453):
```quote
the code I wrote is 100% safe
```

yes and for soundness if it calls an arbitrary opaque function the code can entirely rely on that function not mutating outside the reference
messages.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607631453)：
```quote
我写的代码是 100% 安全的
```

是的；而为了保证健全性，如果它调用了任意的不透明函数，那么代码完全可以依赖于该函数不会修改引用所指范围之外的内容

messages.en: the type system already ensures that
messages.zh: 类型系统已经保证了这一点

messages.en: the function only receives ownership of the field in question
messages.zh: 该函数只获得了相关字段的所有权

messages.en: but all that is safety invariant / type system reasoning
messages.zh: 但这些都属于安全性不变量／类型系统推理

messages.en: so please explain to me why we go from "this is unsound" to "everyone does this" when discussing subobj prov
messages.zh: 所以，在讨论 subobj prov 时，请你解释一下，为什么我们会从“这是不健全的”转而说“大家都这么做”

messages.en: https://www.ralfj.de/blog/2018/08/22/two-kinds-of-invariants.html
messages.zh: https://www.ralfj.de/blog/2018/08/22/two-kinds-of-invariants.html

messages.en: I hope everyone doesn't break the rules, otherwise rust wouldn't be a very useful language
messages.zh: 我希望不是所有人都会违反规则，否则 Rust 就不会是一门很有用的语言了

messages.en: people dont do this *across APIs calling arbitrary unknown functions*
messages.zh: 人们不会在跨 API 调用任意未知函数时这么做

messages.en: but that's the case I'm talking about?
messages.zh: 但我说的就是这种情况，不是吗？

messages.en: they do it internally within their crate, or between cooperating crates
messages.zh: 他们会在自己的 crate 内部这么做，或者在相互协作的 crate 之间这么做

messages.en: that's what you are suggesting to make UB
messages.zh: 而这正是你建议用来制造 UB 的做法

messages.en: can you give an example for where this is done for a reason other than confusing rust with another language
messages.zh: 你能举个例子吗？说明除了把 Rust 和另一门语言混为一谈之外，还有什么理由会这样做

messages.en: or is this 100% a "legacy code we don't want to touch" issue
messages.zh: 还是说，这 100% 是一个“我们不想碰的遗留代码”问题？

messages.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607455108):
```quote
the answer IMO is to do better analyses -- if the address is passed to a function that, in some sense, "does not care" about the address, and dosnt access things outside the field, then we can still do $whatever
```

I would be happy with this so long as we get confirmation from LLVM that this is feasible and just needs implementation work, or that they tried it and and it didn't make a difference
messages.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607455108)：
```quote
我认为，答案是进行更好的分析——如果这个地址被传给了一个从某种意义上说“并不关心”该地址的函数，而且它不会访问字段之外的内容，那么我们仍然可以做 $whatever
```

只要我们能从 LLVM 那里得到确认，确认这在技术上是可行的、只是需要投入实现工作，或者他们已经尝试过但没有带来任何改善，我就会接受这种方案

messages.en: Consider https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/64188, where IIUC an analysis similar to what you propose here would allow resolving the soundness issue—and yet, after nearly 3 years, it's still open. Does not inspire great confidence
messages.zh: 考虑一下 https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/64188。根据我的理解，如果采用一种类似于你在这里提议的分析，就可以解决这个健全性问题——然而将近 3 年过去了，它仍然处于开放状态。这实在无法让人对其抱有太大信心

messages.en: So... is the vibe basically that no matter what the vibe on subobject provenance actually is, there is no choice and we cannot have subobject provenance?
messages.zh: 所以……基本上的意思是，无论 subobject provenance 实际上是什么样的，我们都别无选择，也不可能拥有 subobject provenance，对吗？

messages.en: yes that should work
messages.zh: 是的，这应该可行

messages.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629907):
```quote
it is rather intended to balance good properties for optimization with an easy mental model
```

In my experience, unsafe code authors find TB intuitive and have no problem with its complexity. Humans are just like that. Remember how lexical borrows were the obvious strategy because scopes are simple and everyone is used to thinking about programs in terms of scopes?
messages.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629907)：
```quote
其本意是要在有利于优化的良好性质与易于理解的心智模型之间取得平衡
```

以我的经验来看，unsafe 代码作者觉得 TB 很直观，也不认为它的复杂性有什么问题。人类就是这样的。还记得吗？词法借用之所以被认为是显而易见的策略，是因为作用域很简单，而且每个人都习惯于从作用域的角度来思考程序。

messages.en: And now it's clear that what people actually want to write code against is even more complicated than dataflow analysis
messages.zh: 而现在很明显，人们真正想要据此编写代码的东西，甚至比数据流分析还要复杂

messages.en:

@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607567862):
````quote
I dont see any thing in the standard permitting those to be used to do ptr arithmetic outside of arrays
````

[6.3.2.3 Pointers, item 7](https://www.iso-9899.info/n3047.html#6.3.2.3)
```quote
When a pointer to an object is converted to a pointer to a character type, the result points to the lowest addressed byte of the object. Successive increments of the result, up to the size of the object, yield pointers to the remaining bytes of the object.
```
Which yes, relies on &x.foo not being a restricted to a subobject (otherwise you could argue that it doesn't even let you access the next array element). While I agree with that q&a that this is unclear rather than clearly unrestricted, certainly the default assumption by programmers has been that it is unrestricted.

uintptr_t would rely on Footnote 73, which is just a footnote - "The mapping functions for converting a pointer to an integer or an integer to a pointer are intended to be consistent with the addressing structure of the execution environment." Otherwise pointer/int casting is at least allowed to be encrypt/decrypt, which would break using it for pointer math (since uintptr_t is only required to work for the same value pointer->int->pointer).

@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607567862)：
````quote
我没看到标准中有任何内容允许使用这些指针在数组之外进行指针算术
````

[6.3.2.3 Pointers, item 7](https://www.iso-9899.info/n3047.html#6.3.2.3)
```quote
当指向某个对象的指针被转换为指向字符类型的指针时，结果指向该对象地址最低的字节。对结果依次递增，直到达到该对象的大小，就会得到指向其余字节的指针。
```
这确实依赖于 `&x.foo` 不被限制为只能指向一个子对象（否则你可以认为它甚至不允许访问数组中的下一个元素）。虽然我同意那个问答所说的：这与其说是明确不受限制，不如说是不明确；但程序员长期以来的默认假设确实是它不受限制。

`uintptr_t` 则依赖于脚注 73，而脚注终究只是脚注——“用于将指针转换为整数，或将整数转换为指针的映射函数，其意图是与执行环境的寻址结构保持一致。”否则，指针／整数转换至少可以被实现为加密／解密，这会破坏将其用于指针算术的做法（因为 `uintptr_t` 只被要求保证同一个值经过指针→整数→指针转换后仍能正常工作）。

messages.en:
I guess that the answer changes in the `fn bar` case by "forking" the original `x: &mut _` reference into multiple references `&mut x[0]` and `&mut x[1]` - in a world without subobject provenance both of these would have write access to the entirety of the array `x` but that "other forked reference" limits what they can actually do without triggering UB. Compared to just holding the original `&mut x` and a derived `&mut x[1]`, we of course do not consider these two references aliasing since the original one is "turned off" while the derived one lives.

I personally cannot really say I like this from a surface language point of view, ... but at least we (hopefully) don't lose optimisations like in the last `fn inner` if we can argue that forking references does effectively produce a restricted form of subobject provenance.
messages.zh:
我猜，在 `fn bar` 这个例子中，答案会因为把原始的 `x: &mut _` “分叉”为多个引用 `&mut x[0]` 和 `&mut x[1]` 而发生变化——在没有子对象 provenance 的世界里，这两个引用都会对整个数组 `x` 拥有写权限，但那个“另一个分叉出来的引用”会限制它们实际上能做什么，否则就会触发 UB。相比之下，如果只是持有原始的 `&mut x` 和一个派生出的 `&mut x[1]`，我们当然不会认为这两个引用存在别名关系，因为在派生引用存活期间，原始引用处于“关闭”状态。

就表层语言而言，我个人确实不能说喜欢这种设计……但至少，如果我们能够论证引用分叉实际上产生了一种受限形式的子对象 provenance，那么我们（希望如此）就不会像最后那个 `fn inner` 示例那样损失优化机会。

It has nothing to do with types, it's just about byte ranges in memory. And I didn't pick the name, I've been using "subobject provenance" because that's the name you've been using and this is not a bikeshed thread. I think this is a compelling argument against using this name - we don't have anything called "objects". I would prefer to gloss it as "references have access to only the bytes of the target type".

As a structural feature I don't find it surprising in the slightest when put up against the other examples that Aapo has used - you can easily end up with references restricted to their region by using adjacent borrows in TB today. @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607833205):
```quote
I don't think this is a hard model to teach
```

And that's essentially CHERI's model: flat memory where capabilities are mostly an address and a window where that address is usable. The question is what's the window of a new pointer?

Today it's the allocation for pointers returned by the global allocator, and that same allocation for derived pointers. The rationale being what Ralf said: offsets between allocation is dynamic, offsets within allocations is (usually) static. Of course if you implement an allocator within an allocation (like a custom allocator), then that rationale doesn't work anymore because offsets between custom allocations are dynamic but still share the same window inherited from the global allocation they are drawn from.

The second question is whether we can change that, to which there's at least 2 options:
1. Explicit: the user may shrink the window when creating a new pointer (by default it inherits the window), which could be in the form of `restrict_provenance`.
2. Implicit: pointers (or maybe just references, TBD) get a window based on their type (possibly depending on attributes on the outer/inner types).

The problem of "implicit windowing" is legacy code (if the attributes are not opt-in). The problem of "explicit windowing" is optimizations (which are not "enabled by default"). Which is why it seems to all boil down to how much legacy would break and how much optimization would we get (to which I have no ideas, but according to the thread and AFAICT: non-negligible legacy would break and no clear optimizations except for enums)
messages.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607833205)：
```quote
我不认为这是一个难以讲清楚的模型
```

这本质上就是 CHERI 的模型：内存是平坦的，而 capability 主要就是一个地址，以及该地址可以使用的一个范围。问题在于，新指针的这个范围应该是什么？

对于全局分配器返回的指针来说，目前它是整个分配；对于派生出的指针来说，则沿用同一个分配。理由正如 Ralf 所说：分配之间的偏移量是动态的，而分配内部的偏移量通常是静态的。当然，如果你在一次分配内部实现了一个分配器（比如自定义分配器），这个理由就不再成立了，因为自定义分配之间的偏移量是动态的，但它们仍然共享从中分配出来的那个全局分配所继承的同一个范围。

第二个问题是，我们能否改变这一点；至少有两种方案：
1. 显式方式：用户在创建新指针时可以缩小这个范围（默认情况下继承原范围），这可以通过 `restrict_provenance` 来实现。
2. 隐式方式：指针（或者也许只有引用，待定）根据其类型获得一个范围（可能还取决于外层类型或内层类型上的属性）。

“隐式设置范围”的问题在于遗留代码（如果这些属性不是选择启用的）。而“显式设置范围”的问题在于优化（因为它们不会“默认启用”）。所以问题似乎最终都归结为：会破坏多少遗留代码，以及能获得多少优化收益（对此我没有什么想法，但根据这个讨论串以及我的理解：会破坏数量不可忽略的遗留代码，而除了枚举之外，没有明确的优化收益）。

````quote
Maybe that's the best way to put it: flat memory is very intuitive to many people, but also clearly doesnt work. The closest approximation we can have is to be "flat within an allocation". Subobject provenance breaks with that.
````

But of course, that can't be the full model, because the *heap allocator itself* is free to rely on the offset between allocations it creates. There is a natural tree structure here—`malloc` gets access to big chunks of memory from e.g. `mmap`, cuts them into smaller pieces, and hands those to its callers—who are themselves free to slice and dice further

@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607832376)：


但当然，这不可能是完整的模型，因为*堆分配器本身*就可以依赖它所创建的各个分配之间的偏移量。这里存在一种自然的树状结构——`malloc` 从例如 `mmap` 获取大块内存，把它们切分成更小的部分，再交给调用者；而调用者自己也可以继续切分这些内存。

messages.en: As I understand it a `restrict_capability` operation is rather important for security on CHERI to ensure code that shouldn't have access to anything outside of the subobject in fact doesn't have such access even in the face of memory unsafety. messages.en: the operation is used to isolate allocations from each other, which is a key part of their memory safety story indeed
messages.zh: 这个操作用于将各个分配彼此隔离，而这确实是 CHERI 内存安全机制的关键组成部分。

messages.en: being able to do it inside an allocation is more of a nice-to-have IMO. as discussed above, the decision about the default place projection behavior does not preclude the option of language extensions down the line that have their own rules.
messages.zh: 我认为，能够在一次分配内部进行这种操作，更多算是一项锦上添花的功能。正如上面讨论的，对默认 place 投影行为的决定，并不排斥未来通过语言扩展加入拥有自身规则的选项。

messages.en: also I dont think CHERI is very relevant here, we certainly won't add *Undefined Behavior* (with all its associated costs for every Rust program ever written) for the benefit of CHERI
messages.zh: 另外，我不认为 CHERI 在这里有多大相关性；我们当然不会为了 CHERI 而给所有曾经写过的 Rust 程序都增加 *Undefined Behavior*（以及随之而来的各种成本）。

@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607907508):
```quote
if we expect people to be able to opt-out of subobject provenance and have `&Header` work when passed through safe code, `restrict_provenance` needs to be `unsafe` or do nothing on `&Header`, since otherwise `read_after_header(restrict_provenance(get_header()))` is UB
```

There could be a world in which you have both of:
* a `restrict_provenance` that becomes a no-op when used on `&T where T: NoSubobjectProvenance`, and
* a different such function that *fails to compile* in that case, because that’s a sign that you’ve done something broken with the ownership of a `T` like putting it in a `Box` that has none of the neighboring memory present

Though, hm, that’s another distinction in use cases, that one could want to make explicit, too. “This type may be used in a way which requires no-subobject-provenance” vs. “this type *is always* used in a way which requires no-subobject-provenance". The latter would mean that trying to construct `Box<Header>` is a logical error potentially leading to unsoundness, and the former would not.

Is any of this worth doing instead of using (newtyped) raw pointers? I don’t know. But I am both skeptical about the usability of "just use raw pointers", and wanting to not live in the world where accessing out of bounds of a reference's referent is OK, which means I wish that Rust did have an explicit opt-out (or opt-in!) per type.
messages.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607907508)：
```quote
如果我们希望用户可以选择不采用子对象来源信息，并且让 `&Header` 在经过安全代码传递后仍然有效，那么 `restrict_provenance` 要么必须是 `unsafe` 的，要么对 `&Header` 不执行任何操作，否则 `read_after_header(restrict_provenance(get_header()))` 就会产生未定义行为
```

也可以存在这样一种设计，同时提供以下两者：
* 一个在用于 `&T where T: NoSubobjectProvenance` 时变成空操作的 `restrict_provenance`；
* 以及另一个在这种情况下无法编译的类似函数，因为这意味着你对某个 `T` 的所有权处理方式有问题，比如把它放进了一个周围没有任何相邻内存的 `Box` 中。

不过，嗯，这又涉及使用场景上的另一种区分，而且这种区分也可能值得明确表达出来：“这个类型可以用在不需要子对象来源信息的场景中”与“这个类型*总是*用在需要不采用子对象来源信息的场景中”。后者意味着尝试构造 `Box<Header>` 是一种逻辑错误，并可能导致不健全；前者则不会。

与使用（通过 newtype 封装的）原始指针相比，这些做法是否值得？我不知道。但我一方面对“直接使用原始指针”的可用性持怀疑态度，另一方面又不想生活在“访问引用所指对象范围之外的内存是可以的”这样的世界里，因此我希望 Rust 确实能按类型提供明确的选择退出（或者选择加入）机制。

but not everyone can, and not everyone who can does. So whether you personally would be willing and/or able to write your code that way isn't the question, the question is whether you think that it is a good idea to *force every Rust programmer ever* to write their code that way.

messages.en: an important subset of Rust users that can't test on MIRI but need no subobject provenance on some types: safe FFI where some C API uses the `Header` pattern and you represent that in Rust with `OwnedHeader` that derefs to `&Header` but not `&mut Header`

messages.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/608087615):
```quote
at least on `&mut` I think it can be safe -- if you take in an `&mut Header` from outside code, you have no way of knowing that there is a tail after that header.
```

Why would there be a difference between `&Header` and `&mut Header`? Either way, you have to encapsulate the type such that outside code can't create a place of type `Header`. And if outside code can create a `&mut Header` without there being a tail, then it can trivially also create `&Header` without tail.
messages.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/608087615)：
```quote
至少对于 `&mut`，我认为它可以是安全的——如果你从外部代码接收一个 `&mut Header`，你没有办法知道这个 header 后面是否还有尾部数据。
```

为什么 `&Header` 和 `&mut Header` 会有区别？无论哪种情况，你都必须对这个类型进行封装，使外部代码无法创建一个类型为 `Header` 的位置。而且，如果外部代码可以在没有尾部数据的情况下创建一个 `&mut Header`，那么它当然也可以创建一个没有尾部数据的 `&Header`。

messages.en: If you can get an `&mut Header` with a tail, you can `replace_with` and move the header wherever. So either it's safe to restrict the provenance, or it's unsafe to hand out the `&mut` at all
messages.zh: 如果你能获得一个带有尾部数据的 `&mut Header`，就可以通过 `replace_with` 将 header 替换掉，并把它移动到任意位置。所以，要么限制来源信息是安全的，要么根本就不安全地提供 `&mut`。

messages.en: Oh, I see. That's true when there's any non-trivial relation between header values and size/contents of the tail. I think there are some (rare) cases where swapping via `&mut` is safe because the safety invariants w.r.t. tail are the same for all values of the type. For example, if there's a trailing array but the length of that array is stored at a fixed offset before/after the `Header` type. (Don't ask me if there's a good reason for not having such data in the header type itself)
messages.zh: 哦，我明白了。当 header 值与尾部数据的大小或内容之间存在任何非平凡关系时，确实如此。我认为有一些（少见的）情况，通过 `&mut` 进行交换是安全的，因为对于该类型的所有值而言，关于尾部数据的安全不变量都相同。比如，存在一个尾随数组，而该数组的长度存储在 `Header` 类型之前或之后的固定偏移处。（别问我为什么不直接把这种数据放进 header 类型本身。）

messages.en: I propose we commit to *not* having subobject provenance for arrays/slices: https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/622.
messages.zh: 我提议，我们明确承诺不为数组/切片采用子对象 provenance：https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/622。

messages.en: fwiw I am rather in favor of keeping Rust strict here and abundantly teaching "don't do pointer arithmetic on (stuff derived from) references". Choosing to allow moving between array/slice elements feels more like "trying not to break code written by ppl used to C" than "useful capability that allows code we couldn't otherwise".
messages.zh: 仅供参考，我比较倾向于让 Rust 在这里保持严格，并且反复强调“不要对（从引用派生出的）东西做指针算术”。选择允许在数组/切片元素之间移动，感觉更像是“尽量不破坏那些习惯了 C 的人写的代码”，而不是“提供一种有用的能力，让原本无法实现的代码得以实现”。

messages.en: I would describe it as "trying not to break code written in the first 5-10 years of Rust where we didnt much talk about aliasing"
messages.zh: 我会把它描述为：“尽量不破坏 Rust 最初 5～10 年间编写的代码——那时候我们还不太讨论别名问题。”

messages.en: to date we still have no docs that clearly say that you cant do ptr arithmetic on (stuff derived from) references, and raw ptr ergonomics are still terrible
messages.zh: 截至目前，我们仍然没有文档明确说明不能对（从引用派生出的）东西做指针算术，而裸指针的使用体验依然糟糕透顶。

messages.en: so I dont think we can blame programmers for writing such code
messages.zh: 所以我不认为我们可以责怪程序员写出这样的代码。

messages.en: maybe it takes 15 more years before we can exploit this UB without causing miscompilations galore, seems ok to me
messages.zh: 也许还要再过 15 年，我们才能利用这个 UB，而不会导致大量错误编译；我觉得这没什么问题。

messages.en: Maybe we can have a kind of "opsem edition" so that old codes get the more permissive semantics with fewer room for optimizations, but the new edition has more UB and requires the code to conform to new aliasing requirements. In old editions, miri emits a warning that it is going to be UB in future editions, and in new editions it just rejects.
messages.zh: 也许我们可以引入一种“opsem edition”，让旧代码采用更宽松的语义、牺牲一些优化空间，而新 edition 则包含更多 UB，并要求代码符合新的别名要求。在旧 edition 中，Miri 发出警告，说明未来 edition 中这将成为 UB；而在新 edition 中则直接拒绝。

messages.en: People who use Miri to check their code are already told not to do this. Our problem is with users who don't, and we can assume they won't notice the edition change if it doesn't raise a warning of some sort
messages.zh: 使用 Miri 检查代码的人已经被告知不要这么做了。我们的问题在于那些不使用 Miri 的用户，而我们可以假设，如果 edition 变更没有引发某种警告，他们不会注意到这次变更。

messages.en: It could be a separate number than the normal edition. Then users could ask themselves that what is the effect of the number that I'm bumping, and do I need to fix anything / check with miri? And they can downgrade their edition if they hit any "miscompilations".
messages.zh: 它可以使用不同于普通 edition 的编号。这样用户就可以问自己：我正在递增的这个编号会带来什么影响？我是否需要修复什么，或者用 Miri 检查一下？如果遇到任何“错误编译”，他们还可以降级 edition。

过去编写了大量代码，而且这些代码很可能不会再更新。永远维护项目是要花钱的，通常没有资金支持的项目负担不起这笔费用。更不用说，并不是每个项目都能在 Miri 中运行。

messages.en: And doing it via editions would mean that the "true" rust opsem would have to support both. For this, perhaps that is fine (although it does beg the question of whether or not it's worth it to introduce something as complex as 'opsem editions' for this case), but generally this seems very difficult and confusing to me. This 'opsem edition' would also be dangerous to update, especially for projects that can't run under miri. And having the more permissive opsem in the older edition means there would be cases where downgrading opsem editions would be desirable, which seems like something we shouldn't want (AFAIK downgrading normal editions is currently only done for wider compiler version support). This also doesn't even get into the complexity macros would introduce here.
messages.zh: 而通过 edition 来实现，就意味着“真正的” Rust 操作语义必须同时支持两种情况。对于这个问题，也许这样还行（不过这确实会让人思考：为这个案例引入如此复杂的“opsem editions”是否值得），但总的来说，这对我而言似乎非常困难且令人困惑。这个“opsem edition”在升级时也会很危险，尤其是对那些无法在 Miri 下运行的项目而言。而让旧 edition 保持更宽松的操作语义，意味着会出现一些应该降级 opsem edition 的情况；这似乎不是我们想要的（据我所知，目前降级普通 edition 只是为了支持更广泛的编译器版本）。此外，这还完全没有涉及宏会在这里引入的复杂性。

I think it would be very bad if we went another 10 years with a spec that has weird footnotes like "cant exploit this UB before 2040" for major things like subobject provenance. and that's not even touching on the point that I find it questionable that  we should just unleash entirely avoidable UB (as in, we can avoid unleashing it) on legacy code.
messages.zh:

messages.en: I wanted to get something landed in the Reference because we need to nail down the related https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/621. saying in the Reference "it's UB to ever do an access outside the memory the reference points-to" feels like a huge disservice to our users, introducing an entire new class of UB out of nowhere now for patterns that we have seen again and again in real-world code.
messages.zh: 我想先把一些内容写入 Reference，因为我们需要明确解决相关的 https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/621。在 Reference 中写上“任何时候，只要访问超出该引用所指向的内存范围，就是 UB”，我觉得这会严重损害用户利益：它会凭空引入一整类全新的 UB，而我们明明已经在现实世界的代码中一次又一次地看到这些模式。

messages.en: okay, but you've already seen that lots of people would like to see a path forward to where that is actually UB. I understand your concerns, but I'm not sure you understand ours. Please engage with the brainstorming on how to make something that satisfies everyone
messages.zh: 好吧，但你已经看到，很多人都希望能有一条前进路径，最终让这确实成为 UB。我理解你的担忧，但我不确定你是否理解我们的担忧。请参与讨论如何制定一个能让所有人都满意的方案。

messages.en: yes, Miri has errorred for such code for a long time, but that was an experiment to figure out how much UB we can get away with in this space. and to me the experiment showed that no we can get away with this.
messages.zh: 是的，Miri 很久以来都会对这类代码报错，但那是一项实验，目的是弄清楚在这个领域我们究竟能容忍多少 UB。而在我看来，实验表明：不，我们不能容忍这种做法。

code is either UB or it isnt. it's hard to make a middle ground for a particular program.

I already made a huge compromise by saying that projections to fields and enum variants enforce subobject provenance, and that it's UB to change the discriminant via references to fields. this is middle ground between what I think we should do and what you and Nadri are advocating for. I feel like I was extremely accommodating for your enum proposal, even though I am of the opinion that we shouldnt do anything like that. and yet that's not enough for you and now you claim I am unwilling to engage?!?
messages.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619977844)： ```quote 好吧，但你已经看到，很多人都希望能有一条前进路径，最终让这确实成为 UB。我理解你的担忧，但我不确定你是否理解我们的担忧。请参与讨论如何制定一个能让所有人都满意的方案。 ``` 对于某个特定程序来说，代码要么是 UB，要么不是 UB；很难在两者之间建立某种折中状态。 我已经做出了很大的妥协：我同意，对字段和枚举变体的投影会强制要求子对象来源信息，而且通过指向字段的引用修改判别值属于 UB。这是在我认为应该采取的做法，与 ​​你和 Nadri 所主张的做法之间取得的折中。我觉得，对于你的枚举提案，即便我个人认为我们不该做任何类似的事情，我也已经极尽包容了。然而这对你来说仍然不够，现在你居然还说我不愿意参与讨论？！

messages.en: for example, one way to make "opsem editions" work would be to have two different operations for subobject projection, both spelled &x[0] but on different editions, and only one does permission trimming
messages.zh: 例如，要让“opsem editions”可行，一种办法是为子对象投影定义两种不同的操作：在不同的 edition 中都写作 &x[0]，但只有其中一种会进行权限裁剪。

messages.zh: （我稍微编辑了一下上一条消息，如果因此让人感到困惑，抱歉。）

someone already noted above that this violates a fundamental tenant of editions --  automatic or near-automatic transitions to a new edition
messages.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619978055)： ```quote 例如，要让“opsem editions”可行，一种办法是为子对象投影定义两种不同的操作：在不同的 edition 中都写作 &x[0]，但只有其中一种会进行权限裁剪。 ``` 上面已经有人指出，这违反了 edition 的一项基本原则——自动或近乎自动地迁移到新的 edition。

messages.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619978317)： ```quote 到目前为止，我不认为你在这里提出过任何方案；你只是在否决其他人的所有方案，然后说“我们就把‘什么都做不了’这点定死吧”，这看起来很不真诚。 ``` 我真的不知道你到底想要什么。我已经提出了一项明显朝着你的方向迈进的方案，见 https://github.com/rust-lang/reference/pull/2338。在我已经付出巨大努力去迁就自己并不认同的观点、同时只坚持一些不愿妥协的小原则时，却得到这样的回应，这让我觉得非常难以继续讨论。

messages.en: I think the evidence of this thread is that it is not near consensus

messages.en: My position is that I am willing to accept these type of FCPs provided that we have a path for how to get the UB behavior in <infinity  years
messages.zh: 我的立场是，只要我们有一条路径，能在 <infinity  years> 内实现 UB 行为，我愿意接受这类 FCP。

messages.en: even if different syntax is needed or what have you
messages.zh: 即使这意味着需要使用不同的语法，或者采取类似的其他做法。

messages.en: It does feel like you're completely unwilling to compromise and then you go and accuse those not willing to adopt your position as being unwilling to compromise.

messages.zh: 从我的立场来看（我不希望有子对象溯源），https://github.com/rust-lang/reference/pull/2338 已经是朝你的立场迈出的一大步了。但它确实还没有*完全*走到那一步，所以还不够？

messages.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619976429):
```quote
having field projections is amazing but doesnt solve any of the issues around autoref.
```

For autoref, I'm proposing a `implicit_operation_near_unsafe_code` lint that warns on autoderef/autoref, match ergonomics, and a couple other implicit operations in a function body that also has an `unsafe` block. Does that not address the issues around autoref? Or are you objecting to it on other grounds?
messages.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619976429)： “有字段投影确实很棒，但并没有解决围绕自动借用的任何问题。” 针对自动借用，我提议增加一个 `implicit_operation_near_unsafe_code` lint：当函数体中同时存在 `unsafe` 块时，对自动解引用/自动借用、匹配人体学以及其他几个隐式操作发出警告。这样还不足以解决自动借用相关的问题吗？还是说你是基于其他理由反对它？

messages.en: @**Thom Chiovoloni** , if your comment is directed at me: do you have an argument for not having subobject provenance in the far future which isn't of the form "lots of legacy code exists"? I would really like to hear a positive argument against subobj provenance
messages.zh: @**Thom Chiovoloni**，如果你的评论是针对我的：你能否提出一个理由，说明为什么在遥远的未来也不应该有子对象溯源，而这个理由不是“遗留代码太多”这种形式？我真的很想听听反对子对象溯源的正面论据。

messages.en: sometimes "too much legacy exists" *is* also a critical reason why you're locked into something. see: most other systems in the world
messages.zh: 有时候，“遗留代码太多”*确实*也是让你不得不受制于某种方案的关键原因。参见：世界上大多数其他系统。

messages.en: I think legacy code is a genuinely good reason. But I also would probably be in favor of having no subobject provenance anyway, since I think it's less error prone.
messages.zh: 我认为遗留代码确实是一个很充分的理由。但即便如此，我可能还是会支持完全不采用子对象溯源，因为我认为那样更不容易出错。

messages.en: Of course I recognize it as a constraint, but I also think that "stability without stagnation" is a good principle and if we can find a way to have our cake and eat it too that would be great
messages.zh: 当然，我承认这是一项约束，但我也认为“在不陷入停滞的前提下保持稳定”是一个很好的原则；如果我们能找到一个两全其美的办法，那就太好了。

messages.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619976429):
```quote
I think it would be very bad if we went another 10 years with a spec that has weird footnotes like "cant exploit this UB before 2040"
```

It wouldn't even be part of the spec, only an implementation choice for the sake of not breaking users too much. And even if it was, I don't see why that's a problem? We'd still have the systems language with the best spec.

 We'd make a blog post about "btw, never do pointer arithmetic on references" to make sure everyone is aware. We'd update the nomicon if it's not already clear. Once we settle on TB/SB, we're already squarely in the realm of "opsem of references has subtle provenance" anyway, and that's also something we'll have to document/teach well so it's not a whole new world of problems either.
messages.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619976429)： “如果我们再用一份带有诸如‘在 2040 年之前不能利用这个 UB’之类奇怪脚注的规范过十年，我认为那会非常糟糕。” 这甚至不会成为规范的一部分，只会是为了不至于过多破坏用户代码而采取的一项实现选择。即便它属于规范，我也不明白这有什么问题。我们仍然会拥有规范最完善的系统语言。我们可以写一篇题为“顺便说一句，永远不要对引用做指针算术”的博客文章，确保所有人都知道这一点。如果 Nomicon 里还没有说清楚，我们也会更新它。一旦我们确定采用 TB/SB，我们本来就已经明确进入了“引用的操作语义具有微妙的溯源规则”这一领域；这同样是我们必须充分记录并讲解好的内容，所以也不会凭空带来一整套全新的问题。

messages.en: put another way, I do not accept "legacy code exists" as a reason to *permanently* block off some design avenue, although the runway to get onto it might be very long. I would like the t=infinity limit of Rust to be a perfect language, so the only thing that will get me off having a design permanently is if there is an argument that it is not good on its own merits
messages.zh: 换句话说，我不接受“存在遗留代码”作为*永久*封锁某条设计路径的理由，尽管走上这条路径的过程可能会非常漫长。我希望 t=infinity 时的 Rust 能成为一门完美的语言，所以，唯一能让我永久放弃某项设计的理由，就是有人能论证它本身并不好。

messages.en: I don't think there's such a thing as a perfect language. It's all subject to taste. That means if changes which break old code are okay, then they will be made continuously, since tastes change. That means that people have to maintain software indefinitely, which means that things without indefinite funding will be broken. So I don't agree with that at all.
messages.zh: 我不认为存在所谓完美的语言。一切都取决于个人偏好。这意味着，只要允许做出会破坏旧代码的改动，那么这种改动就会持续发生，因为偏好会发生变化。也就是说，人们必须无限期地维护软件；而没有无限期资金支持的东西最终都会被破坏。所以我完全不同意这种看法。

messages.en: Anyway, I think UB should have to justify itself as being worth how error-prone it makes the language. I think this is a case that genuinely makes the language more error-prone (as evidenced by how often this is hit), without benefit to compensate for that.
messages.zh: 总之，我认为 UB 应该证明自己值得承担它给语言带来的易错性。我认为这确实是一个让语言更容易出错的案例（从它在实践中被频繁触发这一点就能看出来），却没有相应的收益来弥补这一点。

messages.en: So I would be against it even without the legacy argument.
messages.zh: 所以，即使不考虑遗留代码这个论据，我也会反对它。

messages.en: being error-prone is certainly an argument against it on its own merits. I don't think it's a matter of taste, it's an empirical matter
messages.zh: 容易出错当然本身就是反对它的理由。我不认为这是品味问题，而是一个经验问题。

messages.en: "references ever existing make more code UB" was one of the most common errors with SB in the past
messages.zh: “只要引用曾经存在过，就会让更多代码变成 UB”是过去使用 SB 时最常见的错误之一。

messages.en: I agree with Thom -- even ignoring existing code, I don't think it's obvious that "pervasive subobject provenance for references" would be the best place for Rust to end up in eventually. It seems almost certain that any useful aliasing model will be subtle for many programmers to wrap their heads around. But that doesn't mean further sources of UB are automatically (near-)free. It's still a trade-off how many things unsafe code authors have to be very careful about. At least in today's Rust, this is empirically a very common footgun in the wild. It's not obvious to me if and how a far-future Rust can fully remove these footguns.
messages.zh: 我同意 Thom 的看法——即使不考虑现有代码，我也不认为“对引用普遍采用子对象溯源”显然会是 Rust 最终最理想的归宿。几乎可以确定，任何有用的别名模型对许多程序员来说都会微妙得难以理解。但这并不意味着增加额外的 UB 来源就自动等于（近乎）零成本。对于不安全代码作者必须格外小心的事项究竟有多少，这仍然是一种权衡。至少在今天的 Rust 中，从实际情况来看，这确实是现实世界中非常常见的坑。我不清楚遥远未来的 Rust 是否能完全消除这些坑，以及要如何做到这一点。

messages.en: My argument for it is that it's easier to teach, and therefore less error-prone. I know Ralf will argue something about UB monotonicity here but I don't think it's as simple as that, if there is some weird edge case that people may or may not be allowed to exploit in certain circumstances that seems problematic and error-prone to me
messages.zh: 我的理由是它更容易教授，因此也更不容易出错。我知道 Ralf 会在这里谈论什么 UB 单调性之类的东西，但我不认为事情有那么简单：如果存在某个奇怪的边界情况，导致人们在某些情形下可能被允许、也可能不被允许利用它，那在我看来这就很有问题，也很容易出错。

messages.en: I don't think ease of teaching automatically corresponds to ease of use.
messages.zh: 我不认为易于教授就自动意味着易于使用。

messages.en: references making more code UB than pointers already exists with or without subobj provenance
messages.zh: 引用比指针让更多代码变成 UB，这种情况无论有没有子对象溯源都已经存在了。

messages.en: I also think adding UB to code to make things easier to teach is highly dubious.
messages.zh: 我也认为，为了让东西更容易教授，就给代码增加 UB，是非常值得怀疑的做法。

messages.en: it's not the UB itself making things easier to teach, it's the simpler model
messages.zh: 并不是 UB 本身让东西更容易教授，而是更简单的模型。

messages.en: For education you can still go with a 'tower of weakening' style, where you first teach that you shouldn't do this, even if the reality is that you can.
messages.zh: 在教学上，你仍然可以采用“逐级弱化”的方式：先教导大家不应该这样做，即便实际情况是你可以这样做。

messages.en: Yes, you can teach the simplified model without making things that don't fit into the simplified model UB. In fact, we have already officially adopted that approach with the strict provenance / exposed provenance split.
messages.zh: 是的，你完全可以在不把那些不符合简化模型的行为定义为 UB 的前提下，教授这个简化模型。事实上，我们已经通过 strict provenance / exposed provenance 的区分正式采用了这种做法。

messages.en: this is to me very similar to strict provenance
messages.zh: 在我看来，这和 strict provenance 非常相似。

messages.en: the difference being that we haven't yet attempted to FCP whatever angelic provenance model we need to handle the non-strict provenance stuff
messages.zh: 区别在于，我们还没有尝试对处理 non-strict provenance 所需的任何 angelic provenance 模型进行 FCP。

messages.en: we just took the first step in making that code rare
messages.zh: 我们只是迈出了让这类代码变得少见的第一步。

messages.en: and right now we haven't taken the first step in making non-subobject provenance code rare
messages.zh: 而且目前，我们还没有迈出让 non-subobject provenance 代码变得少见的第一步。

messages.en: I think it's not even clear to me whether those on the other side want to see this code discouraged
messages.zh: 我甚至不确定另一方的人是否希望看到这类代码受到劝阻。

messages.en: How is that related to the "it's easier to teach" argument?
messages.zh: 这和“更容易教授”这个论点有什么关系？

messages.en: I'm a pragmatist. I only care about discouraging this code if it's ultimately decided to be UB. Strict provenance is different, in that there are actual downsides to not following it (miri support, if nothing else).
messages.zh: 我是实用主义者。只有在最终决定把这类代码定义为 UB 的情况下，我才会在意劝阻使用它。strict provenance 则不同，因为不遵循它确实有实际的缺点（至少还有 miri 支持这一点）。

messages.en: I'm confused - miri rejects both kinds of code (subobj provenance and strict provenance violations)
messages.zh: 我有点困惑——miri 会拒绝这两类代码（subobj provenance 和违反 strict provenance 的代码）。

messages.en: I think it's pragmatic to discourage code in advance of making it UB
messages.zh: 我认为，在把某种行为定义为 UB 之前就劝阻使用相关代码，是很务实的做法。

messages.en: Non-strict provenance will always be hard for miri to support. Non-subobject provenance, to my understanding, is completely possible for miri to support just fine (even if it only does now under a specific flag).
messages.zh: Non-strict provenance 对 miri 来说永远都会很难支持。据我理解，miri 完全可以很好地支持 non-subobject provenance（即使目前只有在特定标志下才能做到）。

messages.en: At the moment, I do discourage using non-subobject provenance, partially because it's poorly supported in miri, and partially (more importantly) because it may become UB.
messages.zh: 目前，我确实不建议使用 non-subobject provenance，一部分原因是 miri 对它的支持很差，另一部分（更重要的）原因是它将来可能会变成 UB。

messages.en: But if it became defined behavior and were supported fine in miri, I would have no reason to discourage it.
messages.zh: 但如果它最终成为定义明确的行为，并且 miri 也能很好地支持它，那我就没有理由反对使用它了。

messages.en: I mean, it's fundamentally unsafe so it's needed to be discouraged in that way. And it may be easy to break library safety requirements too with it. So I don't think it should be used wildly.
messages.zh: 我的意思是，它从根本上来说是不安全的，所以需要以这种方式加以劝阻。而且，使用它也可能很容易破坏库的安全性要求。因此，我不认为应该泛滥地使用它。

messages.en: This is going out on a limb, but I suspect that miri could be faster with subobject provenance, because you can use more efficient data structures than TB
messages.zh: 这可能有点冒昧，但我猜使用 subobject provenance 后，miri 可能会更快，因为你可以使用比 TB 更高效的数据结构。

messages.en: For me, that's not nearly a good enough reason to make something UB.
messages.zh: 对我来说，这远远不是把某种行为定义为 UB 的充分理由。

messages.en: of course not, but since you mentioned miri support I thought I'd mention it

messages.en: Put another way: it feels to me that removing subobject provenance makes unsafe Rust and especially FFI related code easier to write, but it risks making performance-sensitive safe Rust harder to write.

messages.en: I'm skeptical that that's fundamental. I also think that if the `is_nice` check is complex enough to be performance sensitive, the compiler will have trouble deduplicating it anyway, and if it's simple then the performance won't matter that much.
messages.zh: 我怀疑这并不是根本性的问题。我还认为，如果 `is_nice` 检查复杂到足以影响性能，那么编译器无论如何都很难消除重复检查；而如果它很简单，那性能影响也不会太大。

messages.en: I also think that even if it is true, performant code being easy to write is less important than correct unsafe code being easy to write. (And I say that as someone who has written a lot of performance critical code)
messages.zh: 我还认为，即使这确实如此，让高性能代码更容易编写，也不如让正确的不安全代码更容易编写重要。（我这么说，是因为我写过很多性能关键型代码。）

messages.en: Also, given that you often need to dip into unsafe to write high performance code, unsafe code being easier to write will make some kinds of high performance code easier to write anyway.
messages.zh: 另外，考虑到编写高性能代码时经常需要涉及不安全代码，让不安全代码更容易编写，本来也会让某些类型的高性能代码更容易编写。

messages.en:
Hot take: Rust already has subobject provenance https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/index.html#allocation

Allocations essentially are a particularly strict form of subobjects. Using allocators on top of other allocators, you can have a build a whole tower of nested sub"objects" (allocations). The rules around how this nesting works are seriously underspecified and full of open questions—but there's (AFAICT) broad agreement that we want to give the compiler broad latitude to optimize around allocations, despite the challenges that poses.
messages.zh:
我的一个大胆看法：Rust 已经有子对象来源了 https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/index.html#allocation

I've kinda been confused about this: the intention is AFAIU that bytes outside a reference are writable if the referenced data contains cells: so if you get a reference to `struct Foo { a: usize, b: Cell<X> }` and want to mutate `a` then can't you just reference the `&foo.b` and then access out of that to `foo.a`. messages.en:
But yeah, my four cents are that lack of subobject provenance (or maybe it should be called "reference access restrictions")

1. does seem to forbid some optimisations that one might consider reasonable (whether they're worth it is another thing),

2. puts pressure on safe Rust to do odd things to regain said optimisations (like create a `&self.foo` and explicitly remove it after a cross-cutting call to prove no mutations, while hoping that the compiler doesn't use a stack slot on it),

3. seems to also be a slippery slope to Cells leaking interior mutability into their surroundings (`&Cell` has to assume bytes outside of it are also interior-mutable, hence `&StructContainingCell` has to kinda assume all of its fields are interior-mutable),

4. seems to be a fairly all-or-nothing thing, in that a hypothetical `fn restrict_provenance` or an attribute to do the same either has to be unsafe, or a function containing reference access expansion has to be unsafe with the precondition of said function or attribute not being used. (The attribute is easier if the library doesn't enable foreign code to create the referenced data.) Effectively, if a `&Header` reference may or may not be restricted (depending on if a `restrict_provenace` was called on it, of if it lives in a restricted struct?) then we have a risky reference validity condition (used by some functions) that is not visible in the type system. (I've generally preferred making newtypes for these cases so that I can see in the type system that I have less restricted access that the pointer referree type suggests.)

But as said above: I'm but a little chick and definitely don't know much about opsem, nor do I know that much about compiler optimisations. I also don't really know or understand if the ~6000? UB cases found with SB Miri is a lot or not, and therefore whether halving that to around 3000? IIRC with TB and no subobject provenance is a big deal or not.
messages.zh:
不过，我的四点看法是，缺少子对象 provenance（或者也许应该称为“引用访问限制”）：

1. 确实似乎会禁止一些人们可能认为合理的优化（至于这些优化是否值得，则是另一回事）；

2. 会迫使安全 Rust 做一些奇怪的事情来重新获得这些优化（比如创建一个 `&self.foo`，然后在一次跨领域调用之后显式地移除它，以证明没有发生任何变更，同时还要祈祷编译器不要为它使用栈槽）；

3. 似乎还会滑向这样一种局面：Cell 将内部可变性泄漏到周围区域（`&Cell` 必须假定其外部的字节也具有内部可变性，因此 `&StructContainingCell` 在某种程度上就必须假定其所有字段都具有内部可变性）；

4. 似乎是一个相当非此即彼的问题：假设有一个 `fn restrict_provenance`，或者一个能实现相同效果的属性，那么它要么必须是不安全的；要么，包含引用访问扩展的函数就必须是不安全的，并以不得使用该函数或属性作为前置条件。（如果库不会允许外部代码创建被引用的数据，那么使用属性会更容易。）实际上，如果一个 `&Header` 引用是否受限取决于是否曾对它调用过 `restrict_provenace`，或者它是否存储在一个受限结构体中，那么我们就有了一个有风险的引用有效性条件（某些函数会使用它），但这个条件在类型系统中不可见。（对于这类情况，我通常更倾向于使用 newtype，这样我就能从类型系统中看出，我拥有的访问权限比指针所指向的类型所暗示的更受限。）

不过，正如上面所说：我只是只小菜鸟，对 opsem 确实不太了解，对编译器优化也所知不多。我也不太清楚、也不理解 SB Miri 找到的大约 6000 个？UB 案例到底算多还是少，因此也不知道在 TB 下、没有子对象 provenance 时，如果我没记错，能把它减少到大约 3000 个？这件事是否意义重大。

messages.en: Funnily enough this kinda suggests that shared references are easier to optimise than exclusive references, since the shared nature of them gives a stronger guarantee of "callee must not mess with my non-Cell memory as I would see it as well". For exclusive references the callee is given exclusive access and the caller temporarily disables theirs, therefore losing the ability to assert that they could see the mutation.
messages.zh: 有趣的是，这似乎说明共享引用比独占引用更容易优化，因为共享引用的性质提供了更强的保证： “被调用者不能修改我所看到的非 `Cell` 内存”。而对于独占引用，被调用者会获得独占访问权，调用者则会暂时禁用自己的访问权，因此失去了断言自己能够看到该修改的能力。

@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/620013558):
```quote
Hot take: Rust already has subobject provenance https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/index.html#allocation

Allocations essentially are a particularly strict form of subobjects. Using allocators on top of other allocators, you can have a build a whole tower of nested sub"objects" (allocations). The rules around how this nesting works are seriously underspecified and full of open questions—but there's (AFAICT) broad agreement that we want to give the compiler broad latitude to optimize around allocations, despite the challenges that poses.
```

allocations are *explicitly* created and destroyed. it's hard for the programmer to miss that. that's very different from the kind of subobject provenance people are advocating in this thread.
messages.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/620013558)：
```quote
大胆的观点：Rust 已经拥有子对象 provenance https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/index.html#allocation

分配本质上是一种尤其严格的子对象。通过在其他分配器之上使用分配器，你可以构建出一整座嵌套子“对象”（分配）的高塔。关于这种嵌套如何运作的规则严重缺乏规范，且充满未决问题——但（据我所知）大家普遍同意，我们希望给予编译器围绕分配进行广泛优化的空间，尽管这会带来种种挑战。
```

分配是*显式*创建和销毁的。程序员很难注意不到这一点。这与本主题中人们所主张的那种子对象 provenance 非常不同。

FWIW I'd be totally fine with having such a magic intrinsic.
I have 0 concerns with having it unsafely. I have some concerns with having it safely.  the example above could still be salvaged by saying that the library simply can never hand out an `&Header`, if it wants to preserve access to the surrounding fields it has to hand out a `HeaderRef` or so that prevents `restrict_provenance` from being called.
messages.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/620031318)：`restrict_provenance` 我认为第 4 点不对，因为安全不变量已经由子对象 provenance 保证了，所以 `restrict_provenance` 可以是安全的。不过，在非子对象 provenance 的世界里，我不知道该如何实现它，除非使用某种魔法 intrinsic。顺带一提，如果真有这样一个魔法 intrinsic，我完全可以接受。我对把它设为不安全没有任何担忧，但对把它设为安全有一些顾虑。上面的例子仍然可以这样补救：如果库想保留对周围字段的访问权限，就不能直接提供 `&Header`，而必须提供一个 `HeaderRef` 之类的类型，阻止调用 `restrict_provenance`。

messages.en: imo if you're passing out a `HeaderRef`, there's no point in trying to make references work at all since it could just be `struct HeaderRef<'a>(NonNull<Header>, PhantomData<&'a ()>);`
messages.zh: 我觉得，如果你要传出一个 `HeaderRef`，那就完全没必要再想办法让引用正常工作了，因为它直接可以是 `struct HeaderRef<'a>(NonNull<Header>, PhantomData<&'a ()>);`。

messages.en: so, I think we should try to make references work and not require the use of a `HeaderRef` wrapper
messages.zh: 所以，我认为我们应该尝试让引用正常工作，而不是要求使用 `HeaderRef` 包装器。

messages.en: HeaderRef would only be requried if you hand out references to other code. Im not sure how common that is. for instance BTreeMap uses a pattern like this but never hands an &Header to other code so it doesnt mind `restrict_provenance` being safe.
messages.zh: 只有在你要把引用交给其他代码时，才需要 `HeaderRef`。我不确定这种情况有多常见。比如 `BTreeMap` 就采用了类似的模式，但它从不会把 `&Header` 交给其他代码，所以并不介意让 `restrict_provenance` 保持安全。

messages.en:
Yeah, if `restrict_provenance` is safe, then I can't use `&Header`, and have to wrap it in `Wrapped<'a>(&'a Header)`. This basically eliminates several (admittedly not all) of the benefit of supporting this, IMO. Now you need both `Wrapped<'a>` and `WrappedMut<'a>`, along with conversions, reborrowing (if you need it), and so on.

It works, but it's pretty painful, and it's the same thing you have to do now with raw pointers (which is why I say it eliminates several of the benefits). In theory custom refs may help here, but I have to imagine it will still be a ton of boilerplate.

What's the motivation for it being safe, anyway? (Sorry if I missed this). It's not like you can even observe that provenance was restricted purely from safe code.
messages.zh: 是的，如果 `restrict_provenance` 是安全的，那我就不能使用 `&Header`，而必须把它包装成 `Wrapped<'a>(&'a Header)`。在我看来，这基本上抵消了支持这一功能所带来的几项好处（当然不是全部）。现在你既需要 `Wrapped<'a>`，也需要 `WrappedMut<'a>`，还要处理它们之间的转换、重新借用（如果需要的话）等等。它确实能用，但相当痛苦；而且这和现在使用裸指针时必须做的事情一样（这也是我说它抵消了几项好处的原因）。理论上，自定义引用或许能帮上忙，但我只能想象那仍然会带来大量样板代码。话说回来，把它设为安全的动机到底是什么？（如果我漏看了相关内容，抱歉。）毕竟，单靠安全代码，你甚至无法观察到 provenance 是否受到了限制。


messages.en: What if we say that pointers with provenance are either a real address, or some magical value that's just an allocation id plus an offset (like pointers already are in const)? @_**Max|960514** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621454287):
```quote

Otherwise after inlining we just have this huge mess of unused stuff on the stack
```

I mean, just being honest, I know how to write systems code if the compiler can't clean up the stack as well. The code is slower, but you can focus on hand-optimizing other parts to make up for that. (This is especially true for heap allocations, where it's better to just try and not perform the allocation if you won't need it. In practice, the compiler rarely is able to fully remove them anyway, especially these days due to the alloc_shim_is_unstable stuff (although the compiler can still remove the allocation in some cases despite that, I'm not claiming otherwise)).

Conversely, I'm not sure I know how to write systems code if I can't compare pointers anymore. (I mean, realistically, I think people will just have to do it anyway). Among many other things, it's hard to enforce safety in many cases with such restrictions.
messages.zh: @_**Max|960514** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621454287)：“我觉得我们能够移除未使用的变量也很重要。否则内联之后，栈上就只剩下一大堆未使用的东西了。” 我的意思是，说实话，如果编译器连栈都清理不好，我还是知道该怎么写系统代码的。代码会更慢，但你可以专注于手动优化其他部分来弥补这一点。（堆分配尤其如此：如果你用不到某个分配，最好一开始就尽量不要执行它。实际上，编译器很少能把它们完全移除，尤其是如今还有 `alloc_shim_is_unstable` 这类东西的影响，不过在某些情况下编译器仍然可以移除分配，我并不是说做不到。）反过来，如果我再也不能比较指针了，我就不确定自己是否还知道该怎么写系统代码。（我的意思是，现实中我觉得人们无论如何都只能这么做。）除此之外，在这种限制下，很多情况下很难保证安全性。

@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621425124):
```quote
What if we say that pointers with provenance are either a real address, or some magical value that's just an allocation id plus an offset (like pointers already are in const)? And then we can further say that if you convert a magical allocation id plus offset to an integer, then that's UB, and all allocations use angelic choice to determine whether it should pick a real address or a magical allocation id plus offset value.
```

Besides angelic choice being a problem: (1) now safe code can cause UB, and (2) you need to prove that every optimization reduces memory consumption. ((2) is not disastrous though)

For the version with NB, besides NB being difficult, again you can't optimize away `{ let _x = 0; x.addr(); }`
messages.zh: @_**Max|960514** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621424287)：“一个大概行不通的建议：在你查看分配的地址之前，分配并不存在，也可能彼此重叠。” 这样一来，`.addr()` 就可能触发 OOM，使其具有副作用，从而成为一道很强的优化屏障。比如，在这个提议下，你不能把这样的代码块优化掉：`{ let _x = 0; x.addr(); }`。@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621425124)：“如果我们规定，带有来源的指针要么是真实地址，要么就是某种神奇的值——它只包含一个分配 ID 加偏移量（就像指针在 const 中本来就已经是这样）？然后我们进一步规定，如果你把这个神奇的分配 ID 加偏移量转换成整数，那就是 UB，并且所有分配都通过天使式选择来决定究竟采用真实地址，还是采用神奇的分配 ID 加偏移量值。” 除了天使式选择本身是个问题之外：(1) 现在安全代码也能导致 UB；(2) 你需要证明每项优化都会减少内存消耗。（不过 (2) 倒也没那么灾难性。）对于带 NB 的版本，除了 NB 很难处理之外，同样也不能把 `{ let _x = 0; x.addr(); }` 优化掉
